6. "Bidwell’s" Summer Cruise Extracts from the log of "Bidwell" - Westerly Storm 33 - being sailed by the Gardner family, normally of "“Blucette": The date of departure soon arrived. We were plarming to cruise the Northern Brittany Coast in our friends’ boat "Bidwell" from Plymouth to Biscay. He would join us after two weeks to bring the boat back; a highly illegal thing to do, according to the RYA!* 3rd August. Forecast was good but very poor visibility, less than 200m. After fueling and storing up we left Queer Anne’s Battery, Plymouth at 1315. Wind virtually nil SW. First problem was finding the gap in the Plymouth Sound (big barrier wall.) We followed the breakwater until we sighted the Lighthouse. Turned onto 180'm. According to Decca we passed Eddystone Light half a mile off, but couldn’t see it. Eyes and ears strained, we pressed on being sure it would clear soon. Then the sun appeared and - disappeared. After three and a half hours it was clear, bright and sunny, only a SW 1 so we motored on. The highlight of the trip was about 1730, when we spotted several gannets feeding in the water, and the next thing we knew, about six dolphins swam alongside for 10 minutes or so, much to the delight of all on board. Settled down for the night, wind up and down, engine on and off several times! Beautiful quiet night, all children crashed out on the saloon floor! At one time we counted 18 sets of ship’s lights but at 0300 after having picked up Ile de Batz light, it disappeared as visibility dropped again. Decca going well, and we soon picked up the Lighthouse again when one and a half miles off. Being an East Coast man, we weren't used to seeing these huge dark shapes rearing out of the sea all around - yes, rocks, hundreds of them. Soon we were lying to anchor fairly close to the Roscoff Ferry terminal ready for sleep. 0530 and 100.4 miles on the log. 4th August. Visited Morlaix briefly, but we got the tide wrong - one hour out. Soa scorn headed back and picked up a mooring off the Chenal de Ile de Batz in blazing sunshine. sth August. Surmy hot day, had to wait for tide to rise sufficiently to tackle the Chenal (Channel) de Ile de Batz. The narrow channel running between the Isle and the mainland being a very tortuous, not well buoyed, track betweer rocks. Bit exciting in one place when depth read 0.00 but no bump - only the bumping of the heart beats as they rapidly increased. Through and out into the sea, wind SW 4ish. Our first taste of the full Atlantic swell about 2-3 metres, a little like being on a roller coaster. Headed for L’Abervrach and negotiated the entrance, again, rock strewn. The biggest problem; the boat was going so fast now we had difficulty slowing down in the very narrow channel (Blucette normally has max speed of 6 knots, we were managing 8 knots). 7th August. Forecast NW 4-5 so it’s off through the Chenal du Four. One lock at the chart is enough to get the heart racing as there are so many little rocks. Pretty unrestful passage as wind dropped and we motored again. We could just see Usharnt off to Starboard, as visibility not too good again. A lot of tide here. Decca’s giving us 9.5 knots S.0.G. and only 5.0 on the log. We shot through the Chenal like a cork in a river bobbing all over the place. Tremendous overfalls could be seen, I’m glad the wind was light! Sailed on to Cap de la Cheval and inta the Bay de Downanez. Decca not very accurate row so more traditional navigation methods had to be used. Arrived Norg at 2100 with 47.3 miles on the log. 8th, 9th, 10th August. The whole of the Bay is really beautiful and we spent a few days, Swimming, visiting local beaches and even being boarded by the local maritime police one evening. The off-putting part was the gunboat standing half a mile off. They proceeded to ask us lots of questions and finally circled the boat in their dinghy taking photos! contd. 2s

7. 1tith August. Raz du Sein today. Departed 0615 from Treboul, light airs, visibility half mile. Decca pretty useless now. We stood well out as we approached the Raz and the tide was pulling us hard towards the rocks. After all the stories one hears about the Raz it was most disappointing, water very confused, but once through, it was a boring 30-mile sail down an uninteresting coastline. Few rocks now and land much flatter. Arrived in Loctudy after having completed 55.3 miles. Weather still glorious, again local trips made for an interesting couple of days. contd. 13th August. Today Iles Glenans. A beautiful archipeligo of about 10 islands seven or eight miles off the coast. Still weather red hot. We found a beautiful anchorage off Ile de Penfret. Beautiful gold sands and beautiful water. You could see the anchor in the bottom at a depth of 11 metres - not quite the same as the Blackwater? Spent a grotty night at anchor as the wind changed from blowing off the land to blowing off the sea. Poor ’Bidwell’ was a bit short on chain and all night the chain snatched and banged. 14th August A quick trip to Cancarneau today, only a few miles away. Beautiful town and lovely Marina next to the Castle. Almost too hot taday, water had ta be thrown on the decks te cool things down. 15th August. Spirmaker up today. With only Hilary and our two girls (9 and 11) we hadn’t flown it yet. 1,000 sq ft seemed a bit daunting but she flew well as we headed further South to Ile de Groix. Wind increased and we eventually pulled the spinnaker dawn as we reached 8.5K with 18 knots of wind over the boat. Exciting, though! Into Port Tudy on Ile de Groix, certainly the most crowded port of all the holiday. Anyhow moules (mussels) and wine scon made up for that. 16th August. Short hep to L’Orient (mouth of the Loire) where we had decided after frantic phone calls to meet the ’new crew’ on Saturday. Total of 328 miles on this trip. A wonderful holiday as the weather had been so hot and sunny, combined with cheap wine and good food. A superbly beautiful coastline enjoyed by all the family. Sc nice it was to come home by Brittany Ferries and not have the worry of getting "Bidwell" back. "Bidwell" did have a good trip going South to beyond Morhiban and back. The final leg from L’Abervrach ta Flymouth, they had 40 knots of wind, but did arrive safely back in Plymouth a fortnight later. Derek and Hilary Gardner *Ed’s note: I’m puzzled as ta why it can possibly be illegal to swop skipper/crews, before a boat completes its round trip, can anyone enlighten me? 8. NAVIGANS PAST 1966 - the politics of office and is ‘one more than three' just one too many ? - the "syndicate" moves into the catering trade; has ‘the mob' arrived at Stansgate ? - Fred and Mark visit the Pirates (but they're not from Penzance) January - The Editor (Jack Reeve) points out that many people have still not paid their 1965 racing fees, mooring fees and/or dinghy park fees. "Pay Up", says Jack - or the Committee will have to ‘name names'. Attendance at the 1965 AGM was 120. Amongst the Committee's proposals was one to employ a paid steward for cleaning and maintenance of club premises and site; also care of the club's rescue launch and Brazil (but not run the galley !). 69 voted 'for', none against and 4 abstained (I often wonder why people ‘abstain’ on such relatively uncomplicated issues ?) A proposal to allow Terry Hallam as Commodore for another year over and above his alloted 3-year stint appears to have been much debated. Some thought a sub-committee should be formed to negotiate the new club-site lease and that the Commodore should not carry out the negotiations. Another suggestion was that Terry be elected a Vice-President and lead a sub-committee to conduct negotiations. Others felt that club rules specifically aimed at preventing anyone continuing in office over and above the 3-year span and, given the onerous task of Commodore, felt the 3-year period was the limit of anyone's efficiency. However, others equally felt it permissable to change rules that were found ‘restrictive’. Up to this point, Terry had chaired the meeting, but "Mr Millett" took the chair and a secret ballot re-elected Terry Hallam as Commodore for an additional year by 60 votes ‘for’ and 20 votes ‘against'. Also elected were Nick Tovey (Vice-Commodore), Stan Allerton (Rear Commodore/Hon.Treas), John Witter (Sailing Sec) - and Jack Bigden as a Vice-President . Part 1 of the Mamgu Trophy prize-winning log by C.S.Molyneau, giving an account of his single-handed cruise across The Channel. A notice reminds us that all members should observe a 10 mph speed limit along the approach road to the club. Finally, an invitation to a ‘get together' (pub binge ?) for the embryo Hornet Fleet, the notice describing the Hornet as "the Aston Martin of dinghies". A new Hornet (less sails) costs £265 (wOod) or £295 (GRP) with sails an extra £43 or so. Apparently 4 new boats have been purchased which, with the 2 existing club Hornets, brings the fleet to 6 before it has even got on the water. February - Jack Reeve is looking for an Assistant Editor. Leonnie Carlisle is congratulated on reaching her majority whilst Olive and Brian Partridge expect to acquire a ‘new crew’ in the coming summer. Congratulations to Peter and Marlene Lawrence and to John and Eleanor Witter, each of whom clearly ‘tied the knot' (presumably a nautical one) during February. A Handicap Fleet meeting promises racing for GP14s, Hornets, Mirrors and Torches whenever possible, all hopefully encouraged by the news that no race fees will be charged for "closed club events". The Hornet crowd also held their own ‘convivial evening’ and reveal another 5 members express interest in buying Hornets. Part II of the prize-winning log by C.S.Molyneau. Finally, Jack Bigden is selling a Graduate for £100. March - Alas, no volunteers came forward to help Jack Reeve with Navigans production. However, the paid steward (Tom Polden) has been recruited and “is certainly giving us value for money". "Notes for Swinging Race Officers" require the R.0. to have (a) absolute patience (b) ability to decipher hand- writing in Hindustani written by a Chinese whilst planing in a Force 9 on the way to the start of a race and (c) a good command of basic english to explain why the 10-minute gun was 5 minutes late, and the 5-minute gun was 10 minutes early ! I'm sure we can all ‘identify’ with the sentiments ! Essential RO equipment includes (i) a whitewash brush (to obliterate all personal blame whatsoever), (ii) a clock (to tell when the bar is open) and (iii) two guns (one for starting, the other (preferably a colt.45) for the RO's personal use). K.N.Littlebury writes an article promoting the Snipe dinghy - a lost cause I fear but the article will, 1 suspect, resurrect the 'third class racing’ controversy. In the meantime, Jack Reeve reports upon the inaugural meeting of the Torch Class Owners Association, which was attended by the Torch designer, Mr Bert Keeble who 7 believe lived in Maldon. Also an unsigned article about the GP14 is also published. Also published is a summary of the basic racing rules in readiness for the coming season. Part III of C.S.Molyneau's prize-winning log. April/May - a major Marconi Company ‘re-organisation’ (oh! dear! more dis-organised chaos so beloved of the 1960s ‘high flyers') has delayed the issue of Navigans, hence the ‘double issue’. Peter Croft is trying to organise a Cruiser Class Whitsun Cruise, whilst the expected ‘resurrection’ reference Hornet v. Snipe has materialised; Peter Jennings quite clearly took exception to the claims made concerning the attributes of the Snipe over the Hornet, and challenges the Snipe sailors to a race. Peter points out the Hornet Fleet is now 10 boats strong. A "Galley Syndicate" (Chris Allerton, John Hutchings and Paula Jones) has been formed to manage (and run ?) the galley. They will open Sats and Suns 11.00-14.00 and 15.00-17.00 (plus extended hours if customers await).

3. The ‘syndicate’ (sounds rather sinister) will serve tea, coffee, sweets, etc, plus hot pies and sandwiches. They will also take over the catering for club parties. In addition, tea,sugar and powdered milk will be available mid-week on a ‘serve yourself’ basis - but don't forget to put your money in the till. An announcement by the Cadet Captain (Simon Darney) that, for the first time, there will be a Cadet Week at the club (instead of a cadet Weekend) in the 2nd week of August. This will fall "in line" (does he mean between ?) the Cadet Weeks at Stone SC and Maylandsea bay SC. On the sailing front, the 'man to beat' appears to be John Tillotson in the Hornet Class, with Julian Bigden not far behind. The 'Club-house Rules' are published and Jack Reeve draws attention to the Rule concerning ‘Transistor Radios’. No guesses as to what that rule said. Part IV of the prize-winning Mamgu Trophy log by C.S.Molyneau. Presumably it is the last because he ends by stating "....only a Customs Officer can fall out of bed at 5.30 in the morning and start drinking neat rum !" But I thought that was what cruising was all about ? June Stone SC apparently had "rescue launch problems" this year and it was literally the MSC to the rescue. Good comments on the Regatta (was it the first Regatta ?). However, only 12 Marconi entries out of 79 in all. Robbie Simms (who else ?) controlled the Race Box with 9 starts at 5 minute intervals. Robbie and family have been doing the Regatta starts ever since. One Mirror apparently missed 'C' mark at Goldhanger and continued all the way around Osea, taking 3's hours instead of the expected 1+ hours. You'd have thought he wondered where the others were, wouldn't you ? The Mona's cup was “a bit of a tragedy" with 3 out of 13 finishing, the rest capsizing or coming to other grief. The Marconi (Singhy) Challenge Cup attracted about 50 entries but not much wind. Best Marconi boat was Nick Tovey (Enterprise) in 3rd place. Seven Shearwater Cats (6 from Stone, none from Marconi) seemed to have a special separate race. The Sailing Sec. publishes the names of members who have either (a) registered their boats but not paid the fee or (b) paid their fee but not registered their boats or (c) neither registered their boats or paid their fee. I bet there were a few red faces around ! Finally, Olive and Brian Partridge took delivery of their new crew and Mark is his name - most appropriate for a dinghy sailing family. Would he become a racing Mark do you think ? July - Warnings of 'Spot Checks' on membership status. Apparently “unauthorised people" have been using the site. So what's so different ? You have been warned ! What happened to the much-praised new steward Tom Polden ? A notice says "thanks" to an even newer steward, Mr Underwood. Confirmation of the Cadet Week “under canvas" which will apparently be run along “navy lines" with "messes" etc. Oh Dear! Will it work I wonder ? Anyway, ‘tis all under the control of the Cadet Officer, Tom Gaskell. Fred Partlett writes Part 1 of his "Visiting the Pirates" adventure. He and son Mark took a Wayfarer up to Frinton and back over a long week-end. I'm not sure what he means by "Visiting the Pirates" but he was not welcomed by the fisherman at Walton Pier who prefered he keep at least }-mile away. Cor, I wonder what they think about our East Coast Piers Race ? August/September - a 'one-page' Navigans due to Holidays and work-load taking up a very large slice of the Editor's time, Apparently, the club was broken in to but not much was taken. A letter (attached to this Navigans ?) was circulated to all members concerning club discipline (or rather the lack of it). Complaints about blatant wrong-doing & disregard (for the rules), including "non-authorised" use of the club by non-members, and possibly a hint of abuse of the definition of ‘visitors’. October - another single-page ‘temporary Navigans' only. Unfortunately Jack Reeve had to resign from the post of Editor due to pressure of work and ill-health and none had responded to his appeal for an Assistant Editor. November - Eleanor Witter is the new Editor. She states " I wouldn't exactly say that I'd been Jumbered with the editorship - I sort of volunteered - with a bit of pushing’. I wonder if the Sailing Sec. had a hand in ‘the bit of pushing' and gentle persuasion ? An announcement of a Cruiser Owners “Jug UP" - apparently ladies are (also) welcome ! Sounds like a bit of an afterthought, that one. A write-up of the laying Up Supper (written, 1 suspect, by Eleanor). Although things started out OK, a ‘hiccup' occurred when more people turned up than suppers provided. The guest of honour was Mr F.N.Sutherland who presented the MSC with the model Arab Dhow which is on display over the stairwell at Stansgate. In his speech he explains why ships are called "she" (unpredictable, often in stays and involved with sheets) which, whilst not original, usually guaranteed to raise a laugh. More laughs from Jack Bigden (MC) and his ‘games’. Eleanor confessed she laughed so much she got hiccups; mind you, she does confess to being fed canned beer from her "2nd ladies Race" prize (small ladle) by her crew, Bernard Tillotson and consequently not being able to remember who won (but does she mean “who won" the games - or the ladies Race ?). The ‘supperless' presumably didn't entirely relish the whole evening - but Eleanor says she thorughly enjoyed it, and no wonder !

10. The Prize List includes prizes for Enterprise, Hornet and GP14s but nowt for Fleetwinds or the Torctr & Mirrors. Only one handicap race was held and that was won by Leonie Carlisle. Susan Tillotson won the Ladies Cup, Norman Palmer won the Helmsman of the Year (with Jane Cottam finishing 5th, having won the last race of the series) and Jack Bigden won the over-40s race. Charles Holding won the Mug's Mug (spelled that way); was this the first award of the Mug's Mug ? A notice to say that a boat shed was to be erected at the club and Jack Bigden would like all the help he can get. December - Our new Editor chides those who do not circulate 'their' Navigans around their family. She also praises the enthusiasm of the Hornet sailors and their writer-of-articles who signs himself/herself as "H.Ornet" The Commodore's report for 1966 is not entirely ‘upbeat’. The failure of the Marina project to ‘go ahead’ has had indirect reprocussions in that the club lease has not yet been renewed - merely extended for one more year. Social events at the club, although successful, have barely broken even. A sad "lack of interest of the Cadets" (in racing ?) is reported whilst the rest of the sailing is described as "patchy" despite the removal of race entry fees. However, he praises the Hornet fleet. The Steward/handyman (Mr Underwood) is praised, particularly for services performed beyond the call of duty e.g. he turned out at 3 a.m. during a gale to check that all was well at the club. An ex-EEV Co. building (presumably wooden) has been obtained to replace the current clubhouse (assuming the lease is renewed) whilst a smaller building will be used for the boat shed. Also, a new 20' rescue launch has been bought. The new Commodore is Jack Bigden (does he remain a Vice-President ?) with Stan Allerton (Vice Commodore) and Nick Tovey (Rear Commodore). John Witter remains as Sailing Sec. and two names familiar to me appear on the Committee ie. Pat Black and Cyril Drakeford. On the sailing side, a Hornet team race against Saltcote SC resulted in a win for Marconi. Fred Partlett and son Mark complete their return journey to Stansgate, take two days rest, and then apparently sailed around to Burnham-on-Crouch. Arising from the lack of ‘Cadet activity’, Tom Gaskell has been appointed as the Cadet Skipper with a view to organising a programme of events to encourage the cadet Section. Previously, I believe the cadet captain was, in fact, a Cadet member. was Tom the first Cadet Skipper ? I suspect so, and surely we can reflect with pride upon what has been built upon his initial efforts. So 1966 ends with a bit of a ‘sailing wimper' - but we've always got the Hornet Fleet to ginger things up; rather like our present-day Catamaran Fleet. By the way, I still can't work out what "Visiting the Pirates" had to do with Fred and Mark's voyage of discovery or am I looking too deeply ? KKK KK KKK Keak KKKkKk

Helm of the Year - 1991 "Beware the femme fatale nautique" tttttttt++ The Helm of the Year final was sailed on Saturaday, 12 October, 1991, and it is congratulations to:- Lucy Boreham who became the first lady to win the "Helm of the Year" trophy in the 27th year of the competition. The trophy was presented to the Sailing Section of the Marconi Athletic and Social Club in 1965 by Sir Richard Costain to celebrate the opening of the new MASC pavilion at Beehive Lane, Chelmsford, on 17 July, 1965. It was inscribed as to be awarded to "The Helmsman of the Year" but, in recent years, we have tended to call it "The Helm of the Year" - a move initiated by Malcolm Stuart (if I remember rightly) in anticipation of just such a result as seen in 1991. This year, six fleets were represented in the HoY final and they sailed 6 races in Toppers, with 5 races to count. The finalists were:- Steve Glynn (Fast Catamaran Fleet) Paul Harrison (Slow Catamaran Fleet) Lucy Boreham (Dart 18 Fleet) John Salmon (Solo Fleet) Jane Williams (Monohull H'cap) Mike Boreham (420 Fleet) Unfértunately, the Mirror Fleet didn't sail enough races to qualify for a representative in the HoY final. The forecast Southerly Force 3 failed to materialise and the competitors had to be content with Force 1 - 2. Race Officer,’ Mike Turner, set an olympic-style course of several short laps ( each 'lap' being a triangle and sausage) for each race but shortened course as he thought appropriate). As a consequence, a steady nerve on the start line was necessary, a good start highly desirable - and the failure to avoid ‘tactical errors' became almost ‘sudden death' to the competitors. At 12-years old, Paul Harrison has done particularly well this year to qualify. I don't know if he is the ‘youngest ever' to take part in the HoY final but he must have a very strong claim to the honour and it was a just reward to Paul for the regularity with which he turns out for the racing and the effort he puts into his sport. I've no doubt we'll see a great deal more of Paul as he gains rqcing experience. Race 1(start 11.15 - one lap) All very shy of the line at the start and Jane Williams was first away, but Steve Glynn reached the windward mark first. However, he lost the lead to Lucy after he went too far down-tide and Lucy went on to win. Race 2 (start 12.08 - one lap) Again everyone was well back from the line at the start but Lucy led from start to finish. Mike Boreham mis-judged the adverse tide conditions and wrapped his main sheet around the wing mark (followed by 720). He then compounded the error, and threw away 4th place, when he fouled John Salmon on the final beat (another 720). Race 3 (start 12.54 - one lap) Jane again had the best start with Lucy close behind. Jane led to the wing-mark but Lucy overtook to reach the 2nd windward mark in the lead and she went on to win. Steve and John had an ‘inside overlap’ clash at the wing mark - and Steve did his 720 but still managed to come 3rd. Race 4 (start 15.40 - two laps) Lucy had the best start and led from start to finish. Mike thought he'd got a good start but again misjudged the tide and hit the outer-distance mark (another 720 and 6th place followed). Jane and Steve swopped 2nd and 3rd spot al] the way around but it was Steve to finished 2nd and Jane 3rd). Race 5 (start 16.18 - two laps) John had a good start but, much to his chagrin, the R.O. signalled a general recall since everybody was over the line. Mike was pleased; he'd been heading the wrong way against the flow of traffic when the gun sounded. The second start again saw John over the line, but Mike surprised himself by finding himself in the lead. However, it was Jane who reached the windward mark first, followed by Steve, Mike and Lucy ‘trailing’ in 4th place - but all were close together; but them Lucy and Mike had moved into lst and 2nd places by the time they reached the wing mark. On the way round, Steve hit: a mark and John fouled Steve ("15-a11"). Lucy and Mike held their places to the finish with Jane 3rd. Race 6 (start 1700 - one lap) Lucy had a good start and very quickly established a clear lead. Mike also had a good start and trapped John and Jane on starboard tack when really all they wanted to do was to tack on to port. Alas, he ‘let them off the hook' too soon and John secured a good 2nd place in this race. Lucy, having won all 5 of the previous races, had quite clearlywon the HoY trophy but both Steve and Jane knew that they were tied for 2nd place overall - and each needed to finish in front of the other. Steve came 4th to Jane's 6th place, and so secured 2nd place overall. Steve Glynn could probably claim the prize for being the heaviest competitor (an admitted 13% stone); nevertheless that didn't stop him from frequently being in, or close to, the lead and his 2nd place overall was particularly noteworthy. Steve has had very little experience of sailing monohulls.

COMMODORES RAMBLINGS Over the last three years the reputation of the club has soared. We are providing, good sailing, enjoyable activities on and off the water and organising open events to a very high standard. The support of all club members has contributed to this, but I think you will all agree that the lions share of the credit must go _ to our Commodore during this period. Neil Pembleton has provided a very positive lead, pulling together the varied interests and aspirations of the club’s membership. This has meant a lot of hard work on his part, thinking about, organising, attending meeting , and being in attendance at events to provide a lead to the club. But Neil wouldn't have been able to carry this out without the support of his family. On behalf of the club I wish to thank Neil's family particularly Barbara for their patience and tolerance. Thank you Neil too! At the AGMs of the various fleets, site security was a common issue. Dinghy's, cats, and cruisers have all been subjected to theft or vandalism. It is in all our interests to ensure we help each other by being more aware of this problem and taking’ steps to reduce the risks. The gate must always be shut. Open meetings are the only exception to this. Please make sure you always close the gate. Don't leave valuable items on your boat which will attract attention. Challenge anyone you don’t recognise, particu- larly if they are wandering around any of the boats. The footpath is along the road not through any of the boat parks. Report any damage or theft to the police, who will be making regular patrols to the club. Note Steve Hill's comments on keys in this issue of Navigans. We need your help for the Working party on the 27 =December. Please try to come. We will be clearing the ditch, so you will need old clothes, gloves and strong footwear. Tools would be useful too. Team leaders on site will show you what needs to be done. The work will be the first stage in preparing to lay drain- age pipes in the ditch . In carrying out the work we intend. to retain as much of the existing hedge as possible. On the 4 January 1992 the club will have a number of boats taking part in the Maldon Rowing race. I will be taking part myself, which should provide some merriment so please come and support. On behalf of all the officers of the club I should like to wish you a MERRY CHRISTMAS, AND AN ENJOYABLE SAILING SEASON IN 1992 Mike Duckmanton

A view from the Rear of Catamarans and Crews... Well, what else could it be called? You will undoubtedly have read elsewhere through the pen of Mike Boreham (welcome to the Cat Fleet Hike & Maggie) the analysis of the 1991 season. What a fantastic growth in the Cat Fleet, and, you may be interested to know, as auch a result of people racing more frequently as new entrants. However, every set of figures tells a story, and the other story of 1991 has to be the sad reduction in the Handicap Fleet. The overall effect has been a reduction in the total number of people participating in Club racing from 200 to 190. I am very conscious of the fact that racing is not everyone’s cup of tea and that several boats “cruise”, but I wonder how good a return soe people are getting when their boat doesn’t appear to aove from March to November. Any comments or ideas gratefully received... As most people only know me as Spot’s appendage!??7) and the twerp that suffers from verbal diarrhoea in Navigans, I thought I’d just give you an idea of my sailing background before you get Duckmanton’s (his hearing aid batteries are on the blink anyway!). I learnt to sail with ay school in Penzance in the boat I hate the most, the Enterprise (sorry Lan, but you try sailing one on the open sea!). This was at the tender age of 1! in 1966...... After a couple of years in which I crewed in everything - Redwing, Hornet (sliding seat version), 1928 International 14 (they're a bit different now), Uffa Fox Jollyboat and Ospreys - a mate of mine built one of the first Fireballs in the Club (Sail No 4437!) and we spent a couple of years iearning how to sail that. In the interia I’d sold ay electric train set and bought a Cadet for £25 -built in 1947, sail no. 197 and should have kept the train set!!! As a gentle aside I had ay first intro to cat Sailing and Reg White’s companies via a Mk I Iroquois that we sailed when there was too much wind to dinghy race. Seventeen knots in that was impressive surfing across the Runnel Stone on the way back from the Scillies! In 1973 ay parents noved to Exeter just as I was off to university, and after helping run the Enterprise Nationals (213 boats) as Gate Launch Driver. I found a new club at Topsham, on the Exe, where they sailed Hornets and (wait for it) Solos, and you could only sail four days a fortnight (tidal). I crewed again for a bloke who still had a sliding seat and had no spinny chute (those were the days). Mind you if you had the bottle to wind your legs under the seat in a blow you certainly had an advantage over the trapezers! Having been spoiled by sea and estuary sailing I didn’t fancy puddle jumping in Larks when I went to University and so only sailed in vacations (including the Fireball Nationals in 1974) whilst rowing in the terms. In 1975 Father moved job back to Piymouth (the things they did to avoid ae !) and I became a nenber of the Royal Plymouth Corinthian. The first couple of seasons were in what is my favourite mono - the 505. Three Sail reaches (20 sq. m. kite) were ‘ansua, and have only really been matched by the 19. Then came a season at the back end of an Albacore on loan, better than an Enterprise, but really the two aan version of the Finn followed by ay second foray into boat purchase, a Laser (No. 7357). That was extremely good fun downwind in a blow (splash) but flaming hard work uphill. At the same time I was co-opted as Sailing Sec - with no other people to help out! J was involved with organising Plymouth Regatta Week, Scorpion (I think) Nationals, and (of all things) the Silhouette Rally! By this tine I had developed the urge to be one of the property owning class so I outed the Laser and bought a flat. That meant a hunt for a new berth which I found on an Albin Gallad for round-the-cans (roles - start tactician, main trimmer, spinnaker trimmer) and some passage races (role - up-chucker in chief). Unfortunately the owner died(!) and I found another home on a Sonata, and, if you've not heard it already, I’m quite prepared to tell the story of The Broach. During this latter berth I'd managed to get myself entangled with a female to whom I got married, stopped sailing and took up horse riding (dressage for the cognoscenti)....... Which brings me up to date. The wife went with the horses, the new boat was going to be a Dart 18 as 7 thought 1 was getting on a bit for slogging a Laser round, but thanks to our new Commodore, that was stopped in its tracks-just like a Dart would be if I was sailing it! On a personal note, I’m a Physics graduate from Magdaien, Oxford and have worked for British Rail and Lex Service in General Management positions before becoming an Executive Search Consultant 5 years ago. Any questions? The ¥inter Series goes from strength to strength, with the last two races sailed attracting 10 and 12 starters respectively and the Final Fling being abandoned due to fog. I] should like to welcome new members of the Sailing Subs Jane Williams as Handicap Fleet Captain, Chris Patmore as Cat Fleet Captain, Colin Kidner as second Cat Fleet rep (as per new constitution), and, last but definitely by no means least, Peter Flook as Safety Co-ordinator. I hope that, together with the old guard, we shall be able to continue the work started by Mike O last year. First items to be dealt with include drawing up the various duty rosters...... watch this space! Larry Botheras

CLUB NOTICE BOARD - BACSPA NEWSLETTER River Blackwater - the 8 knot speed limit proposal for the Blackwater has been raised in various guises but Maldon Council require some form of practical capability before any change can be implemented. A parking ban for beaches is also required. The old gravel pit at the back of Maldon designated as a watersports recreational area. Some 25% of the area will set aside for nature conservation. River water tested at West Mersea has been found to be well below the level required by EEC regulations. A plan of the proposed Salcote Marina does not show what dredging/channel facilities are required into the River. In spite of several attempts by Blackwater SC to obtain further information, they have received no replies about navigation, dredging activities or spoil dumping. River Colne - the coastal protection scheme barrage at Wivenhoe will require about 16 boats being moved so that work can procede. Generally, good relations have been held with the developers who have arranged a reasonable deal for Wivenhoe SC Clubhouse. Considerable problems occur with dangerous water skiers and they seem likely to deteriorate further with a statement from the police saying that they are not going to prosecute further as warning notices are inadequate at Stone Point opposite Brightlingsea. It was noted that the Harbour Authorities do not have budgets for provision of bouys, etc. for the various water activities. RYA - Bob Foster has given up Chairmanship of the RYA Eastern Region but has agreed to carry on as RYA representative for BACSPA for one more year. His appointed successor is George Baker. The Sports Council has put aside £10,000.00p for the Topper Fleet if this ammount can be matched by the Clubs. An appeal is to be launched for this. It was noted that a new two person dinghy is required particularly for small/young people for training purposes. Robin Duchesne, RYA Chairman will be present at the annual Semina at Belstead House, Ipswich, on Saturday 23rd November. Conservation - a document produced by the RSPB is considerate and sensible. They particularly make reference to the importance of the Blackwater and Colne estuaries as "staging posts" for migrating birds. Specific "quiet" areas set aside during migration, should not be encroached upon further. Their findings suggest that yachtsmen and birds can get along together but jet-skis and birds dont. They would welcome designated areas to protect the interests of both sportsmen and wildlife in general. The jet-ski section of Stone Watersports Club are requesting an area for races, etc. and would like an officially designated area for their activities. BACSPA Delegates agreed in principal to an area East of Stone as previously suggested in the BACSPA 1990 proposal of designated areas. This area would, it was hoped also be acceptable to the RSPB.

All MSC members must be members of the Marconi Athletic and Social Club (MASC) and must have a current MASC membership card and number in order to open or renew their MSC membership. NEW Member applications lacking a valid MASC number must be accompanied by the completed MASC application form. All other applications without a valid MASC number will be returned. All Members must pay the MASC fee directly to the MASC. Every candidate for membership must be proposed and seconded for election by a Full or Famil Member of the Club, both of whom must be personally acquainted with the candidate. ( Rule 11) 2. CLASSES OF MEMBERSHIP (Rule 6) Full Being a person who, at the date of election, or renewal, is over the age of eighteen Family Being a married couple, or one or two parents, and all their children who are under eighteen years of age Junior Being a person who, at the date of election, or renewal, is under the age of eighteen 3. Postage fees must be paid where no GEC internal mail facility from Chelmsford is available. 4. Fees include VAT at the applicable rate. 5. All boats incur a Hard Fee. The First boat of a Member is always deemed to be the boat incurring the highest Hard Fee. Subsequent boats under 10 ft (e.g. tenders) are free. 6. Winter storage fees are payable, in advance, at these rates on boats, trailers and cradles to be kept at Stansgate during the period 31st November to 1st March, following the renewal date. Cruiser Owners must also ensure in advance that space is available for their boats. 7. Renewals and applications should be returned to:- The Membership Secretary, Mr. R. Beckett, [redacted] Benfleet, Essex. [redacted]. Telephone [redacted] The MASC fee, as advised will be invoiced to you separately and is payable directly to the MASC. 8. NEW Members joining the MSC after Ist July shall be entitled to a discount of one half the Subscription fee only. NEW Members joining after 1st November shall pay no fees, other than winter storage, until 1st January the following year. 9. Any Members in any category of membership being over the State Retirement Age, shall pay one half the full fees for Full or Family Membership as appropriate (Rule 7). 10. Membership renewal fees are due on Ist January and are payable by 31st. January. Late renewals incur the penalty fee (Rule 8e). Persons wishing to resign their membership at renewal time must indicate so on this form and return it,together with all MSC keys with which they were issued, to the Membership Secretary. £4 will be refunded for each undamaged key returned. (See also Rule 15).

If unable ta perform the duty at all for reasons of health or age, then please write ta Steve and let him know: Steve Hill [redacted] 44 [redacted] Scuthminster Essex, [redacted] 26 Jan 92 Sun - JE Walker [redacted] 1 Mar 92 Sun - T M Willett [redacted] 8 Mar 92 Sun - RL Smith 2 Feb 92 Sun - RD Smith [redacted] 15 Mar 92 Sun - R D Anderson 9 Feb 92 Sun - J R Stuthers [redacted] 22 Mar 92 Sun - MM Stuart [redacted] 16 Feb 92 Sun - LA ha [redacted] 29 Mar 92 Sun - PC Shephard 23 Feb 92 Sun - GEV 01-[redacted] A tribute to our friend, Navid Greenhalah Many members will be saddened by the news that David Greenhalgh died on Christmas Eve, aged 70. David and his wife, Marie, were familiar figures at the club, particularly during the camping fortnight, and consequently their absence, during the last camping fortnight, from their usual spot just inside the site gate first alerted us to David's illness during 1991. The subsequent "Get Well" card and best wishes sent to David and Marie by 'the regulars' was, I know, very much appreciated. David joined the staff of the Marconi College in 1950, and he and Marie joined the Sailing Section of the MASC in 1963 . They initially "pottered" around the Blackwater in an Enterprise, E8201, and I believe their son, Peter, still has the boat in Shrewsbury. David claimed he knew little about tides in those days and so they always carried an anchor to await 'the turn of the tide’ when they inevitably got ‘caught out'. However, having observed how much they enjoyed "“pottering" in the club boat “Idlevice" and their own Topper in recent years, I suspect their being ‘caught out' was rather more deliberate. David and Marie were often to be seen setting out for Heybridge or Maldon "to buy an ice cream" and I often wonder whether, at literally the end of the day, they achieved the greater sailing satisfaction compared to my own habit of racing around the restricted area of the club'$> racing marks. David wrote to me last November to express his pleasure at reading the 'Navigans Past' series of articles. He recalled Frank Savill as an apprentice - and Eleanor Eldridge (later, of course, Eleanor Witter) as a graduate apprentice and also Nick Tovey as an early fellow Enterprise owner. Before joining the club, David and Marie sometimes visited the club as guests of Bert Brewster, and David remembered the very successful social evenings onboard Mamgu and also the ceremony at the Heybridge ‘Hut on the Wall' club-HQ when the ashes of Fred Garrett were spread on the waters of the Blackwater. In his letter, David not only recalled the names of many old friends and colleagues from ‘the early days' but clearly reflected the great pleasure he and Marie had received from sailing and from their long membership of the club. To those of us who knewDavid only in more recent years, that pleasure was obviously as stong as ever and much to be admired. Characteristically, David had asked me not to reply or acknowledge his letter and, to my shame, I allowed time to slip by, intending to contact David in the new year to gather more ‘background information’ of what he recalled of the club's past. Alas, that is now not possible, but I value his recollections and his letter will be part of the club's recorded history. I'm sure all members will join with me in expressing their sympathy and condolences to Marie, to son Andrew and granddaughter Katie who are also members of the sailing club., and to other members of David's family. Mike Boreham

7. NAVIGANS PAST - 1967 "It's no fun anymore". Maggie's anguished voice arose from the kitchen - and she was obviously not happy. “What's no fun ?" I asked, rapidly running over a number of possible "It's" and coming to some alarming conclusions. "Your 1967 Navigans Past" says Maggie, "It's too long and ton detailed. Why don't you scrap it and start again". Well, you can imagine the effect that had on me. What would Leonardo have said if someone had told him to “put a really bright ‘toothpaste’ smile on the face of your lady friend," in place of the Mona Lisa's enigmatic smirk ? However, I'm not Leonardo, so I tore up the 27 pages of closely typed observations of the 1967 Navigans issues - and started again. January - The Sailing Sec (John Witter) confirms that the 1966 Regatta was the first, but that we need more club entries for the 1967 effort. Of course, many members regard Regatta as a good excuse to do somethina else, and more than one cruiserman high-tails it for Tollesbury over the week-end. On the other hand, many other members get ‘pitched in' to Regatta and have a fine old time. You pays your money - and has your choice. The Editor (Eleanor Witter) reminds everyone that subs are due on lst January and not at the start of the sailing season in March/April. On the social side, Jack Bigden and Joan Gaskell apparently demonstrated the Tango - or maybe it was the Foxtrot - but whatever it was, I suspect our modern day ‘younger set' now rate it alongside the Valeta. Ah, the good old days when the lady of your choice would, one hoped, save the last dance for you. The Hornet Mob also tried to look cherubic as the Hornet Choir, but clearly failed, for their rendering of “Pennies from Heaven" was rated as “hardly a polished performance". February - A write-up of a working party sounds pretty familiar. You know what I mean, assorted people leaning on spades lookingabit lost whilst those with a conscience attack bits of grass at the road edges and hope that coffee time is not too far off. Come about 3 p.m. people start to slope off, hoping no one will notice, whilst the tractor driver, and those who seem to know what's going on, look set to last it out to 10.p.m. March - Apparently several people claim they haven't received a subscription renewal form, but Eleanor rather scornfully points out it's at the end of the January Navigans. She tersely states " If Navigans is so boring that you didn't read that far, please let me know". I can't help feeling it would be a brave man to say so; personally, I'd plead I'd lost it which, as well as possibly true, would certainly be safer. I certainly wouldn't say I hadn't read it. A note says "Handicap racing is very light-hearted.....Don't be afraid that you may look a B/F as most of the others are in the same boat". Well, if they're all in the same boat, no wonder it's fun - all nice and cosy like. Mind you, they'll] look very much like B/Fs when the boat sinks. April - Eleanor confesses to "...feeling awful". Maybe she had a twinge of remorse for her "If Navigans is boring...." bit - or maybe someone was fool enough to say "Yes, it is". But Navigans is not boring, at least not to everybody and I thought the 1967 Navigans were particularly interesting in many ways. Elsewhere in the issue, a party night is described as successful with the THREE Gs much in evidence. No, they're not a 1960s pop group but stand for "GRUB", “GUZZLE" and "GABBLE". May - Mick Turner and Paul Catanese are given some advice. "If someone calls starboard on you, it is much more advisable to go smartly about....than to tip your boat over and go for a swim". Is this the same Mike Turner who, in our modern times, performs a great double act with Mike Battle as the TWO MIKES during the Cadet Camping Week. I remember once calling "starboard" on a port tacker as we sailed close in-shore and very shallow. The other helm promptly jumped out and claimed he was anchored. I tacked and became firmly June - Eleanor the Ed. and John the Sail capsized in the Pilot Cup. Eleanor writes "Estimated water temperature - low. Have read A Doctor's article (on hypothermia) and know I have only a few minutes to live". Well, I know how she feels; I ofter wonder what I'm doing out there ‘enjoying myself’ when I could be doing something more civilized like wreaking havoc amongst the worms by digging the garden. By the way, Regatta attracted 106 boats, of which 21 were Marconi which was, I believe, an improvement on 1966. July - Mick (or is it Mike) Turner and Rosemary announce their engagement - many belated congratulations. Fred Partlett, with daughter Linda and Allan Polley, went ‘sail about’ up to Clacton (or rather ‘down' to Clacton as the old bargemen would have it) in their GP14. Fred was clearly a rather adventurous member, having previously been up (sorry ‘down') to Frinton and round to Burnham-on-Crouch in his open dinghy. Simon Darney was selected to represent the Marconi Hornet Fleet at the World Championships in Holland. September - Eleanor says she is setting a precedent by missing out the August issue. She also advises the club lease has been extended for two more years, so we're safe until end-1969. Also, the Laying-Up Supper is to be held, for the first time, outside of Marconi establishments. It is to be at the Heybridge Country Club. The cost will be 32/6 per ticket (limited to 230 tickets). In the Hornet Worlds, Simon finishes 9th out of 45 (best result 4th), but his crew (Jane Cottam) unfortunately Jost a toe nail and he had to have a substitute crew. Was 'the substitute’ the Fisher-man of Yachts and Yachting fame ?

8. Former Commodore, Eric Payne, is obviously a man after my own heart, for he wonders how many members have kept their copies of Navigans since it was first issued ? Like me, he feels they are worth keeping for they are a record of the club's activities. behind the pen -name Hé.also asks if anyone knows who is the person of "Barnacle" and he praises Barnacle forhis brilliant series of articles. Well, I'd certainly like to know the real name of Barnacle (but only in strictest confidence). At least Eric has answered one question for me; I had thought Eric was Barnacle but this clearly is not so. ew Beavine = Ed, October - The introduction of 'the Breath Test’ results in a coach being hired for the Laying-Up Supper at a charge of 6/- return. The Over-40s race is now called ‘The Jackpot’ and "....was sailed in two parts following the inability of more than half the entrants to sail unassisted to Saltcote. Perhaps Saltcote's beer revived them - more finished the return race". November - Linda Partlett won the Ladies race whilst, alas, echoes of former years as we were beaten by the Ariel (ie. BBC) S.C in a team race at Teddington. After the Laying-Up Supper, Jack Bigden (Commodore) was apparently stopped by the police on his way home - but he was not ‘breathalized’. Apparently the boot of his car was partly open. However, I wonder why his boot was partly open ? Did he start the journey with half-a-dozen ‘worse for wear’ companions from the Laying-Up Supper, and they fell out of the boot along the way ? The mystery definitely deepens ! December - In the Commodore's Report, Jack Bigden judges 1967 to be a successful year. Having lost our radio operating licence due to non-complient equipment, the MASC granted 50% towards the cost of new radios whilst the remaining 50% was donated by members, with a particularly generous donation from the club President, Dr Eastwood. The Laying-Up Supper at the Heybridge he judged as the best ever. Unfortunately, three burglaries during the year resulted in substantial loss of cash, etc. and Jack raises the the point about site security, particularly as it is known that "....not all the people seen at Stansgate are members of MSC". During the year, the MSC took steps to begin repairingthe road to the club and the AGM approved the levy of an additional 10/- subscription for 1968 to help pay to finish the job. It was also suggested that those who used the club most might wish to volunteer an additional donation or two. Discussions with Mr Sparrow (the landlord) for a lease extension continue. The Marina Project "....has not been shelved but it may be modified to be developed in stages". It seems the MSC is involved in the first stage, whereby the club might then secure a very long lease. The club already have various planning permissions granted in anticipation of a longer stay at the site and this demands serious thoughts about financing. With this in mind, the MASC have now undertaken to pay the clubs' fixed expenditure such as rent, rates, sewerage, insurance etc, thus allowing the MSC itself to start to build some ‘surplus funds' for possible future developments. The Sailing Sec reports that during 1967 we had 114 dinghies and 44 cruisers registered, of which 4 cruisers and 50 dinghies took part in racing. Since the inception of Helmsman of the Year Trophy, it had been run as a two day series of 4-5 races. However, the bad weather played havoc with the 1967 series and there is thought to spread the series throughout the year in future. The AGM elected Jack Bigden (Commodore), Stan Allerton (Vice Commodore), Nick Tovey (Rear Commodore) - and Mick Turner as Social Sec. Names familiar to me on the Main Committee are Pat Black, Dennis Byatt and, of course, John Witter. Socially, the MSC reputation as a good place for ‘boy meets girl' continues unabated as Julian (Bidgen ?) and Jill announce their engagement. Lastly (and the mind boggles) it is reported that a bullock sat (yes, sat !) on John Witter's car as he arove about the ‘smaller roads’ between Marconi sites. Actually, a similar thing happened to a friend of mine many years ago as he met a herd of cows on the way to work. He decided to ‘nudge’ one along a bit and the cow similarly ‘sat’ on the bonnet - but added a vital additional letter to the word ‘sat’ ! wee Mike Boreham eek KEKE PS. to Navigans Past 1967 I happened to mention to Pat Black that in the 1967 Navigans he got ‘an honourable mention’ about his alleged difficulties in getting back into his OK dinghy after a capsize. Instead of an embarrassed denial, Pat's face broke into a very broad grin as he recalled the strain he put on the club's rescue resources in those days. He built the OK himself, including mast, but it was so buoyant, he never did manage to clamber back in - he claims it had nothing to do with the bar-opening times. The November '67 Navigans has a ‘for sale' notice for "MUGGS Fleetwind No. 150 - £65 - can still show new boats the way home". It's rather sad, isn't it, when the boat which has featured so prominently in the club's early history and lends its name to our present-day MUG'S MUG (even if spelt differently) should be ‘for sale' at £65 - and presumably was actually knocked down for a little less. What happened to MUGGS in the end ?

MSC-DOC-1992-02-constitution-and-rules.p: CONSTITUTION AND RULES OF THE MARCONI SAILING CLUB. SECTION 1 - Name and Objects. The name of the club shall be "Marconi Sailing Club" (hereinafter referred to in these rules as “the club"). 2. The object for which the club is formed is to promote and facilitate the sport of yachting and also to provide social and other facilities for members as may be determined from time to time. SECTION 2 - Officers. (a) The Officers of the club shall be Full or Family members of the club and shall consist of a Club President, a number of Vice Presidents, a Commodore, a Vice-Commodore, a Rear-Commodore, an Honorary Secretary and an Honorary Treasurer. Officers shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting in each year and shall hold office for one year, retiring at the termination of the Annual General Meeting in each year. All Officers shall be eligible for re-election except that the Commodore, Vice Commodore, and Rear-Commodore shall not serve more than three consecutive years in any one post. (b) The Commodore, Vice Commodore, Rear Commodore, Honorary Treasurer and Honorary Secretary shall be deemed to be the Executive Committee. The Honorary Secretary shall:- (a) With the Registrar keep a register of club members names, addresses, boats and fees paid; (b) Conduct the correspondence of the club; (c) Keep custody of club documents; (d) Keep full minutes of all meetings of the club, the committee (as defined in Section 4) and, with the sub-committee secretaries, all sub-committees which shall be confirmed and signed by the appropriate chairman upon the agreement of the club, the committee or sub-committee at the following meeting of the club, committee or sub-committee; (e) Administer such insurance policy or policies as may be needed fully to protect the interests of the club, its officers, its members and its property; (f) Maintain contact with the club’s legal adviser to ensure that the club’s affairs are managed in accordance with the current Law. The Honorary Treasurer shall: (a) Cause such books of accounts to be kept as are necessary to give a true and fair view of the state of the finances of the club. (b) Cause all returns as may be required by law in relation to such accounts to be rendered at the due time. (c) Prepare an Annual Balance Sheet as at 31st December in each year and cause such Balance Sheet (and accounts as necessary) to be audited at least once annually and shall thereafter cause the same to be exhibited in the club premises at least fourteen days before the Annual General Meeting. SECTION 3 - Membership. 6. There shall be the following categories of membership with power to vote at all meetings of the club as indicated hereunder. Each Full members and one member of a Family unit must be a paid up member of the Marconi Athletic and Social Club. The rights and privileges of each category of members are as defined in the Latest edition of the bye-laws of the club. A FULL MEMBER - being @ person who, at the date of election, is over the age of eighteen shall have one vote. Issued 17/11/91 Page

CONSTITUTION AND RULES OF THE MARCONI SAILING CLUB. A FAMILY MEMBER - which expression shall include:- A)Married couple B)One or two parents (as may be) and all children under eighteen years of age. The family unit shall have one vote, exercisable by one person over the age of eighteen. A JUNIOR MEMBER - being a person who, at the date of election, is under the age of eighteen shall have no vote. Such member shall be one who at the commencement of the subscription year joins the club other than as a full member or a family member. AN HONORARY MEMBER - who shall be nominated and elected in the manner described in Rule 46 shall have one vote. A TEMPORARY MEMBER - who shall have no vote. No member except a Temporary Member may use the club premises, or any of the facilities of the club until forty-eight hours have elapsed from the date of posting of notice of election. The rate of Entrance and Subscription Fee for each category of Membership shall be proposed by the committee to the members at the Annual General Meeting in each year. Any member in any category of membership and being over the State Retirement age shall pay 50% of the appropiate MEMBERSHIP subscription. Any proposed changes shall be approved by a majority of those present and entitled to vote and shall become operative on the first day of January in the year following. The current rate of Entrance and Subscription Fee shall be prominently displayed in the club premises. Members shall also make the following annual payments as appropiate:- (a) An Annual Boat Permit fee of such a sum as the committee shall from time to time prescribe which shall entitle a member to sail his or her boat from the site at any time of the current year; and to store the boat at the site between ist March and 30th November of the current year. (b) A Winter Storage fee of such a sum as the committee shall from time to time prescribe which shall entitle a member to store his or her boat at the club between 31 November and 28 February of the following year. (c) An Annual Mooring fee of such a sum as the committee shall from time to time prescribe which shall entitle a member to use the mooring as allocated by the Mooring Secretary. (d) An Annual Postage fee of such a sum as the committee shall from time to time prescribe to cover the costs involved in distributing the club magazine “Navigans". (e) A Penalty fee of such a sum as the committee shall from time to time prescribe which shall be payable by any member who has not given notice of resignation in accordance with Rules 15 and 16 and who has not paid the appropriate fees by 31st of January. (f) The rates of the above fees shall be proposed by the committee to the members at the Annual General Meeting in each year. Any proposed changes shall be approved by a majority of those present and entitled to vote and shall become operative on the first day of January in the year following. ALL Subscriptions and Annual Fees cover the period January to December. ALL members shall pay their Subscription and Annual fees to the Club by the presribed payment date as notified on the Application for Renewal of Membership. 10 Every member shall furnish the Honorary Secretary with an up-to-date address which shall be recorded in the Register of Members and any notice sent to such address shall be deemed to have been duly del ivered. Election and retirement of members an Every candidate for membership (except candidates for Honorary Membership) shall be proposed and seconded for election by a Full or Family member of the club, both of whom must be personally acquainted with the candidate. Issued 17/11/91 Page

CONSTITUTION AND RULES OF THE MARCONI SAILING CLUB. 12 An application for membership shall be in the form from time to time prescribed by the Committee and shall include the name, address, and occupation of the candidate, and the signatures of the Proposer and Seconder. 13 Each application shall be accompanied by such entrance and other fees as shall be shown on the application form. These fees will be held by the club until the election has been held, and if the applicant is unsuccessful shall be returned in full. Provided that a member elected after the first day of July in any year shall pay half the annual Subscription applicable for that year; and a member elected after the first day of November in any year shall not be required to pay any Subscription or Annual Fee, save Winter Storage fee, but shall pay the Entrance Fee, Subscription and Annual Fees in respect of the year following election. 14 Upon receipt of an application for membership with the exception of Honorary Members (see Rule 46), the Honorary Secretary shall enter such application in the Register of Candidates and shall cause the application form to be prominently displayed in the club premises for at least fourteen days before the meeting of the committee at which such application for membership shall be considered. The election of all classes of members is vested in the Management Committee and shall be by a simple majority vote of those members present and voting at the relevant meeting of the Management Committee. The Honorary Secretary shall inform each candidate in writing of the candidate’s election or non election. He shall furnish an elected candidate with a copy of the Rules and Bye-laws of the club. 15. A member desirous of retiring from membership shall give notice in writing to the Honorary Secretary before the last day of November and shall not then be Liable to pay the subscription for the following year as long as all his property has been removed from the site. Upon re-application by a past member the committee may, at its discretion, excuse the payment of an Entrance Fee. 16 The committee may cancel, without notice being given, the membership of any member whose annual subscription and other annual fees are more than three months in arrears provided that the committee may, at its discretion, reinstate such member upon payment of arrears and Penalty Fee. No member whose annual payments are in arrears may enter any club event or regatta nor vote at any meeting. Conduct of members. 17 Every member, upon election and thereafter, is deemed to have notice of, and compliedly undertakes to comply with, the club Rules and the current Bye-laws and Regulations of the club. Any refusal or neglect to do so, or any conduct which, in the opinion of the committee, is either unworthy of a member or otherwise injurious to the interests of the club, shall render a member Liable to expulsion by the committee. PROVIDED THAT, before expelling a member, the Committee shall call upon such member for a written explanation of the member‘s conduct and shall give the member full opportunity of making explanation to the committee, or of resigning. A resolution to expel a member shall be carried by a simple majority vote by those members of the Management Committee present and voting on the resolution. 18 Members shall enter the names of all guests in the Visitor’s Book. Not more than three guests may be introduced in any one day and the same guest may not be introduced more than three times in any one calendar year. No member may introduce as a Guest any person who has been expelled from the Club under Rule 17. 19 A member shall not knowingly remove, injure, destroy or damage any property of the club and shall make restitution for the same if called upon to do so by the committee or by the Honorary Secretary upon the instructions of the committee. 20 A member shall not cause any communication in whatever form to be exhibited on any designated Official Club Notice Boards or premises without permission of the Honorary Secretary or other member of the Committee. 21 A member shall settle any indebtedness for refreshment or otherwise before leaving the club premises, or in accordance with any bye-law relating to the settlement of such indebtedness. 22 ALL suggestions shall be entered in the Suggestion Book and signed by the Member. CONSTITUTION AND RULES OF THE MARCONI SAILING CLUB. 23 Complaints of any nature relating to the management of the club premises shall be addressed in writing to the Honorary Secretary. A view from the Rear..... 5, With the new season, when you read this, just a few weeks away, the Sailing Sub and I thought it worthwhile to reiterate a few points for everyone’s benefit Early Season Sailing on the Blackwater Water temperature in March and April is at the low point of the year, and with a fair amount of fresh water sluicing into it upstream giving a constant flow with very little chance to stand and ware up, probably sits at around 6° C. That is around 31° lower than body temperature and is a very effective method of cooling. No matter how hot the sun, if is extremely likely that anyone immersed without a wet or dry suit for protection will start to suffer the effects of hypothermia within about 10-15 winutes. Hore relevant is the fact that the temperature will much more quickly reduce the power of your muscles, and so whilst you could expect to right your capsized boat easily within that time you will find your capability to do so dramatically reduced. This of course means that someone else will have to save your life, either (if you're lucky) a Club Support boat that will be with you within a few minutes or the RNLI or Police, which takes auch longer. THE MORAL 1S TO WEAR APPROPRIATE PROTECTIVE CLOTHING FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY. Support Boat Duties This relates to the above, only more so. Any one rostered as crew on either the RIB or Jack 6 must expect to go over the side to assist in a recovery operation. Bear in mind that you will also generally be very inactive and (on the RIB in particular) relatively exposed. PLEASE ENSURE THAT YOU ARE PREPARED WITH A WET OR DRY SUIT TOGETHER WITH ALL THE OTHER BITS FOR SUCH DUTIES. The Rule Book I am very aware that for the vast majority of people the Rule Book is a daunting publication (131 pages, 78 Rules, 16 Appendices (2 RYA, 14 IYRU for the barrack room lawyers)) and is enough to put all but the brave off starting to race. For your information, only a very small proportion of it is requisite knowledge for club racing. The basic Right of Vay Rules (31 to 41) are completely contained in 4 sides (pages 34-37). The slight complexity added when at a mark or obstruction (Rules 42 to 46) take up about 1/2 a page wore (pages 38-42). There are numerous books which include pictures of examples and explain the situation in detail (e.g. The Rule Book by Eric Twinname, updated by Brian Willis}. However, even this can be a bit daunting so in the spirit of making things simple my in-house expert (AKA Spot) has developed a fair amount of expertise discussing things over the winter. Watch for his articles in the august pages of future editions... Eariy Season Quiles The first few weeks of the Race Duties are given below. 6. ERREEE EE EREEERER EEEEEE EERE ERAGE RE RE EERE ES * * * * 40 YEARS AGO - MARCH, 1952 & * FEES OI A a Formation of the M.A.S.C. Yacht Section. A fair number of yachting and boating enthusiasts attended a meeting called by L.L.Jackson (8addow) for Friday, March 28th, to discuss the formation of a Yachting Section of the M.A.S.C. Mr.Hallam took the Chair. The following Committee of organisers was chosen :- Mr. Gill Hon. Organising Secretary and representative of New St. Mr. Nichols ) New St. Mr. Greatrex ) Mr. Quill New St. and Rivenhall Mr. Quilter E.E.V. Co. and Waterhouse Lane Mr. Colchester Bedell's End Mr. Hallam ) Baddow Mr. Jackson ) Mr. Sharpwel] Marconi College and Apprentices Mr. Tyler Broomfield A number of matters were discussed and it was agreed that a meeting of the Committee followed by another General Meeting should take place in the near future. KKK KKK KKK At 30 March, 1952, Mr L L Jackson sent the above brief resumé of the initial meeting (to discuss the formation of a Sailing Section) to the Secretary of the Marconi Athletic & Social Club, Mr Impey. In the covering letter, Mr Jackson explained that they hoped to hold another general meeting on 18 April at the MASC, and also pointed out that one main principle decided upon by this first meeting had been that anyone wanting to join the Sailing Section must become a member of the MASC. In another letter, to Mr Gill, I am struck by the formality shown by Mr Jackson. You would have thought that, having met together to plan the formation of the Sailing Section, he would at least address the Hon. Organising Secretary as ‘Mr Gill' - not so, for he addresses him as ‘Dear Sir' and formally sians off by ‘Yours faithfully, L.L.Jackson'. A sharp contrast to the informality of 1992. KKK KKKKKEKEK My meeting with Maurice Greatrex. One of those who attended the initial meeting to plan the formation of the Sailing Section was Maurice Greatrex who, at 88, is still a member of the MSC. Maurice has been following the ‘Navigans Past' series with great interest and I was pleased to accept his invitation to meet him and his wife to talk about the early days of the club. Unfortunately, Maurice was unable to offer any information on any 'informal' sailing section before 1952 or why our Commodores Board shows the names for 1950 and 1951. However, he believed the first meeting might have been held in the Blue Lion. Amongst the many anecdotes he recalled was when Eric Payne, sailing his yacht Electra II, left his mooring at Maldon - only todiscover that his keel remained firmly behind in the mud !. Others included Geoff Wardell loosing his wallet, and all his money, inacapsize and our old friend, Robbie Sims, driving around in a Rolls Royce (now thems was the days, Robbie !). Joe Gill (presumably the Mr Gill above) produced the winning design for a club burgee and received a glass ornament as a prize and which was created by Eric Cottam (who was both an MSC member and a glassblower within Marconi). We finally got around to talking about the river Blackwater in general and the traditions of Maldon, Brighlingsea and Tollesbury. It was then that Maurice claimed a somewhat distant Kk relationship with Captain Edward Carrington Heard (born 1879) who was possibly one of the most successful of the professional 'J' class and 12-metre class skippers between 1919 - 1939. It was Capt. Heard who sailed the America's cup 12-metre Endeavour I back home across the Atlantic, through storm and hurricane, taking some three weeks and being given up for lost with all hands. Maurice was a Rear Commodore of the MSC during the mid-1950's and sometimes pays a visit to the club. I suggested he try to visit us on the East Coast Piers Race day on 26 July as, hopefully, it will be a sunny day, fair wind and a sight well worth seeing. ** see 'The Salty Shore’ by John Leather. Mike B oreham
