Commodore’s Report 1997 In case any of you are wondering who the Commodore is, it’s me! My reasons for not being able to do a great deal of sailing are the same as last year, so I won’t repeat them! However I really do see an end to the turmoil in my job and expect to be spending most weekends at the Club next summer. From the point of view of the Club, I am delighted to report that this year has been mucha better one than last year, in most respects. However the galley service has not proved to be as reliable as we would have liked. When Mark and his team were here the service and food were to most people’s taste. It was a shame that the reliability was not of the same standard. The Club was left without a service on a number of high profile occasions and I and other Club officials were left to apologise to guests for the lack of food. I have to thank Pat Black for spending time liasing with Mark on many occasions after contractual agreements were broken. The main committee agreed that he should be formally censured by letter. It simply is not acceptable to fail turn up to provide a service after agreeing to do so. A lack of explanation or apology when there has been no galley service is also unacceptable and unprofessional. Mark decided he no longer wished to complete his contract and left. The matter will be pursued by the main committee. What is being done about the situation I hear you say? A number of organisations have been contacted and are being invited to tender for the service. The committee will try to ensure that a reliable organisation wins the contract. If there are any Club members who feel that they would like to provide the Club with a galley service they are welcome to put in a bid. Pat Black steps down at the end of the season after three years as Vice Commodore. His efforts have resulted in a great many improvements to the Club. Patio area, barbecue area, relocation of the fuel shed, alteration of the dinghy park to accommodate the Windsurfer rigging area, ditch filling, window replacement, repairs to the hard, galley service, to name but a few. I am sure that you will join with me in thanking Pat for all his hard work over the past three years. You will be pleased to hear that the environmental agency (nee NRA) have finally agreed to pay up for the necessary repairs to the access road. Clive Shenton is the engineer who we have to thank for providing a professional report on the state of the road, costing and specifying what needed to be done to put it right. Armed with this professional report, Larry Botheras was the ‘front man’ who did the negotiations with the environmental agency and convinced the ‘men from the ministry’ to part with the cash to put matters to rights. I am quite sure that without their input the Club would still be arguing with the Environmental Agency. A big thank you to both of you. The work will start after tenders have been received and the contract awarded. The mooring barge had to be replaced this year. Peter Clayton and the mooring team ‘supremos’ designed the improved version and I understand that recovering moorings is now a much easier and safer task. The old barge was sold. Thank you, Peter for your hard work in overseeing the job. The ECPR was again a success and, whilst we didn’t get the expected entry from the continent, everything else seemed to go off without a hitch. We were very lucky to have Libby Purves to present the prizes. I feel sure she will spread the good word about Marconi Sailing Club and the Piers Race. I am delighted that the money which was raised will be going to the Cirdan trust to provide bursaries for deserving young people. Watch for reports from the trust, in Navigans, giving details of how the money we donated was spent. Thank You to Mike Duckmanton and to your team who organised the event and of course to the Cruiser Fleet for providing the mother boats. Once again Charles, Chris and their team of helpers have run a superb Cadet Week. Bigger and better than before. Well done and thank you. | understand that activities for cadets will continue during the winter. Thank you to those Club Members who are taking on the responsibility for running those meetings. The sailing sub committee have worked tirelessly under the direction of Clive Shenton, organising and running a number of very successful open events as well as our own sailing programme. I have mentioned the ‘open day’ in Navigans. I cannot let this opportunity pass without mentioning it again and thanking all those Club Members who contributed to a very successful day which resulted in a number of people joining the Club. I have to thank Liz Hill for her unsung work as membership secretary. The job sounds fairly straight forward and indeed it would be if we all managed to get the paper work right first time and on time! Alas this is not always the case.

3. ’ There are of course a large number of other people who put in a great deal of time and effort to make the Club ‘work’ for us all. I hope all members will think about these folk and thank them as and when they meet them during the sailing season. Last year I hoped that all Club members would work together so that the interests of all Club members could be advanced in 1997. Iam sure that you will all agree that this has happened in 1997, thank you all for your efforts. In conclusion you will be aware that Steeple Bay Sailing Club has had to close through no fault of their own. A large number of members from SBSC will join Marconi Sailing Club. Some already have and I am sure that you will all make them feel welcome. Derek Kirby has already started the process by ‘sorting out’ winter storage for about a dozen cruisers from Steeple Bay. Thank you Derek for all your hard work in this respect. I look forward to everyone’s continued support in 1998. Colin Kidner. PRESIDENT’S PATTER No, I am not competing with the Commodore’s Column! - Just a few personal observations as another season ends. In his Commodore's Report at the AGM Colin felt moved once again to refer to his absence from the Club at weekends. It was extremely good news to hear that he will be able to enjoy his sailing once again next year. We all owe him a considerable debt of gratitude as, despite his extreme workload, his service and leadership to the Club has never faltered. Thank you, Colin, for your dedication and I look forward to ‘dodging’ you on the water next season.* On a personal note I would like to express my appreciation to those of you who attended the AGM and elected Neil. Steve, Peter and Patrick as Vice Presidents and myself as President. Elections to office at the AGM are usually unopposed, but this does not mean that the Officers and Committee members are in any way complacent. The opposite is the case, as more support is urgently needed to share the workload and guide the Club’s development. Another person who deserves special mention is Patrick Black who has completed his three year maximum term as Vice Commodore. In my opinion he has done more than anyone else in recent times to engender a sense of pride in our Club facilities and surroundings. It is up to the membership at large to sustain this effort by ensuring that it becomes the ‘norm’ to ‘tidy up’ before we leave. One aspect of the AGM which disappointed me was the apparent lack of interest by prizewinners in attending to collect their awards. A not inconsiderable amount of work is placed on the Sailing Secretary in organising the proceedings. Surely those who come to the Club each week-to race could make the effort to attend on this important day, or if this is impossible, send their apologies in advance. Finally, Mary and I would like to express our sincere thanks to Ian Caruth, ably assisted by Roseanne, for his term as Social Manager; and congratulate him for organising such a superb Laying Up Supper. The meal was excellent and the music great. Members who don’t come because they think it too formal and stuffy are living in the past. Come on all you wives and girlfriends, make sure he brings you next year. Ron Greygoose Sailing Secretary’s Report, 1997 Season ‘This season has again been less than ideal from the weather viewpoint, with 14 events being lost from the regular Points Series schedule of 44 races due to wind conditions. 67 boats participated in the 30 events sailed in these Series, down on last year’s 81. The largest fleet were the Dart 15s with 18 competitors, but all fleets had reduced numbers compared to last year, except the Solos who repeated last year’s 17. contd....

4. The weather did bless our chosen Open day with sunshine and a blissful force 3 which enabled us to provide enjoyable sailing experiences to a large number of visitors to our Club, some of whom are now members. Many thanks to the substantial number of members who made themselves and their boats available for that event. An informal racing series for Cruisers was organised successfully this year by Mike Turner, and it is hoped that this can be built on next year in order to promote competitive sailing in the Cruiser Fleet. Successful Open Meetings for Dart 15 and Solo Classes were hosted by the Club this year with entries for both in the 20s and the East Coast Piers Race was blessed by good weather and an entry in the high 70s. This event continues to attract the best crews from Europe and the UK and greatly adds to the Club’s reputation. Although it is mainly Fast Cats from the Club who enter, the event could not be held without the enthusiastic backing of the Cruiser Fleet and the other dinghy fleets. Thanks to all who took part. Members competing elsewhere have again put the name of Marconi SC on the map, starting back in December 1996 with JoJo Anderson as crew of a Cadet which gained an outstanding 4th place in the Cadet World’s in Bombay. (Ed's Note: With Dominica Lindsey from Burmham as Helm, the girls achieved the highest position so far for an all-female crew at this event. ) Our 6 boat entry at the Hurricane Nationals won the Team Trophy for the Club, and Mick Jones and Andy Sharp are the Prindle European Champions. Nearer to home, Paul Metcalfe and Steve Glynn finished 2nd and 3rd respectively, in the BJRC Cock of the River Senes. I would like to take this opportunity to offer my personal thanks to the Race Officers and Assistants whose efforts this season have made my job both easy and enjoyable. I must mention particularly John Weedon’s contribution in running the Wednesday Evening Series which remains a popular feature of our racing programme. Thanks also to those who helped crew the rescue boats. Your Sailing Sub Committee, under Clive Shenton’s able leadership, strives to provide you with the best sailing programme that we can, but it is not always easy to know what to aim for. Please tell us through your Fleet Captains, or directly to me, how you want your sailing to be in the future. Finally, 1 would like to end on a very positive note, with the observation that this season has seen the emergence of growing numbers of new cadets into our sailing programme. Let us give them every help and encouragement, for the future health of our Club lies in their hands. John Salmon WHERE ARE OUR TROPHIES? Happy Memories of Sailing Visitors to the Club on 19th/20th July 1997 Part of a thank-you letter from Tollesbury Mudclub: “The four or five boats which made the trip set out on the turn of the tide from Tollesbury in somewhat light winds but a perfect summer’s day. Making headway against the tide made for slow progress but, as time was not of the essence, still most enjoyable. However, the best was yet to come. Having moored to your visitors’ buoy we were received in a most friendly and hospitable way by one of your members and directed to the moorings available for our overnight stay. Coming ashore we found the barbecue already set up and ready to cook our food - what service. The evening progressed and we enjoyed the convivial company of your members and cheap beer. After playing some daft games, a favourite activity of our club, the evening concluded with one of the most beautiful sunsets I have ever witnessed on the river. As we all rowed back to our vessels for the night we could only reflect on what a great experience our trip had been. It seemed somewhat ironic that a cruise which had only involved a voyage of a few miles had been so enjoyable. On behalf of our Club I can only thank you and your members very much indeed for allowing us access to your club facilities, for making us so welcome and for the friendly company. As you may know Tollesbury Mud Club members occupy the moorings owned by Tollesbury Saltings Ltd off Woodrolfe Creek and therefore we do hot have any premises of our own. We do have a rather primitive barbecue and if any of your members are coming our way we will do our best to reciprocate, but doubt if we can come close to the standard of Marconi. Kindest regards, Yours sincerely, Roger Lankester, Chairman, TMC.” Marconi Cruiser Chases 1997 The *97 season is now over and with it the second year for the Cruiser Chase events. CRUISER COMMENTS - from the AGM Our Cruiser AGM was held on Thursday 20th November 1997 with a splendid attendance of 71 members with apologies being received from Danny Ainge, Mark Whitley and Don & Barbara Holdsworth. The meeting gave us the opportunity welcome new members including those from Steeple Bay Sailing Club, together with guests from Essex Police Marine Unit: PC Ian Frakes and PC Geoff Cousins. A brief resume of the points covered in the AGM are listed below: Review of 1997 Sailing Season: Spring Bank Holiday 24-26-May, Shakedown Cruise to Burnham which was attended by 19 boats with 45 members attending a Supper Dance at the Royal Burnham Yacht Club. ECPR on 27th July - As always the response from the Cruiser Fleet, without which this charity race could not be held, was first class. Ten boats, who were scheduled for stations from Brightlingsea northwards, spent the Saturday evening in Brightlingsea, having a meal in the popular ‘Munster House’ . To all of you who were on station for the ECPR event a big THANK YOU. Late Summer (August Bank Holiday) 23-25 August - Twenty four boats made the trip to Shotley Marina, many having stopped over at Brightlingsea on F riday night. Sixty members attended the dinner in the “Shipwreck Bar’ on Sunday evening. Some members had to return home on Monday, whilst the bulk of the fleet went into the River Deben spending Tuesday and Wednesday in Woodbridge. Twenty two boats in all, with the 6 single-handed yacht members hosting the rest of the fleet to Punch, Beer, Wine and Snacks on the Tuesday evening. Thanks, Guys. Events Hosted at Stansgate: On 14th June the Polynesian Cats, also members of the Walton Lifeboat Sailing Rally, and on 19th July, Tollesbury Mudclub. Each of these events were hosted in the Dell Bar, supported by a Bar B Q. Cock-Up Trophy: This was hotly contested by several Cruisers. Those of you who attended the AGM will know the details and contestants. The eventual winner was warmly congratulated. Who knows? In 1998 the star of the show could be you! Working Party: To be on Sunday 14th December 1997. Members’ attention was drawn to the projected Working Party and the various tasks to be undertaken. Election of Fleet Captain & Vice Captain: Both Derek Kirby and Malcolm Yeoman offered to carry on for another year and were unanimously re-elected. 1998 Sailing Season: Spring Bank Holiday, 23-25 May: Shakedwon Cruise to Burnham, details to be advised later. August (Late Summer) Holiday 29-31 August: A return to Shotley Marina with an evening meal on Sunday in the ‘Shipwreck Bar’ was the popular choice (bearing in mind the size of the fleet we take to these events at present) followed by a cruise to the River Deben and Woodbridge for those who are able to take the rest of the week off. Details to be advised later. September: possibility of a weekend in Heybridge Basin with dinghies to do the Watercress run. Watch this space. A.O.B. Boat Recovery/Lay Up: Peter Clayton & Murray Bates out.lined the possibility of using a travel hoist to layup certain types of boat. This is under review and more information will be forthcoming. 10. Sailing: Mr. Kidner read a letter from the Tollsbury Mud Club, thanking the MSC for the use of the club's facilitie in the summer. s He expressed his thanks to D. Kirby and R. Godbold who had organised the event. A letter from Maldon District Council was read, detailing the position of a new channel buoy that will be laid of Stansgate. Mr. Kirby was asked to check its position and inform the fleets. D. Kirby Bar: New registration certificate has been received (this is valid for 5 years). Mr. Godbold reported on the work and improvements that are planned for the winter. Membership: - The following people were put forward for membership of the MSC, e E. Cockerton J. Bennett G. Champion A. Clark G. Darby J. Goody H. Griffiths A. Groves R. Hadley A. Hamill A. Williams J. Burgoyne R. Henshaw All were accepted unanimously. Correspondence: Nothing to report. Any Other Business: Steeple Bay: Mr. Kidner reported that he had met with the commodore and other officers of the Steeple Bay S.C. they had discussed the option of moving to MSC. No decisions will be made until the Steeple Bay hold an EGM to wind up the club, however it is expected that 50-80 people will ask to join MSC. MASC: the executive expressed Concern about the lack of resources at the MASC, which were causing a backlog of tasks to be building up (including bill payment).

17a Dinghy Park Layout 1998 First of all, thank you to all Dinghy owners who have marked their trolleys with their name, etc. and who put their names on the layout to show where they have put their boat. It does make my job easier. You may have noticed that at the peak time of last year, around the end of August, there were only a few spaces left in the Dinghy Park; indeed, some people had parked their boats outside the area. Also we will expect a few new members in 1998, hopefully swelled by some members of Steeple Bay joining. That means we have had to look at how to get more boats in. The layout on Page 17 shows how we can accommodate about 30 extra spaces. It means losing one of the walkways through the dinghy park and the smaller boats having less space allocated to them. It also means that we will have to largely revise the layout and markings before the start of the season. So, please be sure to remove your boat from the Dinghy Park as soon as posssible and recover your anchors, etc. When the new season starts, please do not concrete your anchors in as we need to continue to be flexible in the way the dinghy park is laid out from year to year. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any queries about the new layout. or any other questions come to that. Also I am looking for someone who is willing to take over the dinghy park secretary job - so I will look forward to your call. Roger Smith, Solo 3872, [redacted] Wednesday Evening Pursuit Races 1997 Over quite a number of years now Colin Phillips and Colin Leveridge have between them taken on the Jack B Driver duty for the Evening Pursuit Races, each one taking alternate Wednesdays. This year, due to work commitments, Colin Phillips was unable to continue after the first couple of races, but I would like to use this end-of-year issue of Navigans to once again say thank you to the ‘two Colins’ for all they have done in the past to help with this event. I understand our Clive (Shenton) stepped in on several occasions this year to fill the gap. thank you, Clive. Our thanks also go to John and Mavis Weedon who again this year looked after the Race Officer duties for Wednesday evenings. Without this small team turning up regularly the event, of course. would not happen. The Club is a lovely place to be on a nice summer evening, it is a pity that the journey home from work is too late for many more of our members to be able to take part. Ed.

Commodores Notes. Time and Tide wait for no man. | have resolved to be more consistent with producing these notes this year. At the January Main Committee Meeting the question of publishing the minutes was discussed and it was agreed that this practice could lead to problems when matters relating to the conduct of members was discussed. The main committee has decided that a précis of the matters discussed should be published rather than the full minutes. I now have a ‘spur’ as this job falls to me! 1997 ECPR The Club has donated £3500, the proceeds from the 1997 East Coast Piers Race, to the Cirdan Trust. I received a letter form Nick Back, who runs the Trust, thanking the Club for the donation together with details of the Bursaries this money funded. Lee Harrison, chair of the ECPR committee, will publish the details after the next ECPR meeting. Clubhouse and Site The regular users of the Club will have seen that the ditch between the Cruiser park and Cat field has been filled. Danny Ainge was instrumental in organising the transportation and levelling of this clay. Once the clay has settled the additional space will be used for cruiser storage. The storage of 14 Steeple Bay Cruisers in the Cat Field is a temporary arrangement which had to be organised at very short notice and may have resulted in some ‘ruffled feathers’ in the dinghy fleet whose trailers were moved without prior consultation. This was because Haven Leisure gave Steeple Bay SC members some two weeks’ notice to quit. Sorry about that, but I hope you now appreciate why we needed to move so quickly. The repair work to the access road has now been carried out. The windows on the north and west sides of the Clubhouse have been replaced with double glazed, low maintenance units. A specification for the galley service was agreed. The committee agreed that breakfast, snack lunch and after-racing tea and cakes should be provided during the sailing season as outlined in the year book. The lunch menu should be similar the that offered when Jean Flook was in charge. This specification will be sent to three interested parties who may decide to quote. The interior of the Club will be decorated, a power point provided on the outside of the Race Control Cabin and the Diesel Fuel Store BUND will be constructed. Moorings A proposal to build a Travel Hoist for recovering cruisers has been made. Peter Claytonis gathering design and construction details for the Committee to consider. Social The Laying Up Dinner Dance was a success and we have to thank Ian Caruth for organising the event. Ian has relinquished his position as Social Secretary and we need a replacement please. In the meanwhile Steve Glynn has stepped in to organise the next Laying Up Dinner Dance on Saturday 14 November 1998. Neil Pembleton has agreed to organise an MSC Cruising Association Barn Dance for 1999. Sailing Sub Committee A draft programme for 1998-was presented and agreed. The following revisions are being considered: e Starting sequence and times e Safety boat rationalisation with regard to the Orkney e Prize giving phased throughout the season Maldon District Council are laying a new port hand Buoy at the west end of the moorings off the hard. The Starting canons are no longer ‘verboten’ and will be returned to the Club when Steve Hill can get the relevant police department to return his telephone calls to fix the details. Bar A new cold shelf and bottle cooler will be fitted to the Lounge and Dell Bars respectively. MASC has obtained a Club Registration License for MSC after protracted negotiations. Membership Mrs Lynda Chaplin’s offer to become Club Registrar was accepted. Thank you, Linda, for taking this job on. Next Main Committee Meeting will be in March. (Extended Christmas festivities and the short month of February means a couple of weeks between meetings) That’s all folks. Colin Kidner

Dinghy Park Secretary is Roger Smith, Solo 3872, Q1779-527564 Ed. 01799 RNLI_ ROWING RACE AT MALDON - New Year’s Day. There was a very good turnout of boats and spectators, and lots of Marconi faces were to be seen on the quay. The timing of the event is always dictated by the tide and the usual start times of the event are round about noon. The later 2 pm start was preferred by several of the spectators, but I believe it’s back to its more usual time again next year, and once again on New Year’s Day. Well over £10,000 was raised in sponsorship money for the RNLI. Thank You to all MSC Members who contributed to the total. and thanks from the occupants of the Marconi boat to those who sponsored them, either in advance at the Cruiser Fleet AGM, or on the Quay during the event. We were very lucky with the weather. Thougha bit chilly, it was not the biting cold that we have sometimes experienced and the gales and rain that were gloomily being forecast stayed away till the event was safely over. The Marconi boat (that I know anything about) entered the event with a Star Wars theme for their fancy dress. Darth Vader (Jenny Ball), Obi Wan Kenobi (Lucy Boreham), Han Solo (David Ball) and Princess Leia (Claire Davies) rowed the course in their usual pale blue boat kindly loaned once again by the Anderson family. Thank you to them and to the Boreham family who conveyed the boat to Maldon for the event and returned it to its home afterwards. Ed. FOR SALE Sadler 26, Silver Pearl, £22,500. Geoff Josey, SOLO Fleet Captain, Tel. [redacted] BACSPA News The AGM of the Blackwater and Colne Sailing Protection Association was held on the 27th November at the Maldon Little Ship Club. Mr Eric Rust of Brightlingsea SC was re-elected as Chairman and I continue as Honorary Secretary. New arrivals to the Blackwater may not be aware of the existence of the Association. It was formed as long ago as 1962 by 14 Clubs with the objective of protecting sailing interests on both the Colne and Blackwater estuaries. At that time the major concern was the possible adverse effect on sailing of the creation of marinas. Today the concerns are speeding by jetskis and powerboats: control of access; the environment; sustainable development of leisure activities, etc. The local councils are duty bound to produce so called ‘Estuary Management Plans’ to ensure harmony and sustainability. These plans are non-statutory for the time being but EEC legislation will soon be invoked statutory powers. The plan for the Blackwater was published in 1996 and is gradually being implemented. A copy is available for inspection in the Clubhouse at Stansgate. The consultation process has only just begun on the Colne Estuary and it is unlikely that their plan will be completed until 1999. BACSPA has representation on the Eastern Regional Committee of the RY A along with other associations from the Norfolk Broads, Herts and Cambridge, Crouch and Southend. The Regional Committee is working hard to try to persuade RYA Headquarters to decentralise some of its budget and responsibilities into the regions, in order to make the RYA more accessible and relevant to the needs of the ‘grass roots” sailing fraternity atlarge. Anyone having any queries concerning either the RYA or BACSPA should contact Derek Kirby or myself. Ron Greygoose, Hon. Secretary, BACSPA. CRUISER COMMENTS Working Party: Following up on the splendid attendance at the Cruiser AGM, there was an equally fine response to the Working Party held on Sunday 14th December. Even the weather played its part by providing a fine sunny day. It is impossible to single out people, but clearly the practice of splitting members into teams, each with a dedicated task, worked exceedingly well. I would like to thank the team leaders for organising these tasks so well. I must also pass on all your thanks to Doreen & Julie for organising the mid-day refreshments. Tender Racks: One of the tasks undertaken was to tidy up the Tender Racks. This necessitated moving all the tenders out so the area could be cleared. Many of you had already responded to the request in Navigans to move your tenders. However, those who had not, left us with the problem of some tenders seemingly bearing names of boats belonging to members who have apparently left the Club; and others with no names at all which, not being identifiable, could not be returned to their allocated spaces in the Racks. All of these tenders are at present at the end of the Cat Field waiting to be reclaimed or disposed of. Would those members reclaiming their tender please ensure their boat is suitably identified before returning it to the Tender Rack. Please may we also have all the tenders leaning the same way otherwise the neighbouring tender will not fit into its allocated space. Lastly on the subject of Tenders, would you please make sure the rack your tender occupies coincides with your mooring number allocated in the 1998 publication of the Cruiser List, i.e. if your mooring number has changed then so will your allocated tender space. Cruiser Winter Meeting Dates: Possibly by the time you read this, we will have already had our January Cruiser Winter Meeting at MASC with Frank Turner and his follow-up talk on the Maunsell Sea Forts. Next month. i.e. 19th February, we have Mark Dixon of the Environment Agency talking about ‘The Lost Marshlands of the Blackwater’. Please note there will be an additional Cruiser meeting at MASC on Thursday 16th April to present the 1998 Sailing Programme both for racing and flotilla cruising. Also at that meeting, Peter Clayton and Murray Bates will outline the proposals put forward briefly at last year’s Cruiser AGM with regard to the possible use of a travel hoist for recovery and launching of craft for Winter Storage. Fitting Out Supper, date to be decided: Please note that this will not be held on 18th April as previously stated. Those who attended last year’s event may recall we were not too impressed with the catering, therefore arrangements are in hand with another caterer who is unable do the 18th. As soon as a new date has been fixed I will publish it in Navigans, hopefully the next edition. Replacement Chain & Shackles: With the New Year now under way our thoughts turn to getting the boat ready for launching, but in doing so please do not forget your mooring may need attention too. Do not leave it till the last munute. If you require new chain or shackles from him, Don Holdsworth on [redacted] needs to know in good time, otherwise you may be disappointed. Boat Jumbles: For those interested I have listed forthcoming ones due to be held early on this year: Chatham, Sunday 15th February, 10am Essex Great Leighs, Sunday 8th March, 10am. Adults £4. Children/parking free. Beaulieu, 5th April, Lord Montagu’s Estate. M27 Junction 2: A326, B3054. Well, that’s all for now folks, it only leaves me to wish you all a Very Happy New Year with good sailing. Derek Kirby, Cruiser Fleet Captain

A Piers eye view by Charles Anderson The settling days of autumn are now past and we can all look forward to the lengthening daylight and warm spring days - hopefully. However, this time of year also lends itself to fireside reminiscence and plans for the forthcoming season. At the moment I have only just reached the former and my reminiscence has recently been focusing on last year’s ECPR. It has been prompted by Frank sending me a breakdown of the finances and I am pleased to see that the day raised about £4500 (includes some cheques sent direct to the Trust). Not bad I believe for a voluntary effort by all, both competitors and club helpers. The latter encompasses a lot and as the one who tends to purloin the assistance and stretch the good will of most club members, I have the most to thank you all for. Slim justice could be done to try and isolate the individual contributions but as a section there is no doubt that the cruiser fleet continues to hold the lion’s share. The years of involvement by many have formed a tight, disciplined fleet under the admiral eyes of Derek Kirby. It provides great comfort for those at base that as the fleet takes to the sea in the early hours of the day, the complexities of the coastline and weather are covered by such competent and experienced sailors. Although I have never done it myself I believe the same feeling of security must extend to the competitors as they run their keen eyes from orange flag to orange flag in the knowledge that they are at least heading in the nght direction if not actually leading the pack. I like to think that the involvement provides an added excuse to enjoy a days sailing as well as providing a purpose to the weekend. Perhaps extending the activities in general of the cruiser fleet’s season which are extensive; indeed it is a privilege to be included in their busy calendar of racing, visits to marinas, other clubs, pubs and breweries. What a life! But seriously, the bottom line is thanks and sincere gratitude. I know I have said it at dinners and others have said it on various occasions and it is not because there is the standard response form at the back of this edition. For those well organised members to return and those less _diarised (terrible Americanism sorry) to hang on to and return it later when the engine is \7 fixed, the hull is painted and the sails “==, bent-on. Commodore’s Notes There was no main committee meeting in February, so you have been spared! The Executive did meet, the main item being the ‘Five Year Plan’. We are sttt#tthinking and talking about this and our ideas will see the light of day in due course. Frank (Bennett) , treasurer, electrical expert, electronics wizzo and general all round useful fellow, has been doing his stuff again. Removing and refitting the cabling for telephones and wind indicators during the window replacement operations in the upstairs bar. He has also fitted an exterior weather proof plug on the Race PortaCabin. Thanks Frank. It is an ‘RCD’ so is very safe for use in adverse conditions. However if your equipment is faulty and it causes the trip on the plug to work it is no good you ‘forcing the RCD on’ whilst you complete your job. This action is likely to permanently damage the device so that it will need replacing. (Yes it has been done and RCD devices have been replaced twice.) If there is a problem with your equipment and the RCD device ‘trips’ you are ‘at risk’ if you by pass the RCD and use a power point inside the portacabin. If you use the Dell Bar you cannot fail to notice the CLEAN CARPET. Thank you, Joan, (Smith). Another moan. There are about sixty outstanding MASC contributions at present. These are folk who have been invoiced by MASC but who have chosen not to pay. I will point out that one has to be a member of MASC in order to be a member of the Sailing Section. There are some active and well known Club Members on this list, I am ashamed to say. Please get your cheque book out and pay your dues. If you don’t pay up , your Sailing Section membership will be terminated. Safety is a matter which is exercising the committee following advice from the RYA. Irrespective of whether staff are employed, the provision of cranes, winches, escort boats or other equipment for use by the members creates a statutory duty to ensure that the equipment is kept safe. This means that it must be properly specified and suitable for its purpose and that formal arrangements are in place for regular maintenance to ensure the equipment remains in good, safe working order at all times; that members are able to receive adequate instruction in using the equipment safely and that any breakdowns or defects are reported and promptly rectified. A number of issues with regard to tractor driving are already being attended to. ANNUAL START OF SEASON SAFETY REMINDERS: ADDERS: Members should be aware (and should remind any children they bring to the Club) that at this time of year they might sometimes come across an adder lying in the sun, often concealed in long grass. Please be careful where you walk and try not to disturb the animal which is harmless if left alone. THE SCRUBBING POST is not a safe place for children to play on at any time. Members please ensure that any children you bring to the Club keep off the Scrubbing Post. THE RIVER IS COLD for many months into the Sailing Season, even on apparently warm sunny days. Though Support Boats are out during all Club Races, it may happen that for some reason you can’t be picked up quickly after a capsize. It is important that you take measures before you leave the shore that would delay the onset of hypothermia. The following advice is offered in Navigans early in every season: Wear adequate clothing, ic. Wet Suit/Dry Suit etc. and Buoyancy Aid. Neea , Make sure your boat and its gear are sound. Ensure Personal Buoyancy and the Boat’s Buoyancy are both adequate. if you are inexperienced, cither in sailing or in our sailing area, please ask advice from other ; experienced helms. : 5. If you find yourself beginning to feel cold and tired while Sailing, return to shore straightaway, rather than wait until you are too cold to think rationally. IN ROUGH WEATHER: If Club Racing goes ahead in windy conditions this does not necessarily imply that it is safe to go afloat. Some very experienced helms and crews may be well able to cope with that day’s conditions but less experienced sailors could have a difficult and uncomfortable time. So please remember that even though Support Boats are there for Club Races, you should aim to be entirely self-sufficient, sail within your limitations, and remember on all occasions that your decision to go afloat, whether to race or to potter, is always made on your own responsibility. Ed.

SEA SURVIVAL COURSE on SATURDAY 25TH APRIL 1998 Organised by Cruising Association (Essex Section) The Cruising Association (Essex Section) are organising a 1 day course and would like to invite any members of Marconi Sailing Club who are interesed. Numbers are limited so the allocation of places will be strictly on a ‘First come - First served’ basis, with preference being given to Cruising Association members. The course will be run according to the RYA syllabus and those who successfully complete it will receive a certificate. The course will include: *Preparation for survival *Lifejackets and liferafts *Practical drill - approx 2 hours in swimming pool with lifejackets and liferaft *Principles of survival - routines, rationing, hypothermia *First Aid problems *Search and Rescue (including the use of flares) The date is: SATURDAY 25 APRIL 1998. Time: 09:00 (for 09:30 start) until 17:00 The venue is) MOULSHAM HIGH SCHOOL, BRIAN CLOSE, CHELMSFORD, ESSEX CM2 9ES. Course fee: £45 (not including lunch - please bring a packed lunch). This is a substantial saving on courses at sailing schools etc. You will need to bring: Notepad and writing implement A packed lunch {tea and coffee making facilities will be provided). And for the practical session: Foul Weather gear Swimming Costume and other light clothing to prevent foul gear chafing your skin Lifejacket Sailing shoes or boots Towel & shampoo/soap etc. For further information, please contact Neil Pembleton [redacted] On past occasions if the course has been oversubscribed, a second course has been arranged at a later date and this may be possible this year. If there is sufficient interest in the Club, some sessions can be arranged where the fundamentals of racing techniques, rules and tactics can be explained both in theory and on the water using RYA training materials. “IT’S HAD A COAT OF PAINT” The nautical equivalent of that pleasurable country pursuit of leaning on the farm gate is to look over the gunwale of a boat, passing the time of day with the people (usually working) on board. Those who did this on Jack earlier B in the year will have noticed that the engine and gearbox are nowa rather pleasing shade of light green. Indeed the heading of this piece came from someone who inadvertantly uttered the understatement of the year. Over the winter Jack B’s engine was in fact changed for a factory rebuilt unit. At the same time the gearbox was overhauled by the manufacturer's agent and the opportunity was taken to replace/refurbish many of the other items such as sea water pump and engine mountings. Many questions have been asked as to what was wrong with the old engine, why was the work necessary and (from a few cruiser owners who have engines of about the same age) what did we know about 11 year old engines that they did not? The answer to all this is that the old engine and gearbox had given reliable service over the previous 11 seasons and had clocked up several thousand hours of running. It is possible that the units may have continued to give satisfactory service for years to come. However, Jack B is essential to all the waterborne activities at the Club; from laying moorings to covering local and long distance racing. Any failure during the season due to the ageing of the major units would take the boat out of service for a long time and could happen when the people with the necessary skills were not available to do the work. It was felt that it would be better to replace and overhaul these major units before any deterioration in reliability occurred. By carrying out the work out of season it was possible to spread the effort and to take the time to get the best deals and do the work in the most economical manner. Hopefully the Club will get as good service out of the new engine as we got from the old. The Club is particularly grateful to Geoff Josey who masterminded the whole project and did the lion’s share of the work. RYA EASTERN REGION DINGHY SEMINAR This was held at Grafham Water Sailing Club on 14th February 1998. Sailing Secretary John Salmon and myself attended again this year on behalf of the Club. The Programme was full and the event well supported. Key points noted were as follows: 1. Latest changes in the RYA proficiency scheme - John Laws. He recommended the new publication ‘Sailing Across the Curriculum’ (ZS10, £9.95 from the RYA). This is a practical guide for those interested in promoting sailing for young people. Courses for Senior Instructor training and assessment are now more management oriented. Courses can be run for 20 persons on request (minimum age 18 years). The Powerboat Scheme is up and running and a similar scheme is being proposed for Personal Water Craft (Jetskis to you and me). 2. New 1998 Race Training Programme - Richard Watson. As from January 1998 ‘Race Trainers’ become a ‘Club Racing Coach’. The RYA ideally want one Club Racing Coach for every 50 members in a club. A new ‘Racing Coach’s Handbook’ is to be published this month, ref: YR10/98. (23,000 proficiency certificates are issued in schools each year, but very few join clubs and go on to race.) The two-day course can be organised on request for 8-15 people. There is a need to run a racing course to move from learning to sail to racing. 3. Youth Development for Clubs - John Allen. John Allen is the RYA Youth Development Officer. He is very enthusiastic, dynamic and knowledgeable, an ideal person for the job. The World Class Programme has £2.2 million backing from the Sports Council. The aim is to target the kids and to create world beaters. The Sports Council will only link with and fund ‘Top Clubs’, i.e. those judged to comply with certain essential requirements for their facilities and coaching abilities, e.g. a minimum of 1 male and 1 female Club Racing Coach within 3 years. A key issue is how to bring ‘non-family’ youngsters into sailing clubs. The social scene is the key - there must be a good youth social scene to attract and keep them. The rules of some clubs (not ours) prohibit or discourage youth membership. Clubs should ensure that all Race Training Establishments have full details of the facilities offered by clubs in their locality - a video was recommended. N.B. Bradwell RTE claimed to have no information on local clubs. 4. Sailing for the Disabled - Bill Smith, East Anglian Sailing Trust. He requested that clubs complete and return the latest single-page questionnaire from Sailability. There is currently no-one co-ordinating activities for disabled sailing in the Eastern Region. Requirements to be considered include: Access - parking, and water (pontoons); bar and changing rooms. Boats - must have a reasonable degree of stability. 5. Adventure Activities Licensing Regulations 1996 --John Laws. The scheme is up for review in the near future, now looking at a voluntary scheme for clubs to come into the main licensing scheme. Clubs at the moment have a privileged position. It is recommended that clubs have a manual showing responsibilities and codes of practice. A Code of Practice must represent what instructors actually do on the water. The RYA has an information pack ‘Risk Assessment Principles’ available on request. 6. Review of experience with the 1997 Racing Rules of Sailing This review was given by Jim Saltonstall MBE, the RYA Senior Racing Coach, (where did you get that extraordinary accent from, Jim?) My guess, in Birmingham. He was concerned that some competitors (even those at the highest level) do not observe any rules; and that the problem was world wide. Who is to blame for this? There is no referee on the ‘race track’. Race Management teams see infringements and do nothing about it! He referred to Racing Rule 69 ‘Allegations of Gross Misconduct’. If a protest committee believes that there has been a gross breach of a rule, or of good manners, or sportsmanship, or the sport has been brought into disrepute, it may call a hearing. Penalties include: warning, exclusion, suspension, reporting to National Authority. He then proceeded to give examples of typical right of way situations under the new rules. He emphasised the need for all competitors to learn and understand the 18 definitions in the new rules. (N.B. ‘Keep Clear’ and ‘Obstruction’ have been amended for 1998) 7. Final Question Session RYA was requested to produce a summary of the Adventure Activities Licensing requirements. Ron Greygoose.

Safety Safety is exercising the executive and main committee following advice received from the RYA. I am reading an RYA publication called Around the Red Tape, Law and Administration for Clubs and Schools. [Some of you may have read it!] I quote from the introduction of this publication. “The enormous increase in legislation in recent years and the ever rising tide of liability claims which threaten anyone organising recreational activities, particularly those withan inherent element of risk, make it essential for the club administrator to have access to comprehensible advice on the relevant law and practice. To ignore the potential dangers is not only foolhardy but may also land the volunteer's fellow members in trouble if any injured litigant chooses to take action against the club as a whole as well as the individual club officers.” “It is hoped that as well as being a source of information to those involved in the administration of sailing clubs and schools, this book will also be a source of comfort and reassurance.” The author is a Barrister at Law. The main committee is looking at the question of potential liability to third parties. We are concerned with the possible legal liability of a yacht club as a result of things done [or not] in the course of its normal activities, especially organising yacht races, and ancillary activities such as launching vessels and providing rescue services. In most cases the plaintiff will allege that the cause of the injury or damage was the negligence of the club. Negligence can be described as either the carrying out of any act which a reasonable man would not have carried out, or the failure to do something which a reasonable man would have done. The reasonable man test is used by the law to determine what standards persons must live up to when carrying out those activities which affect others. What this means in practice is that eventually all the activities which happen at the club will come under consideration to ensure that what we do at the club is as safe as we can reasonably make it. ( Will it pass the “Reasonable man” test?)

SOLO TUNING GUIDE _ This guide was first included in Navigans in 1997 and is repeated for new members and those with poor memories ! Mast Position The distance from the front of the mast at the heel to the outside of the transom at the floor is 3055mm. Forestay This should be just in tension when the mast (without sail) is pushed to the back of the gate. Shrouds These should be just in tension when the mast (without sail) is 10mm from the front of the gate. Chock Use one chock which just fits in front or behind the mast . Light airs Up to just sitting on the side deck. Upwind Chock behind the mast. No cunningham. Centreboard 25-50 mm of forward rake. Outhaul 20mm from black band. Kicker just slack Traveller 0-50mm from centreline. A small amount of leeward heel is acceptable. Off wind Use only enough centreboard to keep the rudder neutral. Leave outhaul on it’s upwind setting. Use enough kicker to stop the boom rising in gusts. Medium Airs __Up to fully hiked Upwind Chock in front of mast. No cunningham. Centreboard vertical. Outhaul 10mm from black band. Kicker just slack Traveller 0-100mm from centreline. Increase mainsheet tension as the traveller moves away from the centreline. Offwind As for light airs except : Ease outhaul up to 100mm Use enough kicker to keep the back of the top batten parallel to the boom. Heavy Airs Fully hiked overpowered. Upwind Remove chock Use cunningham to progressively depower the sail (too much and pointing will suffer) Lift centreboard progressively to reduce weather helm. Outhaul to the black band. Kicker just tight. Ease traveller up to 380mm from the centreline to keep the boat footing - but pull it closer to the centreline in flatter areas to maintain pointing. Use more kicker if the mainsheet needs to be eased often in gusts Offwind Same as medium airs except only ease outhaul and cunningham if more power is needed. Save the questions up for Jim_on September Sth !! Geoff Josey, SOLO Fleet Captain Tel. [redacted]

Answers to Navigans in rhyme please. CADET CAMPAIGN COMMENCES CONVINCINGLY Personally, I am still in shock that I’ve been out on the water already. Usually at this time I am searching the garage wondering where we put the boat. However, this year | thought that I’d better try and make it look as if I had made the effort to get myself organised in time for the first Cadet meeting - in order not to show Dad up. We met on the Saturday of the Bank Holiday weekend at the front of the club house. Dad was worried at 11:55 when there were still only five of us but by about 12:10 there were thirty-four of us! We started of with a quick treasure hunt to wake us all up and then had a capsize drill recap. The younger ones did some rigging then whilst the older ones revised the start sequence. Because the wind was very strong we didn’t get out onto the water until Monday and then, of course, the wind died totally. Due to our remarkable lack of progress the race was abandoned before anyone reached the second mark. The afternoon race was better as the wind had picked up and everybody finished - although it did take me about an hour longer than everyone else to do so. The next weekend enough Cadets turned up to persuade the Race Officer to organise a couple of Cadet races. The first one went very well, with some close racing and everybody finishing. The afternoon race was a different story. The wind became quite strong and a lot of us, me especially, spent most of the time upside-down and had to find alternative transport back to the Club. All in all, it was an extremely good start to the season and according to Dad we all worked together well. Thanks to all of those people who made it happen because we all really enjoyed ourselves. Sarah Davies, May 12th 1998

14. Is Your GPS Bugged? As far as I can establish there will be two ‘bugs’ infesting our GPSs in 1999/2000. If you have a Garmin GPS you can stop worrying right now because Garmin have assured me that none of their equipment will be affected. For the rest of you, you will have to contact the manufacturer/supplier of your equipment. These are the problems as I understand them: 1. “Week Rollover.” The signal sent down by the satellites to adjust the date in GPS receivers is a 10 bit data stream and deals in weeks. The programme has a capacity of 1,024 weeks and started in 1982. Apparently 1,024 weeks takes it up to 31 August 1999 when, unless this has been taken care of in the receiver's internal software (as with Garmin) then the receiver will revert back to August 1982 with associated time and distance errors. (I haven't checked the maths, this was how it was explained to me!) 2. “Millenium Bug.” The second problem is the infamous computer problem. If the receiving equipment utilizes only the last two digits of the year, when it sees the 00 of 2000 it will revert back to 1900 again with associated errors Extra information gleaned along the way: VALSAT: All modern sets including 8 channel parallel are compliant (OK) Source Mantsbrite [redacted] PHILLIPS AP Mk6: All recently (within the last 2 years) purchased or upgraded equipments should be OK. Software version 016 is the latest and is recommended. It was not divulged to me which previous versions are OK, so check your version and then give Comar a bell. To check your version: Enter “Setup’.... then .... “Security Reset’ .... then use <..> keys until “Phillips... Ser No. xxx ....Software Version xxx” is displayed. 6. RACE TRAINING Following the note in May Navigans a few responses have been received from members interested in some fundamental race rules, techniques and tactics training. For those who have expressed an interest, and any others who would like to join in, I plan to organise a little coaching at the Club on Sunday June 28". Those interested should gather at the race-office portacabin at 2pm on this day. PRIZEGIVING: This year we are trying a new experiment by presenting the prizes in three sessions through the season. We hope that this will not only reduce the marathon session which we normally have after the AGM but also make the prizes a little more relevant to the events for which they were sailed. CADET CORNER- See also Cadet Week Form on P. 18 Thomas Anderson It was brilliant to see so many of us on the water over the weekend of the 23" May, and I know that a great time was had by all. On the Saturday we did lots of practise starts, in order to make sure that everyone could recognise their five minute flag and start flag, although it was interesting to see who hadn’t been listening during the briefing, and therefore had to keep asking the committee boat “Is that the four minute/two minute/start gun?” I won’t mention any names (Tim Dowley), but it was good to witness a marked improvement in the starts of those who were there, although more practise is still needed, I suspect! The disco in the evening was thoroughly enjoyed by all the age groups that boogied away until well past their bedtimes! On the Sunday and Monday the bright-eyed cadets took to the water in their Toppers and Mirrors and there was some very competitive racing, especially in the Topper class, and the overall results were as follows: Sunday, 24" May: Race | Race 2 Overall Mitch Glynn 2 1 1* Quintin Hardwick l 4 ’ Michaela Glynn 4 3 :i JoJo Anderson 3 2 gmc As you can see, the top positions were very closely contested, with only two points separating first and second places. Unfortunately I do not have the results for the Monday races, (they should be on the results noticeboard in the clubhouse), but I know they are excellent as well. I would like to mention the Wednesday Night races. These take place every Wednesday evening at the club. They are Pursuit races, 1¢ the slowest boat goes off first and everyone else starts after it, depending on their handicap. You start off the hard, but after that it’s a normal race. This week we had five cadet boats racing, out of about ten, two of them came in the top three, so come down and try and improve your racing skills. As well as this series, there will also be a Summer Term Series over the 14 & 28 June and the 12 & 26 July. Finally, there will be a big race at some point after Cadet Week against cadets from the Blackwater and Royal Burnham sailing clubs, and so we should be honing our skills so we can thrash the pants off them. I am at Collingwood House, Royal Hospital School, Holbrook, Ipswich, IP9 2RX until 28th June. Email address: [redacted]. My home address is [redacted] [redacted], Steeple, Southminster, Essex, CMO [redacted] Keep up the practising and try to get along to the Summer Term Series. * Commodore’s Notes ECPR. Congratulations to Lee Harrison and the East Coast Piers Race Committee for organising a highly enjoyable and successful event. Thanks must also go to all the many folk who supported the event in a variety of ways, the event would not be nearly as successful were it not for your help. The money raised will again be used to provide Bursaries to allow some seventy disadvantaged youngsters to experience the joys of sailing as part of a team. Watch this space for details of who benefited. ‘Lost’ Property. Peter has had his sailing boots returned but his gloves and watch are still missing. Thank you to the person who mistakenly took the boots and returned them when he realised his mistake. I am deeply ashamed of the lack of respect for personal property which some other member/s of this Sailing Club have exhibited in this case. I hope the person/s concemed are able to live with their conscience knowing that they have stolen property belonging to a fellow Club Member. Bricklayer Needed! The Club could do with the services of a club member who has Bricklaying skills. The Environmental Agency state that if the Diesel in the Fuel store should ‘spill’ it must be contained. This means a ‘bund’ (wall of bricks to form a dam) has to be taid on the existing concrete base. If you can help please give Peter Bloomfield (Vice Commodore) a ring on [redacted]. Laying Up Supper. Steve Glynn has taken on the job of organising this year’s Laying Up Supper and yet again has a novel idea to move the event on from last year’s successful event. Please see your fleet captain or any member of the Main Committee for tickets. The event is at the Three Rivers Golf and Country Club and the ticket price is £21.50. Those of you who in the past have found the music too loud can be assured that effective steps will be taken to control the music volume this year. There will also be seating which will be in a quieter part of the room. Club’s Rubbish Skips. The Rubbish Skips provided for the use of Club Members should only be used for typical domestic rubbish. When the skips are collected the driver will check that ‘unauthorised’ rubbish has not been placed in the skip. This means that if he finds objects like car/ lorry tyres, caravan windows or aluminium masts in the skip he retums to base without the skip. The Club receives a letter explaining why the skip has not been emptied and a bill for the “wasted journey’. The offending item/s have to be removed from the skip by us before a further request to empty the skip is made, and separate arrangements have to be made for the disposal of the unauthorised items. I am sure that you agree that the extra work and cost to the Club is unacceptable. Please do not abuse the facilities offered by the Club. Money sent to Club Treasurer. If you send money to the Club Treasurer can you tell him what the money is for and give him your full name so that the funds can be accounted for. (The Treasurer may assume that you are donating funds to his holiday account!) See you on the water. The Piers Race Day Charles Anderson What canI say to you all but a big ‘thank you’. A fresh force 4 started this year’s event with a steady build through the race to the top-end of a 5 before returning to the calmer tolerances of a 3 - 4 by the end. Tony Bullimore finally arrived to get everyone off to an excellent start for both races. His plans originally included staying for the day but a late arrangement to go to Belgium on Monday meant he left us shortly after the starts. He did however satisfy the requests of three cadets JoJo & Charlotte Anderson and Quintin Hardwick. signing the bottom of their Toppers. His advice to them both was ‘if you ever see the signature don’t get stuck underneath’! The 140 competitors were delighted to hear they were destined to do the full course. All the mother boats completed their radio checks and proceeded to stations. The lead boats were very quickly among them reaching Walton Pier in about 1’ hours. With a lively sea running on the ebb one competitor and a TA operator were taken off boats feeling seasick. Another crew member was taken on board the Jack B with severe back pain and Vince and Mark had to retire after Mark sprained his hand badly. They successfully sailed home without requiring assistance. One competitor was dismasted and three others had to be taken in tow. On their return they all came up to thank me (YOU) for the amazing cover and speedy response of all those involved in providing assistance. I think what is rarely remembered and without becoming complacent, is that the ECPR is quite unique in the multihull calendar and that includes the rescue cover provided. I would like to add my word of thanks to all of you for your tremendous support and seamanship throughout three day. I do hope those of you booked in to the Maldon Fantasia arrived bright, breezy and managed to stay awake for the performance. Good sailing for the rest of the season. Don't forget to take part in the Summer Term series which has been well represented so far, often providing the largest fleet of the weekend. The last two are on the 12th and 26th July. Well done to JoJo. Charlotte and Quintin on collaring Tony Bullimore for his autograph on your Toppers.

SOLO MATTERS Welcome to Dennis Cheek who has recently joined the fleet. The Spring Points series has now been completed with John Salmon the winner, Roger Smith second and Ron Greygoose third. 14 races were sailed with a maximum turnout of 9 boats. The average number was 4.4 The Wednesday evening races are proving very popular with a maximum turnout of 7 SOLOS and an average number of 4.7. The fleet has now grown to 24 members with 22 owning SOLOS, so let’s hope for some perfect sailing days and numbers in double figures. Dates for your diary. Sunday 23 August - SOLO Barbecue - After the sailing of Summer Points 14 and 15 Saturday 5“ September - SOLO Training Day withJim Hunt - A must for all SOLO members, especially new ones. Sunday 6" September - Marconi SOLO Open Meeting. For those members who have not attended a Training day previously the details are as follows :- The day is split into land based and on-the-water instruction. The land based session starts with rigging a SOLO and then a detailed review of the settings for each point of sailing in various wind strengths. The sailing instruction usually comprises of a number a race starts with short windward legs - finish and then another start etc. Jim observes, coaches and comments from a support boat. It’s all informal, with plenty of opportunities for questions and discussion with Jim whose results speak for themselves with National and World SOLO titles to his credit. CRUISER COMMENTS First, may I say how nice it is to be back with you all having spent the past month cruising Holland aboard ‘HAPPY MEDIUM’ in company with Malcolm & Margaret aboard “SURUCA’. Whilst the weather could have been a lot better, the company could not have been and a great time was had by all. One of the first tasks we had to perform on our return was as Matriarch boat off Weymarks. Fortunately, the weather was an improvement on that generally experienced during our holiday. At this point I would like to thank those Cruiser Members who supported the East Coast Piers Race event. Unfortunately we seldom get to see the celebrities - in this case Tony Bullimore - or the competitors, some of whom travel from foreign parts to take part in this charity event. | was. however, ashore putting my dinghy away in time to hear the Commodore express his thanks to the Cruiser Fleet, together with the warm appreciation from the competitors. Well done, and Thank You. Maureen Ball tells me the next NAVIGANS may be a couple of months away due to the summer break* so I am exercising my mind on what to include in this issue. The most important, I feel, is the Flotilla Cruise to Shotley Marina during the late summer Bank Holiday weekend 29/30/31 August. The plan will be to leave MSC Saturday, locking into Shotley Marina during the afternoon. As with last year. we have been allocated the whole of pontoons *F’ and *G’, the cost being the same as last year, i.e. £1 per metre plus VAT. Those who have been to Shotley Marina before will already be on their computer; for those who have not. it will save time if you complete Shotley’s registration form (copy of which is on P.13) and return it to me by Sunday 23rd August. Sunday 30th August will be a layday for you to do your own thing, however, it is intended we all meet up in the “Stour Suite’ of the Shipwreck Public House at the Marina for an evening meal. Details of the Menu are listed below and the price of the meal is £15 per head with a concessionary price of £7.50 for children. Members who are not sailing up to Shotley but wish to travel by road to join us for a meal will be most welcome. Please complete the reply slip on P. 13 and return it to me, together with your cheque by Sunday 23rd August. For those of you who are able to take the remainder of the week off, a visit to the River Deben is again scheduled for Monday 31st August, stopping off at Ramsholt for the evening before proceeding up to the Tidemill Marina at Woodbridge on Tuesday. Wednesday will be a layday at the Tidemill with a Bar B Q in the evening to which the single handed crews are invited as the guests of the remainder. Arrangements for the rest of the week will be left open with possible visits to Titchmarsh Marina, Woolverstone, Lavington, etc. all up for consideration. As usual there will be a notice on the Club Notice Board, but prompt return of the reply slips would be appreciated. I would also mention that on weekend 25th/26th July we are hosting members of the RNSA who will be sailing up to join us ashore for a Bar B Q and drink in the Dell Bar. If your mooring is available that weekend I would appreciate your call or just leave a note on the noticeboard. I think that’s enough from me for now. Derek Kirby, Cruiser Fleet Captain *Next Navigans will be the October issue which should reach Members at the end of September. Tickets at £21.50per head available from Committee Members or Steve Glynn on [redacted]1 Camping Fortnight Another excellent two weeks with good weather apart from some rain on a couple of occasions. Cadet Week started with 70 Cadets and the wind just a bit strong for the beginners’ comfort. The Cadets soon became confident in going out in any reasonable breeze and were only kept ashore on those occasions when there was no wind at all. The usual disco and prize-giving took place during the middle weekend, details later in this issue. Lack of wind on the middle Sunday prevented a planned race against visiting cadets from Burnham, which was a pity. There are now an extra 6 Picoes added to the fleet of monohulls at the Club - the 6 demonstration boats having been offered at a reduced price and being snapped up by Cadets who had tried them and liked them. It was lovely to see several boats out regularly on the water during the second camping week, manned by increasingly confident cadets. On the last Friday evening there was a ‘hog roast’ cooking all afternoon over an open fire on a rotating spit. Several campers brought their tables and chairs onto the Commodore’s lawn and it became an excellent social evening for those who took part. Grateful thanks go to Charles Anderson and Chris Davies who led the way with organising Cadet Week, to all those former cadets who volunteered as instructors (having a tiring but enjoyable week in the process), and to those adults who helped with instructing and/or who went on the water with the various support boats. Cadet Week could not be the success it is without all of you. As an onlooker J could see Steve Glynn and Mick Richardson amongst others doing various tasks to ensure the smooth running of Camping and Cadet Weeks; thanks to them and to all others who contributed anything to the work involved. The very necessary decision to restrict the number of camping units paid off, especially for those using the dinghy field which was extremely cramped last year. The disadvantage was that some may not have been able to have their preferred spot and some may have been disappointed in not being able to camp at all, especially in the first week. It is a pity, but we have no choice but to tailor the Club’s most popular event to fit into the space available. One other improvement we need is the co-operation of non camping members - that they do not leave their cars parked, at the time camping starts, where the pitches will be. This request and a sketch of the pitches will be published in next year’s pre-camping Navigans, as it was in this year’s, and I do hope those concerned will be willing to help us out. Jack B was hauled out for her-annual summer maintenance during the middle camping Weekend and, with the weather so good again this year, the work did not take long. Thanks to Murray for spraying off the weed and barnacles, to Jenny and David (with the help of Jo) for sanding the old varnish, followed by re-varnishing and painting: and to those who offered to help but weren’t required because the work went so quickly. Jack B, at my request, was kept on the hard for all these tasks, it was the coolest place to work on the boat when the forecast for a heatwave turned out to be an accurate one! David found his lost waterproof jacket in the end - did anyone lose an unusual key fob of the noisy variety at the site during camping? Contact a Ball family member and we'll get it back to you. Ed.

Geoff Josey, Solo Fleet Captain, [redacted] Solos at Marconi Despite dire weather forecasts‘as a result of hurricane Danny, 28 boats, comprising 15 visitors and 13 locals, turned out for Marconi Sailing Club’s Solo Open Meeting on the River Blackwater in Essex on 6th September. Hurricane Danny or not, the start of the first race had to be delayed waiting for the wind to fill in, and light winds were to be the order of the day. After a curious start with the boats trying to avoid being swept over the line by the tide, Roger Smith led the way round in a fading breeze, hotly pursued by Gordon Barclay. In fact Gordon, using his experience of tidal estuary sailing to good effect, just pipped Smith on the line, with Steve Ede third. The boats had to be towed back to the Club for an extended lunch break waiting for the wind to settle and fill in again. It eventually filled in from the South and in the second race Barclay and Jerry Garner battled it out up front against the breeze and the tide, Barclay ultimately coming out on top again, giving him two wins and the overall result. The end of his successful three year term as the President of the Solo Class Association has obviously revitalised his sailing performance. The third race had plenty of incidents, not least of which was the diversion of the rescue craft, at the request of the Coastguard, to rescue the crew of an incendiary power boat on the river.** However, the Solo Fleet was largely unaware of this as they raced to settle the other places. Ron Laurie set the pace, chased by Samantha Husk, Steve Ede, Mike Wilkie and Tony Cook. At the end of the second beat Laurie and Ede had to do turns having touched the windward mark due to the tide, leaving Husk in the lead followed by Cook and Smith. At the end Steve Ede came back to take the race, followed by Cook, Smith and Samantha Husk fourth. Results: Ist. 3934, Gordon Barclay Chichester YC 2nd. 4005, Steve Ede, Ardleigh SC 3rd. 3872, Roger Smith, Marconi SC 4th. 4150, Tony Cook, Littleton SC Sth. 4189, Jerry Garner, Littleton SC 6th 4190, Mike Wilkie, Littleton SC **Ed’s note: I understand from later information that it was a simple case of engine breakdown, and thankfully not a fire, which may have been indicated at first by smoke from their flare.

FLOODGATES - Reminder: _ It is the responsibility of each and every Member to check at the end of the day before leaving the site that the Floodgates are properly closed. This applies between Ist September and Ist May each year. The Floodgates are not locked so a key is not needed to operate them. Opening the right hand gate only, gives enough room for a tender to pass through, but both gates need to be opened for a car. On windy days make sure you open the gates right back to the wall or they could be blown shut on your car as you drive through. To close: viewing the gate from the landward side, the left hand gate is bolted into a slot in the ground and is closed first. Turn the top handle anticlockwise to lower the bolt. The right hand gate has a lever to secure it closed against the left hand one - this is the bit that takes some muscle. Reversing these actions allows you to open the gate.
