Smith, [redacted] Catamaran Park Officer, L Harrison, [redacted] ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING - ELECTION OF COMMODORE It is my intention to offer myself for election as Commodore of the Club at the Annual General Meeting in November. I have been a member of the Marconi Sailing Club committee since 1980 and during that time served in a number of positions including Treasurer, Commodore and Vice President. I am also a Vice President of the Marconi Atheletic and Social Club. In addition I am also a member of the committee for the Essex Section of the Cruising Association. I have been sailing since my youth, initially on other people’s boats, then in Graduate and Mirror dinghies until I bought my Snapdragon ‘Rasputin’ in 1987. For a number of years I was actively involved with the East Coast area of the Ocean Youth Club. I passionately believe that the greatest strength of the Club is the diversity of the boats and sailing that we have available to us, from sailboards through monohull and catamaran dinghies to cruisers; and from very competitive racing to “Mucking about in boats’. Another great strength is the ‘Self Help’ aspect from the acquisition of items to improve and develop the Club, to the volunteers who organise all the activities both on and off the water, resulting in our reasonable membership fees. If I am elected as Commodore, it is my intention to build on these strengths to carry the Club successfully forward into the next Millenium. To this end, I will be arranging a discussion evening early in 1999. This will be similar to the one held during my previous term as Commodore to seek the views of the membership on a number of subjects, including the maximum number of members, improvements to the facilities within the club house, general improvements to the grounds of the Club, and any other comments. This will be your opportunity to express your views to the Committee so that they can develop future short and long term plans to the benefit of all members, fleets and interests of the Club. Jenny Ball will be offering herself for election as Rear Commodore at the same time. As most of you will be aware, Jenny has been a member of the Club for a considerable time, initially as a Cadet and then as a Full Member. During this time she has always been active in her sailing and her support for the behind the scenes activities, such as her help during Cadet weeks and involvement with a number of committees. | fully support her offering to stand and will be proposing her for the position. Neil T. Pembleton

Cruiser Comments August Bank Holiday Cruise. The late summer bank holiday weekend marked the last of this year’s organised flotilla sailing events with a visit to Shotley Marina followed by a meal in the “Stour Suite” of the “Shipwreck Public House” on Sunday 30th August. As with last year the support was tremendous. The weekend started with 8 boats making an early start from the Club for an overnight stopover at Brightlingsea and, whilst it was nice to meet up with Peter Clayton & Family aboard “PEACE”, it was sad that this was the end-of their holiday up the East Coast and they were in fact on their way back to MSC. Saturday turned out to be another glorious day, perhaps too good, since there was little or no wind to sail by. Those leaving Brightlingsea were soon joined by other members off Colne Point sailing up the Wallet towards Walton. Possibly learning the lessons of last year when we arrived almost en b/oc, arrivals this year were more random, with some choosing to sail into the river Stour to visit the hostelry at Wrabness - no prizes for guessing who! - whilst 2 other intrepids ventured into the River Deben since they were unable to join us there later. By Saturday evening 21 Club boats had arrived into Shotley, the last being VARUNA II arriving about 22.30, Roger having to wait for Mike who had come directly from the airport having just returned from Tenerife. The fleet so far comprised: HAPPY MEDIUM, ICARUS, FANTASEA, CAPRICORN, WINKLER, ANGEL II, GAIETY OF LYMINGTON, ALDEBARAN, GREEN PANTHER, PEPPER, CLANEDA, SABRE, RIMFIRE, JAED, RUBICON, TELEMON, WINDSONG, SERUPIN II, MILADY D, KAYMAR, VARUNA II. Sunday saw the arrival of SEA GEM, OCEAN SLIPPER, JUNO, ANTIGUA KISS, HARTLEY, and REFLECTION who had left Ramsgate at 0300 that morning to join us. What dedication! This made the total of boats attending 27, a truly excellent turnout and credit must go to Shotley Marina who made avaliable the two linear berths F & G for our sole use. Even so, the family was not yet complete for Leonard Scholl, who was unable to sail his yacht COMOCEAN up to Shotley arrived by car to join us for the evening meal. So there we were, 28 boats in all. The meal was excellent, the compan, treat and I am sure a good time was had by one and all. Monday saw the break up of the fleet, those needing to return to MSC took their leave whilst the rest ventured forth into the River Deben and up to the Tidemill Yacht Harbour at Woodbridge, arriving by the late afternoon. Learning the lessons of the two previous years, it was decided to hold the Bar B Q at the Tidemill on Tuesday evening. At first this also seemed doubtful as the rain poured down all the previous night into the morning but, undaunted, the arrangements were made, food and drink bought and by the middle of the afternoon the sun was out and a very pleasant evening was had by all, probably helped along by Doreen’s Rum Punch. After this it was everyone doing their own thing, some stayed on in the Deben for another day returning to Brightlingsea the following day, others had already made it to Brightlingsea, others went back into the River Orwell. Was it something I said? By this tme CORNISH GOLD and SURUCA had arrived in the Walton Backwaters being too late to join us in the Deben, so yours truly together with REFLECTION, joined them and, thanks to Peter Arnold’s magnificent water taxi service, we were all able to meet on board SURUCA for an exchange of banter and, of course, refreshments. Sadly the weather put paid to the proposed gathering of the clans at Brightlingsea for a fish and chip supper, but at least everyone arrived back home safe and sound. RNSA Visit. During the weekend 25th/26th July we hosted members of the RNSA to a Bar B Q etc. in the Dell Bar. The weather was fine and a grand time was had by all, resulting in a letter from Terry Ryser, Hon Sec of the RNSA-east coast unit, thanking MSC members for a very warm welcome. (I’m sure no pun was intended.) We look forward to them visiting us again next year. Unattended Cruisers in Cruiser Park. JACK B DRIVERS Propeller Shaft Greaser The shaft greaser should be screwed down just until resistance is felt. It should not be screwed down tight as this creates excessive pressure in the shaft seal which will force it apart, letting in the water. Water Cooling There is a large amount of very fine weed floating in the water. When drawn into the cooling water inlet this is capable of creating a total blockage. The filter may be clean but the hull inlet may be totally blocked. Drivers are asked to keep a constant check on water flow from the exhaust. If flow is inhibited, check the filter and inlet. A piece Of cane is stored aboard for cleaning out the water inlet. Please don’t rely on the engine overheat alarm as, by the time this is activated the raw water circuit will have been running dry for 10 minutes or so, and damage to the raw water pump will occur. Navigans is the means by which all Club Members and Committees can be in touch with each other and keep abreast of Club events throughout the year. Our new Navigans Editor/s are Belinda and Kevin Dowley, whose offer to take over from me at the end of this year was a welcome one which means the magazine can now continue without any break. The new address for all future Navigans contributions is on the front page of this edition so please remember to send them there, though any finding their way to me will be passed on. Any Members, and particularly Club Officers, who would like to communicate with the club at large through Navigans, please make sure you let the Editor’s team have the information in good time — please don’t leave them guessing! Rule of thumb is that an item for a particular month’s edition should reach the Editor at the start of the previous month. A new Editor will mean the chance of a new look and a fresh approach to Navigans and I look forward to seeing the magazine flourish in new hands over future years. Ed. This is my last production of Navigans. During my time with the magazine it has been an enormous help that the printing and distribution have been done by other volunteers. Leon White took care of this for several years (and still helps out occasionally), followed by Keith Starkey, who now shares the work with Tony Holbrook. Thanks are due to them all for giving their time and I always knew my work was finished once the typing was done and the pages were on their way to the next stage. My thanks also go to Committee Members over the years who I know have taken care of many details in the background for me, to Larry Botheras and his Committee three years ago for providing the equipment to make the work so much easier, and lastly to my husband Ray for sensible advice, proof reading, and reminders of what should appear in an issue. On Pages 12 & 13 there is a brief nostalgic trip through Navigans and Editors Past, including a copy of the first issue ever produced, which includes a piece of history - a petrol shortage - due to Suez, I’m told. View from the Rear You may have noticed from elsewhere in this issue that the post of Commodore is being contested for the first time in ages. I believe that it is a sign of a healthy club that people are clamouring to serve its interests. You will also note that I am one of the nominees. I would like to tell you something about me and the direction in which I would seek to take the Club in the next three years. I have been a member for ten years and have been Fleet Captain and, for the last 3 years, Rear Commodore. I sail a Tornado catamaran with my son andI intend to carry on as long as my body lasts. I believe we have a Club to be proud of. My trips to various Clubs throughout the country while campaigning the Tornado have reinforced this belief. Our site and sailing waters are excellent and our broad based approach to sailing adds greatly to the strength of the Club. I see my first duty as Commodore would be to ensure the continued existence of the Club, not for one section of the Club but for all, regardless of whether a member sails a cruiser, dinghy, catamaran or windsurfer either racing or not. The financial administration of the Club been somewhat "hand to mouth" over recent years with self interest groups within the Club pushing for expenditure. I will seek to improve the predictability of our spending by the introduction of a Five Year Plan which would programme all future expenditure. It is no secret that my own vision for the Club is to improve our on-shore facilities so that they reflect my perception that our Club is in the "Top Ten" of national sailing clubs. We are all aware that Lottery money is available for well thought out schemes and it would be my intention to seek funding from that source. Lottery money is not all good news as organisations are expected to find half the money for capital projects themselves. Almost every Club member has his or her own vision of their future requirements for the Club, just as I do. By consultation and consensus the Five Year Plan would be developed to take "on board" as many of these visions as can be practically and financially achieved. The decision to adopt the Plan would be made by the whole Membership, probably at an AGM. I would now like to tell you what I am not. I am not retired, not an ex Marconi employee and I do not sail a cruiser. I truly believe each of these attributes are admirable, and my admiration for Pat Black, Frank Bennett and Peter Bloomfield, who are nominated unopposed for election to the Executive Committee, is unbounded. However, if my rival for the post of Commodore is elected, 80% of the Executive Committee would then be composed of such members, and I do not think that would be representative of the Club as a whole. If elected I will deal fairly and evenly with each section of the Club. If Cat sailors think I will always take their point of view will be disappointed, but they can be assured that their views as well as others will be heard and put on the balance. I have proposed John Salmon as Rear Commodore. John, who sails a Solo, has been Sailing Secretary for two years, and I have come to rely on his perceptive ideas and energy in their implementation. As Rear Commodore, John would Chair the Sailing Sub Committee and be a member of both the Executive and the Main Committee. Together, and with the experience of our colleagues, we will make an effective and representative management team for the Club. Whatever your views and loyalties I urge you to attend the AGM on 15" November and cast your vote in the way that will benefit the Club as a whole. Above all let's remember that we are all members of this Club so we can enjoy our sport of sailing. Clive Shenton, Rear Commodore

THE MOLLIETTE When taking the short cut across Mersea flats there is an east cardinal mark on the Cocum Hills that stands up like a signpost. Whether you are cutting across in the Piers Race or trying to cheat the tide in your cruiser you can’t miss it. In the old days (well up until sometime in the 1970s) this was a green wreck buoy. The locals called it the ‘Molliette’ buoy. At low tide some of the wreckage that the cardinal mark is guarding is visible. What was the Molliette and how did the wreckage come to be there? The story starts with the U-boat successes of the Great War. Steel for shipbuilding was in short supply and a number of ferro- concrete vessels were built on both sides of the Atlantic. (Incidentally this method of building was not new as the first ferro boats were reputed to have been built in 1848.) In 1919 two ferro-concrete vessels were built in the yard of James Pollock, Sons & Co Ltd at Faversham. The first to be completed was the Molliette and the second the Viollette. These vessels were auxiliary schooners with three masts, all gaff rigged but without topsails. As built Molliette had a bowsprit. Each had a 120hp, two cylinder Bolinders oil engine running at 225-250 revolutions per minute. They were very boxy vessels designed for ease of construction. Dimensions were 125 ft. long by 25 ft. beam. The concrete on the hulls was three inches thick. Performance under sail was reputed to be ‘sluggish’. The crew of four or five men lived in the foc’s’le and three officers lived in the deckhouse aft. The story of Viollette is soon told. This unhappy vessel appears to have been unsatisfactory during trials and was not accepted by her intended owners. However she presumably traded until 1921 when in January, in bad weather, she dragged into Southend

11. pier. The pier was severed (marooning the Pierhead Keeper and his family, who in those days lived in a bungalow at the pierhead) and the Viollette sank. She was raised and ended her days as a hulk on the Medway. Molliette had a longer life, although she appears to have had more than her fair share of mishaps. She was damaged in a collision in 1919, was ashore a few times and is reputed to have collided with Tower Bridge although there does not appear to be any record of this. When her coasting days were over Molliette was sold to Essex owners and was fitted out as a night-club. The Molliette story finished (almost) on the Mersea flats during the last war when she was used for bombing target practice. However ferro-concrete vessels are well nigh indestructible thus the wreckage remains on Cocum Hills to this day. (Most of the above information was obtained from the East Coast Digest of February 1976. If anyone has any further information on the Molliette’s history please put pen to paper.) Sailing Section then produced on foolscap paper, and probably typed on a stencil — a very tedious method compared with today’s keyboard and screen, especially for the less accurate typist! Between January 1974 and December 1984 the front page of Navigans included a photograph of a sailing activity at the Club, or occasionally of a winter social event or prize giving. For those of us who were around at that time they are fascinating pages to re-visit. If any of our longer-term Members have copies of 1950s or 1960s editions, which are obviously going to be rarer, I would be pleased to receive them (either to keep or to copy and return) in order to add to the Archive. Maureen Ball, Retiring Editor of Navigans.

20. Commodores report 1997. In case any of you are wondering who the Commodore is, it's me! My reasons for not being able to do a great deal of sailing are the same as last year, so I won't repeat them! However I really do see an end to the turmoil in my job and expect to be spending most weekends at the club next summer. From the point of view of the club, I am delighted to report that this year has been mucha better one than last year, in most respects. However the galley service has not proved to be as reliable as we would have liked. When Mark and his team were here the service and food were to most people's taste. It was a shame that the reliability was not of the same standard. The club was left without a service on a number of high profile occasions and I and other club officials were left to apologise to guests for the lack of food. I have to thank pat black for spending time liasing with mark on many occasions after contractual agreements were broken. The main committee agreed that he should be formally censured by letter. It simply is not acceptable to fail turn up to provide a service after agreeing to do so. A lack of explanation or apology when there has been no galley service is also unacceptable and unprofessional. Mark decided he no longer wished to complete his contract and left. The matter will be pursued by the main committee. What is being done about the situation I hear you say? A number of organisations have been contacted and are being invited to tender for the service. The committee will try to ensure that a reliable organisation wins the contract. If there are any club members who feel that they would like to provide the club with a galley service they are welcome to put in a bid. Pat black steps down at the end of the season after three years as vice commodore. His efforts have resulted in a great many improvements to the club. Patio area, barbecue area, relocation of the fuel shed, alteration of the dinghy park to accommodate the wind surfer rigging area, ditch filling, window replacement, repairs to the hard, galley service, to name but a few. I am sure that you will join with me in thanking pat for all his hard work over the past three years. You will be pleased to hear that the environmental agency (nee NRA) have finally agreed to pay up for the necessary repairs to the access road. Clive Shenton is the engineer who we have to thank for providing a professional report on the state of the road, costing and specifying what needed to be done to put it right. Armed with this professional report, Larry Botheras was the ‘front man’ who did the negotiations with the environmental agency and convinced the 'men from the ministry’ to part with the cash to put matters to rights. I am quite sure that without their input the club would still be arguing with the environmental agency. A big thank you to both of you. The work will start after tenders have been received and the contract awarded. The mooring barge had to be replaced this year. Peter Clayton and the mooring team 'supremos' designed the improved version and I understand that recovering moorings is now a much easier and safer task. The old barge was sold. Thank you peter for your hard work in overseeing the job. The ECPR was again a success and whilst we didn't get the expected entry from the continent everything else seemed to go off without a hitch. We were very lucky to have Libby Purvis to present the prizes. I feel sure she will spread the good word about Marconi sailing club and the piers race. I am delighted that the money which was raised will be going to the Cirdan trust to provide bursaries for deserving young people. Watch for reports from the trust, in Navigans, giving details of how the money we donated was spent. Thank you Mike Duckmanton and to your team who organised the event and of course to the cruiser fleet for providing the mother boats.

21. Once again Charles, Chris and their team of helpers have run a superb cadet week. Bigger and better than before. Well done and thank you. I understand that activities for cadets will continue during the winter. Thank you to those club members who are taking on the responsibility for running those meetings. The sailing sub committee have worked tirelessly under the direction of Clive Shenton, organising and running a number of very successful open events as well as our own sailing programme. I have mentioned the ‘open day’ in Navigans. I cannot let this opportunity pass without mentioning it again and thanking all those club members who contributed to a very successful day which resulted in a number of people joining the club. [ have to thank Liz Hill for her unsung work as membership secretary. The job sounds fairly straight forward and indeed it would be if we all managed to get the paper work right first time and on time! Alas this is not always the case. There are of course a large number of other people who put in a great deal of time and effort to make the club ‘work’ for us all. I hope all members will think about these folk and thank them as and when they meet them during the sailing season. Last year I hoped that all club members would work together so that the interests of all club members could be advanced in 1997, I am sure that you will all agree that this has happened in 1997, thank you all for your efforts. In conclusion you will be aware that Steeple Bay sailing club has had to close through no fault of their own. A large number of members from SBSC will join Marconi Sailing Club. Some already have and I am sure that you will all make them feel welcome. Derek Kirby has already started the process by 'sorting out’ winter storage for about a dozen cruisers from steeple bay. Thank you Derek for all your hard work in this respect. I look forward to everyone's continued support in 1998. Colin Kidner.

22. Sailing Secretary's Report 1997 Season This season has again been less than ideal from the weather viewpoint, with 14 events being lost from the regular Points Series schedule of 44 races due to wind conditions. 67 boats participated in the 30 events sailed in these Series, down on last years 81. The largest fleets were the Dart 15 with 18 competitors, but all fleets had reduced numbers compared to last year except the Solos who repeated last year's 17. The weather did bless our chosen Open Day with sunshine and a blissful force 3 which enabled us to provide enjoyable sailing experiences to a large number of visitors to our Club, some of whom are now members. Many thanks to the substantial number of members who made themselves and their boats available for that event. An informal racing series for cruisers was organised successfully this year by Mike Turner, and it is hoped that this can be built on next year in order to promote competitive sailing in the cruiser fleet. Successful Open Meetings for D15 and Solo Classes were hosted by the Club this year with entries for both in the 20s, and the East Coast Piers Race was blessed by good weather and an entry in the high 70s. This event continues to attract the best crews from Europe and the UK, and greatly adds to the Club's reputation. Although it is mainly Fast Cats from the Club who enter, the event could not be held without the enthusiastic backing of the Cruiser Fleet and the other dinghy fleets. Thanks to all who took part. Members competing elsewhere have again put the name of Marconi S.C. on the map, starting back in Dec 96 with JoJo Anderson's outstanding 4th place in the Cadet World's in Bombay. Our 6 boat entry at the Hurricane Nationals won the Team Trophy for the Club, and Mick Jones and Andy Sharp are the Prindle European Champions. Nearer to home, Paul Metcalfe and Steve Glynn finished 2nd and 3rd respectively, in the BJRC Cock of the River Series. I would like to take this opportunity to offer my personal thanks to the Race Officers and Assistants whose efforts this season have made my job both easy and enjoyable. I must mention particularly John Weedon's contribution in running the Wednesday Evening Series which remains a popular feature of our racing programme. Thanks also to all who helped crew the rescue boats. Your Sailing Sub Committee, under Clive Shenton's able leadership, strives to provide you with the best sailing programme that we can, but it is not always easy to know what to aim for. Please tell us through your Fleet Captains, or directly to me, how you want your sailing to be in the future. Finally, I would like to end on a very positive note, with the observation that this season has seen the emergence of growing numbers of new cadets into our sailing programme. Let us give them every help and encouragement, for the future health of our Club lies in their hands. John Salmon

Cruiser Comments As this is being written for the December issue of Navigans, I expect by the time you read this, many things will have happened, namely both the Cruiser Fleet and Club AGM’s, the Club Laying Up Supper and Cruiser Working Party, all of which I hope were well attended. In addition of course there are the Mooring Parties. Hopefully the Cruisers will by now be safely ashore, I must say October went out more like a raging bull than a lion or lamb. Sadly some boats did go astray, one receiving substantial damage, fortunately above the water line. Juno took herself over to Rolls Farm on the north bank and even though she is a fin keeler I am delighted to report Peter Cullen was able to float her off without any apparent damage. Clearly I am unable to comment on what caused these boats to slip their moorings but it does highlight the necessity to ensure your moorings are adequate for all conditions. Better safe than sorry, don’t’ use the bare essential, go one stage further. The task of getting rid of old cruiser trailers continues, however may I draw your attention to the fact that in future it will be the owners responsibility to remove unwanted trailers from the site. You will have noticed there is now an annual charge of £25 for trailers not being used for winter storage of boats. So if you have a trailer on site and you choose to winter your boat elsewhere you will have to pay to store your trailer. I have received from Essex Police a notice which has been displayed in the Clubhouse stating “REMEMBER VESSELS LAID UP ASHORE FOR THE WINTER ARE VUNERABLE TO THEFT REMOVE ALL EQUIPMENT AS SOON AS POSSIBLE” need I say more? and please don’t forget to lock your ladders and shut the gate. On the question of ladders, it is a practice of mine when walking around the Cruiser Park to remove any ladders that are not secure and place them in the Cruiser Garage, so if you’ve lost one look in there but we will not store it for long. May I close on a more nautical note. In case you have not seen it in the yachting press this was reported in the August edition of “Sailing Today” “The Holland Decca Chain ‘D’ Purple Slave Station at Thorpness in the UK (52 11°N 01 36’E) is to close at 2359 on July 31 this year. This means you will no longer be able to get Decca fixes in the Southern part of the North Sea using the Purple and Green Slave Stations. The *C’ Green Slave is located at Sas van Gent (51 13°N 02 52’E), the ‘B’ Red Slave at Heiloo (52 35’N 04 45’E) and the Master at Gilze-Rijen (51 37°N 04 56E) Special care should be taken when sailing in the vicinity of any base line extension areas, Transmissions from the remaining Decca stations in the Holland Chain 2E, covering the Central part of the North Sea and the Frisian Islands (Chain 9B), will continue until 2359 on December 31 1999” What with the phasing out of Decca and the millennium Bug and its possible effects on GPS systems, I guess it will be back to basics soon! What on earth did I do with my Protractor, Compass, Parallel Ruler etc.? To close off the year, may I and Doreen wish you all a Very Merry Christmas and all the Very Best For the New Year. Derek Kirby Cruiser Fleet Captain. Attention all GPS Users. First the good news, GPS Systems do not have a Year 2000 problem. Now the bad news, some may have a 21st August 1999 problem! The following information was received over the Internet. A US Air Force worker noticed that there was no mention of any field in any GPS message to tell him which 1024 week cycle he was in. Guess when week 1025 arrives? Yes 21st August 1999. The Air Force worker contacted GPS Companies in the OSC, some of whom were aware of the problem, some were not. Apparently manufacturers who were aware of the problem kept quiet in the hope of putting some of their rivals out of business. This will be of scant comfort to our cruisers returning from Holland on 22nd August next year. Perhaps a check with your GPS manufacturer might be a good idea. One last piece of advice from our helpful American friend - don’t travel on 22nd August 1999, (unless you have a sextant with you). (For computer Nerds - check out http://www. yachtingnet.com/forums/power/|. html.) Happy sailing Keith Starkey.

E 3 “a Helm of the Year \ | lf E : cc \ , / ; seenErre rv a, Ad b 3 - f \ H ene Zen bee E «aoe : 3 10th October 1998 rf a | | | | a ~ Navigans sent their roving reporter to Stansgate to cover the contest for this the premier sailing title in the club’s calendar, and what a sensational contest it turned out to be, with the championship only settled in the last race of a closely contested 5 race series. Sailed in Toppers in an almost ideal force 4 breeze, the event was contested between the top helms from each of the regular sailing fleets, determined from the summed results of spring and summer points series. Only Jenny Ball from the Dart 15 fleet was absent from the first choice qualifiers, so the five contestants were Roger Smith (Solo), Steve Monks (Handicap), Jon Yorston Medium Cat), Tim Wallace (Fast Cat), and Peter Tovey (Dart 15). To ensure a fair contest the boats were rotated between the competitors such that all sailed one race in each boat. One result discard was allowed. The event was staged using committee boat starts on short courses around M and D marks, so the clubhouse, sea wall and the hard provided excellent grandstands for the enthusiastic followers. Race 1. Tim, the defending champion, got the jump on his competitors from the start and held them off determinedly to the finish line, thus demonstrating that he was not about to give up his title easily. Steve, showing good boat speed, and benefiting from capsizes of his competitors worked his way through to second. Race 2. Tim’s turn for swimming practice which allowed Steve to steal away for a win from Roger and an improving Peter. Race 3. Steve’s speed and steady boat handling recorded another win, this time chased to the line by Roger and Jon. Tim had the bad luck to be forced into retirement, when well placed, by his outhaul letting go. Race 4. All competitors were getting the hang of the Toppers and competing really hard right from the gun. Tim once again charged his way to the front from Peter with Roger forcing Steve down to fourth. Race 5. Steve and Tim started the last race with two wins each under their belts and everything to play for. Understandably they were keeping a close eye on each other, but this allowed Roger, who had been improving his boat speed throughout the series, to break away for a convincing win. Steve kept Tim at bay all the way to the finish line thus clinching the series. All competitors deserve credit for a keenly contested series in a good spirit. Commodores Notes It is less than three weeks since I was elected to serve as your Commodore and I appear to have been busy. In addition to the normal Executive and Main Committee I have attended the Cruiser Fleet AGM, the BACSPA AGM and the Sailing Sub Committee to hand over to Jenny, our new Rear Commodore. Someone told me that Rear Commodore was the hard job and Commodore was a rest cure, I don't know who it was, but it could have been Colin Kidner. Thanks Colin. My overwhelming impression having attended the Cruiser Fleet AGM was one of awe. You are so well organised all the other Fleets could learn a thing or two. The attendance was more than most Clubs can assemble at their Main AGM. The planning of the Cruiser working party was so detailed it could have been for D-day. All presided over by Derek Kirby with an air of determined authority. I have been very pleased with the level of enthusiasm that is evident within the Club. Neil Pembleton immediately accepted my offer to co-opt him back onto the Main Committee and John Salmon quickly agreed to serve in his old position as Hon. Sailing Secretary. Mick Richardson, Lee Harrison and Rob Davies all volunteered to be co-opted onto the Main Committee and all these appointments have been ratified by the Committee. That's not the end of the volunteers. Laura Gill, Hillary Ashley and Clare Davies will form an Entertainment’s sub Committee to develop that side of our activities, while Steve Glynn will continue to run the Laying Up Supper. My thanks to you all. Phil Longhurst, with the help of Tim dieu de Bellefontaine and Lee Harrison have organised a Winter Series this year. We have had three races so far, each with near perfect conditions. Alex and myself have entered the series and we can both attest to the warm properties of the new(and matching) dry suits that were necessary. Thanks lads - I think! Now two key roles in running the Club remain unfilled, those of Rescue Boat Co-ordinator and Club House Secretary. Mick Richardson has kindly offered to extend his five year tenure of the latter job until a volunteer comes forward. If you would like to serve the Club in either role please phone me on [redacted] for more details. At Main Committee we decided to hold the AGM and Prize Giving in the Conference Room at MASC in Chelmsford next year. So bringing to an end the fun of the scrum at the back of the upper saloon. The Year Book will have the details. It is the night time of year for New Year's Resolutions. Here is a suggestion for the whole Club - Resolve to enjoy your sailing next season. I resolve to sail more both at the Club and elsewhere. We intend to do the ECPR of course, plus the Nore and Forts Races. Also with a bit of encouragement we might be persuaded to try Texel. So how about it? My best wishes for Fair winds and warm seas in 1999. Clive Shenton View From The Rear Same article heading (I hate to break with tradition!) - but, in case you are not already aware, I am your new Rear Commodore and I look forward to another busy and successful year for Marconi Sailing Club. Thanks must go to all those people who have continued to hold positions on our several committees and to those who have taken on new positions for 1999. Your efforts are much appreciated. Rescue Co-ordination One key area is the organisation of the rescue boat rota’s for 1999. Laura Gill is standing down as Rescue Boat Co-ordinator, having worked very hard to provide support crews each weekend in 1998, therefore this position is currently vacant. The Sailing Sub Committee is currently taking a serious look at how to support this and make the co-ordinator’s job less arduous. For example, if volunteers are forthcoming, we could divide the position up so that one person covering spring points, one for summer and one for the autumn series. Your fleet captains will be discussing this at your AGM’s - if you can help or have any ideas, please let them know or contact myself.

Ladies Race Ladies will be pleased to know that we have re-instated the three race series for the Ladies Race in 1999. It has been suggested that his is raced in one type of boat (e.g. Topper, Picos) to even out the wide spread boats we have. The Helmsman of the Year is organised in this way. I would welcome your thoughts on this so that we can make the necessary arrangements. Finally, Marconi will again have an entry in the RNLI Rowing Race on New Year’s Day. We always welcome supporters and it is a good way to blow the Christmas cobwebs away!!! Which leads me on to wish you all a Merry Christmas and a successful laying up/fitting out! Salt in my mouth, There was a young reindeer from Surrey, Spray racing right in. Capsize! Who cooked up a large pot of curry, Fall in. Swim. Right the boat. CRUISER COMMENTS On Thursday 19 November we held our Fleet AGM. which was attended by 68 members representing 46 cruisers. We were pleased to welcome Paul Harris from Maldon Little Ship Club and John Titchmarsh from Maritime & Leisure also our new Commodore Clive Shenton and Rear Commodore Jenny Ball. The meeting opened with a vote of thanks from Neil Pembleton for the support given to him by members present in his bid to become Commodore, however with the election of Clive Shenton he pledged his support to the new Commodore and urged any members who had voted for him to do the same. Clive Shenton responded by revealing he had asked Neil to be co-opted onto the main committee which he agreed to. Both expressed their desire to achieve greater cohesion between the various fleets within the club. A review of the 1998 sailing season commenced with the visitors presenting Frank Burgess with the BLACKWATER MARINE CHALLENGE CUP which he won sailing “Ocean Slipper”, after which Messrs Harris & Titchmarsh left the meeting. The season got underway with our traditional “Fitting Out Supper” held at Stansgate using outside caterers. This was a great success and a similar event is scheduled for Saturday 24 April 1998. Watch Navigans for further details. Burnham has become a regular venue for our “shakedown cruise” 14 cruisers attended with 39 members sitting down to an excellent meal at the Royal Corinthian Yacht Club. The late Summer Bank Holiday cruise at Shotley attracted 26 Cruisers with 60 members sitting down to eat in the “Stour Suite” of the Shipwreck public house. Whilst some members had to return home on the Monday, 14 cruisers went onto the River Deben stopping off at the “The Tidemill” for an enjoyable Bar B Q. The support given by the cruisers at the East Coast Piers Race had been greatly appreciated, it is understood that approximately £5,000 had been donated to the Cirdan Trust. The club had been host to members of the R.N.S.A. who joined us for a Bar B Q and drinks in the Dell Bar. Two club trophies were presented, the first being the “BARNACLE TROPHY” won by Nick Bevins sailing “Gabelle” as overall winner of the clubs series of cruiser races. The now infamous “BIG COCK TROPHY” or is it “cock up trophy” was contested by seven members with the ultimate winner winning hands down. The winner was present to graciously receive this trophy but in accordance with established protocol only those members present at the A.G.M. know the recipient, next year it could be you!!! The winter lay up was discussed and it was acknowledged some craft were short of space. This is sometimes caused by members changing boats, however, I am aware of the situation and it is hoped more space may be made available by this years working party for next year. The introduction of £25.00 annual fee for trailers not being used for storing boats was explained, it was also noted there was a shortage of pallets for moorings due to some being used for bonfires during camping week. Tony Holbrook said he would try to obtain some more. Proposals for the December working party were discussed and where possible team leaders were identified with associated helpers so that when members arrived they knew what to do and what tools to bring. Maureen Ball was going to provide hot soup and french bread and asked if any ladies present would help her in this and also cleaning up of the clubhouse. The election of both Fleet Captain and Vice Captain took place and since there were no other contenders for the job both Derek Kirby and Malcolm Yeoman were elected respectively. Paint Orders - Malcolm and Helen Shaft have performed this onerous but much appreciated task for nine years but now felt they could no longer carry on. Gordon Preston agreed to take it on having first been briefed by Malcolm on the system he had successfully built over the years. At present Boatacs in Southend give a 33 percent discount which may be difficult to better. Chain and Shackles - Don Holdsworth still has plenty of *4” chain at £2.00 per foot. There had been problems with boat anodes which is still under investigation. Don stressed members should not leave their orders till the last minute, to do so may cause disappointment. Rod Hillman said he could obtain mooring anchors at a cost of £65.00 each providing he could make up an order of at least 12. A sample is in the garage and can be viewed by arrangement with Don. Proposals for 1999 Sailing Season Burnham 29/30/31 May Shakedown Cruise Evening meal on 30" at Royal Corinthian Yacht Club. Shotley 28/29/30 August Evening meal on the 29" in the Stour Suite of Shipwreck Pub. Apart from the fact that the above are popular venues, it was also stressed that there are few venues that can cater for the number of cruiser/members attending these events, we are so to speak victims of our own success. Long may it be so and thanks for your support.

London 31° July to 8” August. Single handed cruisers are planning a weeks cruise, stopping over at Queenborough. Contact Pat Black for further details. All welcome. 11/12 September Visit by East Coast Unit of R.N.S.A. It is also hoped that we will be host to competitors in the Walton RNLI Endurance event also the Tollesbury Mud Club. Racing In the absence of Mike Turner and Derek Gardner both being away on business, Frank Burgess outlined the merits of the BJRC fixtures and urged members to support some if not all of these races. The Blackwater Sailing Club will be 100 years old and centenary races will be held to celebrate this, watch Navigans for details. It is planned to run a series of 4 short races early in the season plus chases within the clubs flotilla cruises. Again watch Navigans for details. An update on the Travel Hoist, Power Winch and Mooring Barge/Trailer was given by Peter Clayton. The Travel Hoist was running late due to certain design problems which unfortunately delayed using it for this year’s haul out, however, it was hoped these will be resolved in time for its introduction at the end of next years sailing season. Introduction of the travel hoist will be gradual as members trailers become unserviceable, those with perfectly good trailers will be expected to carry on using them until they become unusable/unsafe. Eric Lawley expressed concern over the commissioning of the Travel Hoist, however, after a lively debate the matter was resolved and Neil Pembleton proposed a motion that the meeting give a vote of confidence regarding the purchase and introduction of the Travel Hoist which was carried overwhelmingly. Malcolm Stuart expressed his gratitude that there were members within the club willing to sacrifice time and effort in the interests of Health and Safety for the benefit of members, AOB - Geoff Baker suggested in the interests of Safety the OOD should carry a portable radio - Derek Kirby said he would take this up at the next Sailing Committee Sub-Meeting. Pat Black is arranging a block booking for the Earls Court Boat Show which would give members a cheaper entry. Forms available from Pat Black, contact him direct. Ray Ball made a collection towards the RNLI rowing race due to be held at Maldon. Members were advised Murray Bates will have new club burgees available at the March 18 Cruiser Fleet Meeting. so come on, lets fly the flag, start saving. After what proved to be a rather long meeting albeit many topics were discussed. The meeting finally closed at 22.25, with the Commodore proposing a vote of thanks to the chairman, i.e. yours truly - thanks. The first of our New Years winter meetings will be held at MASC on Thursday 21 January, our guest speaker being that well known local yachtsman Charles Stock. Charles has now clocked up some 60,000 miles in his green gaff cutter “Shoal Waters”. We meet at 1930 for a 2000 hours start. I am also delighted to announce our speaker on 18 February will be Lynn Guy who will be talking about her experiences whilst aboard “Ocean Rover” during the Whitbread Round the World Yacht Race. Derek Kirby - Cruiser Fleet Captain. COMMODORES NOTES Some of you may have heard about the happenings of Sunday 3 January. The forecast was 6-7 from the SW and Tim Bellefontaine phoned around early to cancel the Winter Series Race. However such wind is meet and drink to the boardsailors and several were out for a New Year adrenaline rush. But the forecast was wrong, the wind did a 90 degree swing to the north and increased to storm force. Several boardsailors got into difficulties and a club member, very properly, called the Coastguard. As several other Clubs had not cancelled their racing, the Mersea RNLI were too busy to attend. This led to one of our members being airlifted by RAF helicopter, back to the Club, after he had taken shelter on Osea. Several other boarders made it back to the Club under their own power and another was picked up by a passing yacht. Fortunately no one was hurt, but the incident does underline the uncertainty of the weather and what an alien environment the sea can be to we land based creatures. Also it shows that the Emergency Services are worth every penny that we put in collecting tins or pay in taxes. Speaking of collecting tins, the RNLI rowing race took place on New Year's Day at Maldon. The weather was excellent and there appeared to be at least forty starters, including the "Yellow Brick Road Crew" from our Club. I thought the Cowardly Lion crew member had a passing resemblance to a Flag Officer, but I could be wrong. The many spectators along the shore had an entertaining morning and I saw many Club Members taking the air and working upa thirst. Will there be a Cat Entry next year? Watch this space! It now seems right to mention that we have three volunteers who will divide the duties of Rescue Boat co-ordinator. They are Barry Hut, Tony Ferguson and Dennis Gilbey. Thank you Gentlemen. The Sailing sub Committee intend to give some thought to methods of making the job easier to administer and implement. Having done the job for a year myself, I can say that every member who is scheduled for a duty could be very helpful to the co-ordinators by turning out willingly, or failing that reliably. Most are reliable and willing but the odd "rogue" makes life very stressful for the co-ordinator. Colin Kidner has volunteered to undertake a newly created role on the Main Committee, that of Safety Co-ordinator. The RYA tell us that some aspects of Health and Safety Legislation are increasingly being applied to Clubs such as our own. Colin will ensure that we formalise our working practices throughout the Club so that we do not fall foul of the Law. He has already enlisted the help of Malcolm Robertson and formed a Safety Committee. This is a complicated and detailed business and I hope to persuade Colin to do a piece for Navigans to tell us more. The Cruiser Fleet achieved great things at their Working Party in December. The Vice Commodore, Peter Bloomfield, now intends to contact other Fleet Captains to encourage them to emulate the efforts of their fellow members. Please give your Fleet Captain your full co-operation so that all the non-sailing tasks can be completed before the New Sailing Season starts in March. See you all at the Barn Dance on the 30" January Clive Shenton VIEW FROM THE REAR Happy New Year!! RNLI Rowing Race A large crowd of Marconi supporters turned out to watch the annual RNLI Rowing Race at Maldon Little Ship Club, despite the early start on New Year’s Day! The weather was very kind encouraging a large turnout of both spectators and competitors who took to the water in all kinds of craft and costumes. The Marconi entry (Clare and Sarah Davis, Jenny and David Ball) were thrwarted by gear failure and were only able to complete half the course. However, we did manage to collect a prize for our fancy dress as characters from the Wizard of Oz. The event raised over £8,000 for the RNLI - a particularly worthy cause in the light of local events caused by adverse weather at the start of the month. Thank you to all who gave us their support. Very sensibly, the organisers have now decided not to schedule the event for New Year's Day next year - so the next RNLI Rowing Race will be held on Boxing Day 1999 - put it in your diaries! Happy fitting out to you all! Jenny Ball Rear Commodore

CRUISER COMMENTS Firstly welcome to the New Year. I hope you had an enjoyable Christmas and New Year Celebration and are no doubt looking forward to this years sailing season. As you know this years winter meetings commence on Thursday 21 January with a talk by Charles Stock followed by another on Thursday 18 February when the speaker will be Lynn Guy. Lynn will be talking about her experiences whilst sailing in the Whitbread Round the World Race on board “Ocean Rover”, both meetings are at 1930 for a prompt 2000 hours start. Last months “Cruiser Comments” were rather long due to reporting the minutes of the Cruiser AGM so I will keep this edition short but there are a couple of matters I would like to mention. First may | thank all those who attended the working party at MSC. It was a splendid turnout and much needed work was successfully undertaken, especially the ditch infill which hopefully we will be able to use next year for winter storage, thus hopefully reducing the wear and tear on the “Cat Field”. Whilst on that subject. may I request those members who have boats wintered in that area, to drive their cars along the hedge on the south side of the field i.e. crossing the ditch immediately on the right after entering the main gate. This will save cutting up the field between the stored catamarans especially whilst the weather is so wet. Thank you. My second matter is addressed to those of you whose vessels are PART 1 Registered as is “Happy Medium” I wrote to the Maritime and Coastguard Agency who replied by saying:- 1. Are you registered on the UK mainland? If yes 2. Does your current certificate show an expiry date? a) If-yes is the expiry date 20 March 1999? If so contact RSS as soon as possible. b) Ifnoi.e. you hold an A4 size laminated certificate with an expiry date after 20 March 1999 you are not affected; you get a renewal notice sent to your last registered address. 3. Is the year of build shown on your certificate before 1950? a) Ifyes, you are affected now and should contact the registry to get a renewal form as soon as possible. b) If no you are not affected now but will be affected in the next 5 years. The timetable below shows when you must apply. Year of build Dates for renewal Before 1950 11 Jan - 31 Mar 1999 1950 - 1970 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2000 1971- 1975 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2001 1976- 1989 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2002 1990 - 20 March 1994 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2003 Year of build unknown Apply as soon as possible N.B. If you have more than one date shown as the year of build you should use the earlier date. Lastly, would the cruiser owner who borrowed a 10 stud wheel from the clubs stock, please return it, as it is required for the travel hoist. Having said I would keep it short, I still seem to have taken up lots of space, still I hope it will be of use to someone. Cheers! Derek Kirby Cruiser Fleet Captain. PLEASE KEEP OFF THE GRASS Please DO NOT drive on the grass during the winter months. With all the wet conditions we have experienced recently the ground is very soft. If you have visited the club recently you will have noticed that deep troughs, caused by vehicles are appearing in the grass and are filling with water. If we continue to drive on the grass it will take a lot of time and effort to return it to its original condition - please use the roads where possible. - Unless absolutely necessary.

You may think it’s all a bit crazy sailing in the winter, but to date the organisers and sailors involved in Marconi’s latest sailing venture have had nothing but almost ideal sailing conditions. We are now almost half way through the series, which consists of one race every fortnight. This format was chosen not because cat sailors are lazy but to give people the chance to still catch up with all those jobs which get put off due to the busy summer sailing calendar. So far in the sailing there is no clear leader, and to date the sailing has all been very close, with results being just seconds apart after a whole hours sailing. So isn’t it a bit cold? Well, so far due to the favourable wind conditions. Once out on the water the sailors have been active enough not to feel the cold. Which if you're brave enough to remove the ice from the boat cover, gladly only experienced once so far, is a nice pleasant surprise. So if you're looking for something to do on the coming winter Sundays, why not come and give your support, even if it is just from the club house, which we endeavour to keep nice and warm. We even have a selection of hot food and drinks available, so why not join us for breakfast. Also if you are a fast cat sailor who wants to join us or a fleet captain who thinks that their fleet would be interested in running a similar series then just give me a ring on [redacted]. Commodores Notes The big news this month was the demerger of Marconi from GEC and the subsequent acquisition by British Aerospace, although those in the know tell me that it is not as simple as that. I assure you that the Main Committee will keep in close touch with developments and be ready for any eventualities. Ardent readers of this part of Navigans will remember that last month I said that our taxes were being well spent on Rescue helicopters. Well, we must have a taxman reader, because three days later I got a bill for several thousand that it is alleged that I owe in unpaid taxes. I will leave the reader to decide on the moral of the story. With not too much happening on the sailing front, it was the Barn Dance that was centre stage this month. All tickets were sold, the band was good and the place was jumping, literally in many dances. The band seemed to have added to the repertoire since we last heard them two years ago. The Black Sabbath/Status Quo/Brian May riffs were unexpected in a square dance, but welcome all the same. Well done Neil and the Entertainment's team, I understand that plans are underway for next year already. Speaking of Entertainment's, Claire Davies told the Committee on Monday, of the delights she has planned for us during the year. A Fitting Out Supper, Quiz night and several other events are in the pipeline. On Monday our discussions once more turned to how we can improve the ambience of the Upper Saloon, especially for the non sailing members. There is a need to avoid major expenditure and so conserve our reserves at present, however we cannot neglect the service we give our members and there is a feeling that "Something must be done". My thoughts extend to a suspended ceiling with concealed lighting, a resurfaced floor and some curtains. If any member has expertise in interior design I would welcome some professional, but unfortunately unpaid, advice. Advice from gifted amateurs and indeed any member with an opinion would also be welcome. I would also like some feedback on the Main Committee Minutes that we publish in Navigans each month. Pat Black does a comprehensive job which runs to several pages. The monthly printing costs for the extra sheets are considerable. Are the minutes useful? Do you read them? Would a shorter edited version be as good? I would like your opinion please. A good method to contact me is by email on [redacted] or just grab me when you see me at the Club. The nights are shortening already and the Spring will be with us before you know it, so start your plans for 99 now. Good Sailing. Clive Shenton View from the Rear Time for the March Navigans already - (where does the time go!) - and the focus is very much on getting ready for the sailing season again. With preparations for the 1999 sailing season already underway, | would like to encourage you all to continue your support for these activities. A number of working parties will be organised by your fleet captains to carry out some maintenance work on the grounds and thc club house. Please try and support your fleet captains in whatever way you can to ensure these are a success! The rosters for support boats and other duties are being compiled and published in Navigans. Please check the lists for your name and ensure that you swap in plenty of time if you cannot attend a duty for any reason. We are all grateful to those who give up their weekends / Wednesday evenings to man the support boats / race box and we each need to do our bit when the time arises! It is also good to see that a number of cadet activities, (winter meetings, bank holiday weekends), are being organised - further information can be found on the Cadet page or in the letter sent to all Cadets. We look forward to the continuing activities of our Cadet Fleet -(so long as they don’t start beating us older people on the water!). Happy fitting out! Jenny Ball Rear Commodore [redacted]

CRUISER COMMENTS Our January meeting was very well attended, it was especially great to see members of our dinghy fleets, who, like the rest of us enjoyed the talk given by Charles Stock on the subject of the rivers, Ore, Butley and the entrances to Southwold (hairy), Lowestoft and Great Yarmouth, taking us into Breydon Water and the river Bure. Not only is he an interesting and witty speaker; his wife Joy wields a nifty camera, sometimes under difficult circumstances. Those who have their boats in the “Cat Field” will by now have realised my mistake in requesting them to enter the field at the southern end. At the time of writing I did not realise a barrier had been placed there! However, with the excellent work done on filling the ditch, access is now possible by using the road through the Cruiser Park and entering at the eastern entrance. You don’t need me to tell you the grounds are a quagmire and it does not take much to cut up and rut, so please do take care. At the last meeting it was mentioned that Geof Baker (Bosham Dreamer) is able to arrange a block booking with Sail Spar for those members wishing to have their standing rigging tested. If you are interested please contact him direct - [redacted]. Followers of the deliberation regarding the future of VHF may have noted that the International Maritime Organisation have agreed the ships should keep a radio-listening watch on VHF CH16 until February 2005. Ships were due to cease keeping watch on this channel in February 1999 as developments in GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress & Safety System) took over. But, recognising few yachts will be equipped with GMDSS the IMO has made listening mandatory for member nation vessels whilst at sea. I would mention it is everyones responsibility to maintain a listening watch on VHF 16 which of course is the distress, as well as the calling frequency. BOAT JUMBLES are due to be held at Chatham on Sunday 14" February and Great Leighs on Sunday 7" March. There is also the Tollesbury Easter Boat Show due to be held between Friday 2" and Monday 5" April from 10.00am to 5.00pm. Vice Commodore Peter Bloomfield attended the last Sailing Sub Committee Meeting where he requested each of the fleets to take on various tasks at their next working parties. Obviously we would like to get ours out of the way quickly so we can get on with our boats and moorings, therefore, it was decided to hold our working party on Sunday 21“ February commencing at 10.00 hrs. The jobs to be undertaken as as follows:- DIESEL FUEL STORE: remove hard core to far end of cruiser park. CRUISER PARK: check, test & service security lights. TRACTOR SHED ROOF: inspect roofing felt & make good as required. CLUB HOUSE PATIO: window shutters, rub down & re-coat with preservative. Our next Cruiser Meeting is on Thursday 18 February when Lynn Guy will be talking about her experiences whilst sailing aboard “Ocean Rover” during the Whitbread Round The World Race. This then leaves the last of our current series of winter meetings which will be held on Thursday 18" March and I believe John Todd “CHIMO” is preparing a most interesting talk with slides, it is also hoped to run through the events that have been organised for this years sailing season. Lastly, may I on behalf of Doreen and myself thank those of you who clubbed together to present us with a treasured nautical gift. Derek Kirby - Cruiser Fleet Captain. Cadet Week 1999 We are heading fast toward the middle of the year and that moment I know you have all been waiting for. Please find the entry form for Cadet Week and it will help us a lot if you can let me have it back as soon as possible, helpers, parents and or cadets. What More! As you have also been reading there are many new initiatives we are trying to line up which depend on your support. There are shore-side training sessions being set up by Jenny and Bradwell based RYA training weeks to get your books signed up for the higher levels. There are setting-up weekends for rigging boats and subject to weather conditions some early training afloat and/or ashore. So get painting and polishing-up those bits of plastic. There will also be disco/bop sessions to help get the circulation going. So make sure you keep your eyes skinned and fill in any other forms floating past your eyes. The Box, Cadet Box, The Locker, The Heads, The Poop, The Gundeck, Crowsnest Whatever it is to be called it is in the capable hands of Steve Glynn. We need more names as the above may not all be eligible for your new cadet room, to be erected next to the Reception Hut. I am afraid that most things enjoyed by kids but provided by adults, it will have to have some simple rules and regs attached to its use. I quite like the idea of re-instating flogging should any be broken or even keel hauling but as sharks are not found in the Blackwater, half the fun is missing.

Commodores Notes I will start this month by mentioning subscriptions. If you have yet to send your Marconi Sailing Club (MSC) dues, then you should do so as quickly as possible. I have had one or two calls from members who have not yet renewed MSC because of some irregularities with MASC numbers on the MSC form. If your MSC renewal form does not have your MASC number then add the right number, if you know it, and send in your subscription to Linda Chaplin. If you do not know the number still send in your money. There have been one or two difficulties this year, but Frank Bennett is putting in a lot of time with MASC to solve outstanding problems, but he cannot start the process until you send in your renewal. You should see elsewhere in this issue that the application for Camping Fortnight is included. Hilary Ashley is again dealing with this hot potato. We believe you will like to get your summer holiday arrangements finalised earlier than in previous years, hence the appearance of the form at this time. The Main Committee have approved some increases in the rates but they still represent very good value for money, so no complaints please. Last month I asked for some unpaid help from an interior designer, and Chris Hutt has kindly offered her services to put some original thought into the Upper Saloon regeneration. My thanks also go to two members who emailed some ideas about this matter. An idea gaining in strength is that the Upper Saloon becomes a dry bar with a wet bar at ground floor. I would be pleased to hear your views on [redacted] or on [redacted]. I ask all respondents to remember that we have very little money available to carry out your ideas, BUT I do want feedback please. I also got two messages that the publishing of the Minutes is appreciated. So I will attempt to save a bit of space by changing the font, and continue to include them in Navigans. As | am writing this, there is only one Winter Series race left to run, and the winner of the fine new trophy made by Tim Wallace, will be in doubt until the result of the last race is known. The efforts of Tim Bellefontaine and Phil Longhurst have been rewarded by a successful and enjoyable event with 9 entries. Same again next year? While on the subject of Winter racing, the catering was undertaken by Ted Mona. | am pleased to tell you that we have done the deal for him to continue throughout the year. The service will start on 21" March but will not be available on 28 March. Thereafter catering will be available each Sunday and Bank Holiday Monday until the end of the season. Remember, they are there to give us the service we need. If you want a change of menu, make a polite request to them, and they will try to oblige. Peter Bloomfield is very pleased with the response from the Class captains to his allocation of tasks. Thanks to everyone who has done his or her bit to get the Club ready for the new season, which is just around the corner. These efforts help us to keep our subscriptions down. Thanks. I look forward to seeing you out on the water in 99. Clive Shenton USE OF THE SKIP VERY IMPORTANT Please note that the HALES skip at the club may only contain low density, non hazardous waste. The contents are removed by a bulk crusher lorry and loads which may cause damage to the crusher are rejected by the operator, resulting in unnecessary cost to the club and unpleasant work for members, to remove the offending materials. Despite this reminder appearing in previous Navigans.... SOMEONE ....... still managed to put bricks and a 7REE in there. PLEASE - THIS IS FOR DOMESTIC RUBBISH ONLY. Should you see any of the above - a gentle reminder to those concerned wouldn’t go a miss. We cannot afford to lose such a facility.

CRUISER COMMENTS. Those of you who attended last months Cruiser Meeting at MASC could not help but admire the courage and tenacity of Lynn Guy who related to us her experiences, high and low, whilst racing around the world on board ‘Ocean Rover’. As always 1 was encouraged to see so many, 70+ including members fron the Solo Fleet, nice to see you. Derek Gardiner, Frank Burgess and Mike Turner have been working hard to organise a racing programme covering ‘chases’ within the flotilla cruises also a series of domestic ‘buoy’ type events plus details of the ‘BJRC Cruiser Races’. (See page 9 for details). As usual a ‘launching list’ will be displayed on the cruiser notice board, please make sure you indicate on this when you propose to launch, making sure you have first made arrangements with a tractor driver. My thanks to those who attended what | hope will be the last of this winters working parties, most of the tasks were completed, there is still the Dell Bar shutters to be done but I guess |’ll get down to that some time during a weekday. For those of you who are interested, the mast derrick will be erected on Saturday 27“ March when we are also due to launch the ‘Jack B’ workboat and mooring barge. Details of this, together with mooring information will be published in this years ‘Information Booklet for Cruiser Owners’. I expect those of you who ordered paint through Gordon Preston will by now have taken delivery therefore on your behalf 1 would like to thank Gordon and no doubt Cynthia for all their hard work on our behalf. I also noticed Don and Barbara Holdsworth have returned from their visit to Australia refreshed and bronzed ready to take on the task of issueing chain. shackles and annodes. Please don’t leave it to the last minute, if you require any, contact Don now on [redacted] Last but not least we will be holding the Cruiser Fitting Out Supper at MSC Stansgate on Saturday 24" April. Space is limited, we can only seat 60 members. If you were unable to attend the Cruiser meeting on the 18“ March when details were circulated, please contact me for further details. Derek Kirby Cruiser Fleet Captain. “THANK YOU FROM DOWN UNDER” Margaret's hospitalisation on day two of our visit to Sydney was a great shock to the family and to many of our friends. We learn’t she had suffered a heart attack which resulted in her having a triple by pass op eight days later. She is now recovering slowly but surely and all credit must be given to the Australian Health System for their prompt and pofessional action which effectively saved her life. The cards and letters bearing kind thoughts and good wishes from our friends at MSC were a great comfort to us both and we thank you all most sincerely. The card signed by many including the guest speaker at the February Cruiser Fleet Meeting was especially well received. Again many thanks to vou all, Margaret and Malcolm Yeoman (SURUCA) 1999 DINGHY PARK (Monohull). Please see the plan on page 4 of the dinghy park for 1999. As reported previously | have made a few extra 2.5m wide spaces in tow B; Bl, B2: B3: and B4 to be precise. Please only use these spaces, and A rows, if your boat is 1.7m beam or greater. This means Wayfarers. Wanderers, Osprey. 505 and the “One offs’. It does not include Kestrels. Enterprises. GPs, 470s. Tideways or Fireballs. Please call me if you have any queries. As before 1 will put lists on the notice board for you to fill in your name etc. In addition | will put small pegs with the berth number on the back of the bay to help you identify it. They will be small so it may be hidden in the grass! As before it will be first come. first served. Solos in S row, A row for the boats wider than 1.7m, C & D rows for Mirrors. Toppers and Lasers etc. Other handicap boats please use B row (except for B1-4) and E row. Again. please call if you have any questions. Roger Smith [redacted] E-mail: [redacted]

Marconi Sailing Club Minutes of the Main Committee Meeting held on the ist February 1999 at the MASC Present C Shenton(Commodore & Chairman), R Greygoose(President MSC), P Bloomfield(Vice Commodore), Jenny Ball(Rear Commodore), F Bennett (Honorary Treasurer), P Black(Honorary Secretary), S Glynn(Vice President), P Clayton(Vice President), N Pembleton, M Richardson, D Kirby, R Godbold(Bar Manager), B Dowley(Navigans Editor), M Bates, M Smith, L Chaplin(Registrar), L Harrison, E Cockerton, C Davies, R Davies Executive Meeting Clive Shenton welcomed Mrs B DowleY and R Davis to the Committee, followed by a resume of the subjects discussed at the January Executive Meeting. e Budget for 1999 - 2000 Capital expenditure. Membership renewals and confirmation. RYA National Go Boating weekend. ECPR Galley franchisee. Future of the Club. Neil Pembleton addressed the Committee on the possible impact on the MASC and the MSC of the recent mergers and take-overs affecting GEC Companies in Chelmsford. The situation will have to be monitored closely. Neil announced that he is to leave the Marconi Communications Co in June 1999. On leaving the Company Neil will no longer be eligible to continue in his capacity as a Vice President of the MASC and a serving member of the MASC Main Committee. He appealed for someone to replace him on the MASC Main Committee (note that only GEC Marconi employees are eligible). Safety Peter Clayton reported that two Draft Operating Instructions, one for the Powered Winch and the other for Tractor Driving have been passed to the Safety Co-ordinator for comment. The Writtle Agricultural College operate a two day course on tractor and ancillary equipment handling, the course costs approx £300, more details to follow. East Coast Piers Race Lee Harrison said that he will continue as Chairman of the ECPR Committee. The Committee plan to hold their first 1999 meeting within the next two weeks. Preliminary enquiries have been made to possible sponsors. Finance Frank Bennett told the Committee at he had submitted the 99/00 budget to the MASC. Clubhouse and Site Peter Bloomfield reported that he had attended the last Sailing Sub Committee meeting to solicit voluntary help from the fleets for some of the pre season tasks. Peter statused the tasks as follows; e Security bars to stair-well window replaced Action closed e Lounge fire doors refurbishment Action Dart 15 Fleet e Wash basins in men’s toilet Action E Cockerton e Cadets Porta-Kabin Action S Glynn e Galley extractor fan Action Dart 15 Fleet e Fuel Store Bund Work has commenced e Galley cooker, replacement Ongoing e Galley Staff, discussions with prospect continue Action P Bloomfield e Cellar floor, urgent task Action P Bloomfield Ron Greygoose said that he had discovered a source of motor tyre disposal, the cost would be 50p per tyre. Action P Bloomfield Moorings Sub Committee Peter Clayton informed the Committee that the revised mooring plan was complete and that all the moorings are allocated. There is currently no one waiting for a mooring. The Cruiser Owners Moorings Handbook has been revised for the 1999 season. Static Power Pack for powering the winches. Duer engineering have a second hand 43HP diesel air cooled unit for sale. Peter gave options for consideration. The Chairman asked Peter to provide a complete cost breakdown. Action P Clayton Murray Bates said that the Workboat engine required a new barrel and piston costing £200.00. This was approved pending a second quotation being obtained from M Richardson. Action M Bates Continuing with the Workboat Murray asked for funding to replace the fenders, eight are required at a cost of £60.00. This was approved. Action M Bates Social Claire Davies reported on the first meeting of the Social Committee. Claire said that the Committee suggested that the established events should remain and that new events should be introduced, these to be; e The Barn Dance which was revived this year is to remain. e Revive the New Members evening making it more of an occasion with music and a buffet. e Fitting out Party to be held at the MASC ® Quiz Night, this will be scheduled for September /October and will be held at the MASC. The Chairman thanked Claire for her report, the Committee were in favour of the Social Committees proposals. Ron Greygoose suggested that we invite other Clubs to our social events.
