Commodores Notes Last month I was getting excited about the close competition for honours in the Winter Series, however the series did not end with a bang but a whimper. The last race was cancelled due to lack of wind. After close attention to the results of previous races, Tim Bellefontaine was presented with the prize for first place at the gathering held at the Green Man at Bradwell. Well done Tim, a good consistent performance. The difficulties with subscriptions to MASC have been largely overcome, but there is still a list of about 20 members who are behind with their dues. Remember that, to be a member of the Sailing Club, you must first be a member of MASC, so pay the invoice when it hits the door mat please. We have tried a policy this year of holding onto the Renewal Packs until we have confirmation that your MASC subs are up to date, so if you have not received yours this year, check you are not holding onto an MASC invoice. ; Our Entertainment's Committee have devised a Fitting Out Supper to be held on Friday 7" May at Chelmsford. This is open to all members and is a new event in the Club diary. I ask you to give our new committee every support and buy your tickets early, I already have mine. Claire Davies, Hilary Ashley and Laura Gill are the people to see. | have had some more reactions from members concerning the upper saloon and redevelopment of the Club. I was elected to the position of Commodore on the manifesto that I would implement a redevelopment scheme at the Club. I also said that any scheme would involve a hike in subscriptions to make it viable. Even if we could negotiate a Lottery grant we would have to match the grant £ for £ with our own funds. How would you feel about paying another £50 per year to pay for a really excellent shore based clubhouse? Your comments/opinion on email:- [redacted] or on [redacted] would be welcome. Don't let the vocal minority decide, let me have your opinion. My current feeling is that we can only afford to carry on with our progressive improvement of the Upper Saloon in the current year. Redevelopment would then be part of the Five Year Plan that is occupying the Main Committee at present. Many members have been working hard to get the Club ready for the season and my thanks go out to all. However I would like to mention Bob Goldbold who has sealed the cellar floor and to Bob and Elsie Anderson who have again brightened the Commodore's Lawn with flowers. Also, Eric Cockerton has replace the taps in the Gent's Changing Room. Thanks to them and all those I have not named. I would like to leave you this month with a thought with which Graham Sawyer ends his emails, "A bad day's sailing is better than a good day at work” Good Sailing! Clive Shenton View From The Rear By the time this Navigans reaches you. the season will be well underway and I hope that the Easter weather we are experiencing as I write is a good omen for the weather to come this year! The Support Boat Rota for 1999 has been included in this Navigans - may I encourage you all to check the dates that you have been assigned on it and to book them in your diary accordingly. I hardly need say that the manning of our support boats is crucial to our racing programme and a lot of other members are inconvenienced if someone fails to turn up or leaves it late to make other arrangements. I would like to thank the Support Boat Co-ordinators, Tony, Barry, Dennis and, in particular, the Sailing Secretary, John Salmon for their work in ensuring that all the arrangements are in place so that the rest of us can turn up and race each Sunday. [ would also like to thank Roger Smith for his hard work in organising the dinghy park spaces so that everyone can fit in. Whilst it is a good sign to have so many boats to allocate, they would not all fit in without Roger’s planning! The dinghy park layout is displayed on the Handicap notice board at the club - please write your name and boat on this plan once you have selected a space. Cat owners should contact Lee Harrison with any queries about the Cat Park. I would also like to emphasise the importance of identifying your boat with your name and contact number. It is important that we can contact an owner of a boat quickly for a whole range of reasons eg, if the boat needs to be moved for any reason or, worst case scenario, should it be damaged in any way. I was disappointed that someone chose to query this requirement by writing anonymously on the club noticeboard - perhaps that person would like to call me on the number below to discuss the concerns they have.

Finally, the last of the Cadet Pre-Season meetings was held on Saturday 27th March. This was the third meeting of its kind held at MASC where Cadets were taught / reminded of the points of sail, meteorology, rights of way, racing etc - interspersed with some interesting games of football! Thank you to the Cadets and parents who turned out, (there were around 20 cadets at each session) - and a special thank you to David Ball for organising the meetings with his able assistants, Lucy Boreham, Claire Davies and Sam Ashley. See you on the water! M.S.C. Commodores Notes May is here and the Sailing Season seems to be well underway. The excellent weather of the early May holiday was just a backdrop to my sailing event of the year- the genneker halyard held the sail up for once, and exciting 3 sailed reach caused hearts to pound harder. In my last article I asked for feedback on an idea to increase subscriptions by £50 and spend the extra on really good on-shore facilities. I have had twenty two replies so far, two of which thought it a good idea and the others against. I have replied to all the emails but not the letters, so I will attempt to summarise the comments and my replies. Firstly, I would like to thank everyone who took the time to contact me. All feedback is useful and will be taken into account as policy is made. Secondly, no increase in subs would be possible unless a majority vote sanctioned it at an AGM. My article last month was just floating an idea to see what reaction I would get. Several respondents have said they like the Club like it is, and no changes are necessary. All dinghy and cat people who have ventured an opinion, say they would be against moving the wet bar downstairs, especially into existing facilities. Various reasons have been cited, but that is the summary position. If you have another view I would be pleased to hear from you. Email is best, but a stamp on a letter still gets through. Now its time to talk about Protests, we had one at the weekend. The protest committee really had to think hard about the Rules before reaching the view that, although the rules had been broken, insufficient notice was given at the time of the incident i.e. No yell of "Protest" nor a flag flown, so the offender had no opportunity to do an alternative penalty. The Sailing Secretary and I both think that a few more protests in the Club would be good for us - they certainly reacquaint you with the Rules. They must not be accompanied by ill feeling however, usually protests arise due to different interpretations of the Rules, and it does no racing sailor any harm to get these things cleared up. The East Coast Piers Race is not too far away in July. This is our Club's blue-ribbon event which puts us on the map nationally and internationally. The fact that we are able to donate up to £4,000 each year to Charity as a result, can make every member justifiably proud. The Club as a whole make the event possible. Charles and Lee tell me that they could do with a few more mother boats and | ask you to consider volunteering by using the form printed on pages 13 - 15 in this edition. We cannot run the Race without them. Clive Shenton email :- [redacted] STOP PRESS....STOP PRESS.....STOP PRESS......STOP PRESS......STOP PRESS.....STOP PRESS...... | have just seen the open letter to me from Sue Arnold, it makes some good points and is similar to many that | have received. | believe my article on the 5 year plan that follows, will go some way to answering the questions raised. On the question of the future of Marconi and therefore the sailing club, the committee have been closely monitoring developments. | am pleased to say that there is no cause for concern at the present, if the situation changes the committee will be ready to act decisively to protect the future of our club. Clive Shenton Commodore Letter from Sue Arnold on page 6 i... Ed. FIVE YEAR PLAN The Main Committee recognised the need for a Five Year Plan at least a year ago. An embryo Plan was published last year, which reasserted the aims of the Club and identified some areas in need of improvement. We now need to define the detail of the Plan and the Main Committee needs your help to do this. Almost every member has, in his or her mind, that some aspect of the Club's activity that is in need of improvement - I know because individual members mention them to me. The snag is, that although we have some money for capital buys each year, it is impossible to fund every one immediately. The object of the Five Year Plan will be to identify what needs doing and then set out a timetable for its achievement during the period of the Plan. We can thereby introduce a greater measure of predictability into our organisation. The method for getting the Plan into place is seen as:- 1. Consultation to identify members requirements for improvement of the Club.(Or "wish list" for short) 2. Estimate costs of requirements 3: Decide which requirements will be met within the Five Year Period. 4. Decide on the priority for achievement of the requirements. 2: Main Committee draw up a Five Year Income and Expenditure Plan. 6. The contents of the Expenditure Plan explained to the Membership at a special meeting.

I expect that the stages will overlap to some extent, in what is fashionable to call an iterative process, but the above show the intended method. Item 1 is a most important phase of this process. If your requirements are not on the "wish list" then they will not see light of day. So I ask you to think deeply about the direction you think the Club should take, then discuss your thoughts with fellow members so as to refine and develop your ideas. If you like the Club just like it is, then it is equally important that you make this view known. When you have formed definite ideas, then it is necessary to make sure they get on the list. The best way to accomplish this is by writing it down and passing it either to your Fleet Captain, a Main Committee member or myself. Members who have emailed me with suggestions already need not repeat the process unless their requirements have changed. To reflect the importance of the consultation process we have allocated until mid August for you to give us your ideas, thoughts and requirements. The list will then be discussed for the first time at the early September Meeting. Events Report for 'Clubs and Classes' Yachts and Yachting A total of eighteen Dart 15s turned out for the first 1999 Traveller event held at Marconi Sailing Club on 17th/18th April. Saturday morning dawned sunny with shifting light airs making it a real challenge for the Race Officer, Roger Smith, to set a course. With the wind filling slightly, competitors set off against the tide on a triangle course with Bob Carter quickly gaining clear air and establishing an early lead. Meanwhile, Andy Jeffries entertained the rest of the fleet by letting his mast fall down and Dave Bladon, having missed the mark on his first attempt. took no chances and hit it on the second rounding. Bob Carter went on to win the race with Nick Dewhirst taking second after a close race with Jenny Ball.

Back by popular demand, the long distance race around Northey and Osea Islands was again scheduled for Saturday afternoon - and with a freshening wind, competitors looked forward to a good race and a chance to do battle with the Blackwater tides. Bob Carter again took the lead by the first mark, closely pursued by Peter Tovey. With a failing wind, Bob Carter rounded Northey Island , chased by Kevin Kirby with Nick Dewhirst, Peter Tovey, Paul Frost and Jenny Ball battling it out behind. Following a lengthy drift with the tide, the wind finally filled in to provide a romping reach back to Marconi and round the final triangle of the course. Undoubtedly the best of the wind of the weekend, this last lap saw Bob Carter take another convincing win, followed by Nick Dewhirst, Paul Frost and Peter Tovey reclaimed two places to take fourth place. The wind was not, however, welcome to Andy Jeffries who, having restored his mast, had broken his tiller extension and he again entertained the fleet by promptly capsizing. Having righted the boat, Andy rounded off the day by proceeding to miss out a mark of the course! Saturday ended in perfect style with an excellent meal provided by Colin Kidner and a few drinks to keep out the cold! Sunday dawned and can only be summed up as: no wind, no water, no race! Although the incoming tide solved the water problem, competitors could only watch in frustration as the wind failed to materialise. The Sunday racing was eventually abandoned - a disappointing end to what had been a great weekend. The event could not end, however, without the presentation of the Coveted Dart 15 Green Jersey award for the most memorable competitor to Andy Jeffries - a well-earned trophy! With Best Wishes Yours sincerely Nicholas Back Chief Executive An open letter to Mr Clive Shenton received from Sue Arnold Dear Mr Shenton, I read with some interest your suggestion in the May edition of Navigans that the membership be invited to donate an extra £50 in fees in order to update the existing club house facilities. I also noted your assertion that you were elected Commodore on a mandate to do just this. My recollection is that the voting for commodore last year was extremely tight. This would seem to indicate that there is by no means universal favour for the idea. I am sure that most of us would see a five year plan for the club as being entirely sensible. particularly in the present circumstances. If the press is anything to go by, Marconi would not seem to be the most stable company at the moment and one wonders where this leaves us as a club. Perhaps therefore the membership would like to know the views of the committee on how they see our future, indeed do we have a future? How is this reflected within the five year plan and where does updating shore based facilities fit into the broader picture? I would like to suggest that it is very difficult for the average member to agree to a hike in fees of £50 without any clear idea what the money is to be used for. Perhaps the committee would like to publish the five year plan in order that the rest of us be in a position to make an informed decision? We are, after all, proud of our position as a self help club and as such are not used to overcoming problems by "throwing money" at them. Most of us were attracted to Marconi Sailing Club because of its small family atmosphere and affordable fees. I seem to remember that the manifesto of the other candidate for the position of commodore last year suggested that, should he be elected, he would call an extraordinary general meeting in order that the membership have an opportunity to discuss the way forward. This would seem to be the appropriate way of harnessing opinion and would leave the committee with a clear mandate upon which to act. I would be interested to learn your views on this. Yours faithfully Sue Arnold Cruiser Fleet.

Minutes of the Main Committee Meeting held on the 29TM March 1999 MASC Matters. Mr. N Pembleton advised the Committee that a new Club Manager, Mr. Ralph Coates, has been appointed to replace Peter Wright who is retiring. The MASC Chairman, Mr. M Marsh and Mr. N Pembleton are to attend a meeting with solicitors to discuss amendments to the MASC Constitution following the recent Company changes. Safety Mr. P Clayton tabled draft-operating instructions for winch operators and tractor drivers for comment. The documents were used in a live situation on the 27° March 1999 to check their applicability. No problems were found. Tractor driver training for Mr. D Baker is to be arranged as previously agreed. Action P Black/P Bloomfield Mr. M Bates reported that the Writtle Agricultural College is able to offer on site tractor driving training for 28 people at a cost of £576.00. Agreed to proceed, proposed M Bates seconded D Kirby. East Coast Piers Race Planning continues. Finance The Hon Treasurer is busy closing the 1998/99 account. Clubhouse and Site Camping fortnight. The booking form has been published in Navigans. Mr. P Clayton said that as soon as names were available he would seek people willing to act as bar supervisors. Action P Clayton Mr. P Bloomfield reported on the progress of various tasks; Fuel store, main work completed awaits finishing details. Cellar floor has been sealed. Refuse skip, notices placed stating household waste only. Mr. C Shenton has received various suggestions on improvements to the lounge bar. Mr. M Richardson noted that the hard was very slippery and asked for funding to repair the mechanical scrubber. Cost to repair:- Bearings £60 Replacement brush £250 There was also some discussion concerning the safety of the tractor Power Take Off (PTO. It was agreed to purchase a guard. A spend of £300 was agreed). Proposed M Richardson, seconded N Pembleton. Mr. R Greygoose said that the main flagpole would be erected in time for the Easter weekend. Mr. M Bates observed that the water miser in the men’s toilets was a little too effective. Action M Richardson Moorings Sub Committee Mr. P Clayton informed the Committee that the tractors had been serviced, the club boats launched, the club trot replaced, and the race marks laid. The Moorings Sub Committee has discussed the future of the club tractors. Tractors are essential to the operation of the club. In the short term the committee recommends that the two of the three Fordsons be re wired to improve reliability. In the long term the committee recommends that the number of Fordsons is reduced to one and a new or more recent second tractor is acquired. This would bring the total compliment of tractors up to three i.e. two general-purpose units and one dedicated to grass cutting. Costs are required for planning Mr. M Bates questioned why the tractor procured for grass cutting was not yet available for use. The reasons were varied, however the way forward was seen to be 1 Training for Mr. D Baker in the use of the new tractor 2 Maintenance schedule to be written & log book provided 3 Nominate shelter for the tractor and the cutters Action P Bloomfield/ M Richardson Mr. P Clayton tabled details and costs of four options available to provide powered winches for boat handling. Finally Mr. Clayton informed the Committee that the moorings trailer had been successfully deployed and recovered using the existing powered winch. Social Mrs. Laura Gill advised the Committee of the Social Committees plans for 1999. A Fitting out Party and new members evening is to be arranged for May 7° at Chelmsford. A Quiz Night is being organized for September 24°" and following this years success a Barn Dance is to be arranged at the MASC early in 2000. The Committee welcomed these events and authorized Laura to make the necessary bookings for the Barn Dance. Proposed L Chaplin seconded J. comment. The Sailing Sub Committee have devised the ground rules for the operation of the cadet cabin and asked if the task of unlocking and locking could be added to the list of OOD duties. Bar Manager Mr. R Godbold informed the Committee that the cellar floor had been sealed, new stock ordered, freezer defrosted and cleaned and a general clean up completed. The proposal for an extractor fan for the cellar was not practical. Insulation material for the cellar walls is being sought. We have a spare cooler in case of failure. The Committee recommended that the bar prices be increased to at least cover the latest increase by the brewers. ECPR - Getting Closer Charles Anderson Cruiser Help Having just spent the weekend moving mooring chain around the hard it was encouraging to see many of you getting closer to the water. Mind you | concede there are still quite a few the wrong side of the wall including me!! I am on the ‘reminder trail’ and that is that I need to coerce around 20+ cruiser owners to join the support craft fleet. It is not an onerous task (I trust) and with any luck adds another dimension to a normal weekend's sail. For those that are not familiar with the event, the club is unique in its annual ECPR. The race is the only one of its kind in Europe and we believe the world. It is a water-borne version of the London Marathon attracting sailors from all over the UK as well as mainland Europe. The event and the individuals get themselves sponsored and the money raised goes to the Maldon based charity, The Cirdan Trust. The Trust provides sailing breaks for the disabled, disadvantaged as well as their helpers (not necessarily together), The money we raise goes towards bursaries which help those less able to pay make use of the charity’s services. For those of us that have read the letters of gratitude that flood into the Trust’s offices it is easy to see how much our support is appreciated and how much others benefit from the sailing experience. Something that most of us take for granted. You may well be familiar with the Trust’s fleet which include Hartlepool Renascence, Duet, The Queen Galadriel and the sailing barge, Xylonite (she still carries the ‘Friends of the Earth’ symbol on her topsail). All of which are often in the Blackwater. Another copy of the weekend's questionnaire is at the back of this copy; please don’t forget that if you do respond, your offer will be taken up so do turn up at the weekend. Barge Trips On Saturday 24 July, we will be organising trips down river. The duration of the cruises will be subject to prevailing conditions but we envisage one in the morning and one in the afternoon. They will be organised on a first come first served basis. All the money raised will go to the Cirdan Trust and for those of you that have not been on a barge it is an experience well worth taking advantage of. At the moment tickets will be £10/person. While it may seema lot look at it as a donation to charity where you get more than just a sticky label on your lapel. Direct Help Some of you may well know or be involved with youngsters who could benefit from the experiences the Trust can offer. Nick Back, the Cirdan’s Chief Executive will be at the Club on the 24th and 25th July and will be only too pleased to talk through in more detail how they can help you and your organisation. 13

Cruiser Racing News The first cruiser race of the season ran on 16 May, with a course up river to buoy 10, at the top end of Heybridge Reach. 12 boats took part ranging from the largest, Derek and Hillary Gardner’s Maxi 1000, to the smallest, the Talisman 18 of Len Scholl. In between there was Eric and Pauline Cockerton’s Westerly Griffon, John Easton’s Westerly Pageant, Jess Rowles’s Contessa 26, Colin Leveridges’s Debutante, Nick and Jan Bevan’s Sadler 32, Roy Mander’s Tomahawk, Dave Paynes’ Sonata, Robin Lovett’s Gibsea, Roger Brown's Super Seal, and myself, Hustler 30. All the yachts got away from the club line at 12.00 running up river with the flood tide to the mark, complicated by there being 2 buoy 10’s! A long beat back into a strengthening breeze initially against the tide, tested tactics, best overcome by the winner Colin Leveridge in the Debutante. The next Cruiser Racing Event will be a short race during the Burnham Rally on Sunday, and I will provide info on the day. There is another important event on Saturday June 26". This is the Blackwater Marina Challenge, a race starting at Osea Island and finishing at Brightlingsea. The race is open to all yachts on the river, from any club, and this year is run by Marconi SC. On Saturday evening there will be a dinner and prizegiving in the Colne Yacht Club with Free Wine provided by the sponsors Leisure Harbours Ltd. It is a really good event with a wide variety of yachts competing, and we would like to see as many Marconi Yachts as possible take part. An application form is included in this copy of Navigans, which includes a booking for the dinner. If you have any questions call me on [redacted]. We offer our deepest sympathy to our Honorary Secretary Pat Black, his wife Rita and their family on the sad news of the death of their son Ian. Commodores Notes It is now mid June. My last 6 weeks seem to have been totally dominated by Texel. The preparations, the event and the aftermath. I have written a separate article on the experience which appears elsewhere in this issue. This time of year is traditionally quiet on the Executive and Main Committees while we reap the benefit of our winter meetings and just enjoy sailing. It has not been like that this year. Main Committee had a full agenda and sat well into the evening. Since retiring as Commodore, Colin Kidner has chaired a Safety Sub-committee which has identified potential hazards in the Clubs operations, carried out risk assessments and amended and developed new Guidance Notes. This has all been necessary as the RYA told us some 18 months ago that the Health and Safety Regulations were increasingly being applied to private Clubs. This work is painstaking and unglamorous but essential. I wish to thank Colin, his principle advisor Malcolm Robertson and his hard working sub committee. I also thank Peter Clayton and Murray Bates for their co-operation in every stage of the process. The work is far from finished, so keep up the good work gentlemen. Camping Fortnight will be almost upon us as you read these notes. I wish to call your attention to the Bar and to the hours that the law permits it to open. The Main Committee has resolved to ensure that closing time is met. You will be asked to vacate the Bar after 15 minutes drinking up time. Please respond properly to this request. I will not issue threats, but you can be assured of the Committee's resolve to ensure that we keep within the Licensing Laws. Before the Camping we have the Piers Race. This continues to be unique in the UK. Not only do we have a good time sailing, but we donate around £4,000 to charity each year. You can help make this year great by entering either the full Monty(Walton and back) or the fun race to Jaywick. As usual Charles Anderson and Lee Harrison and their team have been working hard making sure the organisation runs smoothly. To all volunteers from the fleets who help on the day I thank you in anticipation of another job well done. Lastly I wish to call your attention to the Log Book which is on the shelf at the west end of the Upper Saloon. It is a black A4 diary. This is for all members to report items that they feel the Committee should know about. Recently there have been a number of complaints about shortfalls in the maintenance of the on-shore facilities, for example the shower pump is very temperamental. Texel - A pilgrimage Texel had been on the "must do" event list for some years for myself and Alex. This year we got there. Texel is an island off the north coast of Holland, and for the last 20 odd years it has hosted what has become the largest cat race in the world. For the last few years the entry has been limited to 700 for safety reasons, and competition to get ones entry accepted is fierce. After discovering that entries were only being accepted via the Internet, we made our application which was quickly confirmed. Preparations started. First the trailer had a total overhaul, new hubs and suspension and a paint job. A Hotel was booked and the boat examined with a fine toothcomb. Many minor jobs were completed to ensure the boat was on the top line. We left Harwich by the Sea Cat on Thursday morning and by evening we had formalised our entry, had the boat towed onto the beach by tractor and booked into, what turned out to be, a comfortable hotel. Day one missions accomplished. Day 2 dawned cold, wet and windy. We assembled the boat and improvised some holding down methods to prevent it being blown away. The shake down sail before the Race did not seem sensible in the force 7 that was blowing, so we retired to the hotel hoping for better weather on the morrow. Day 3 - Race Day dawned with no wind, slate grey skies and a thunderstorm, Oh yes and rain - lots of it. Undaunted we rigged the boat after as good a breakfast as the excitement would permit, and attended the briefing. Result -race postponed for 90 minutes while the storm moved away. Then the sun came out to the accompaniment of a gentle force 3 anda start time was confirmed. Launching at Texel is over a flat sandy beach and the surf was curling in nicely while 700 cats attempted to launch. We were just about to take our turn, I was sorting out the mainsheet and tiller extension prior to jumping aboard when the tiller connecting bar parted company from one rudder - The 6mm stainless connecting pin had sheared! But we are experienced campaigners, we have spare runners and tillers. The rudders were in the car about 1000m away across sand dunes. Alex ran both ways, in his full dry suit in record time while I took off the failed rudders. New rudders quickly fixed in the surf and we were off the beach before the 5 minute. Now for the Race. As we sailed out through the surf I must have got them down too early, the waves dumped us onto the bottom severely damaging the gudgeon to the extent that I later needed an hour with a hacksaw to get the rudder off the boat. Thoughts of starting immediately evaporated - we now had a new problem, how do we go about and get back through the surf without causing major damage. Well somehow we did it in time to watch the smoke from the helicopter on the start line turn to white and the race got underway accompanied by Alex's screams of frustration. I just felt numb. An hour later we were half way through dismantling the boat when the thunder came back, it belted with rain and the wind rose to force 7. It was not until next day, when we saw the broken masts and empty trailers, that we heard that less than half the entrants had finished and that abandoned boats littered the 60 km perimeter of the island. It slowly dawned on us that perhaps, just perhaps, we had had a lucky escape. Within 10 minutes of coming ashore with broken rudders we had resolved to return next year and get the job done. This time its personal! Positive things that came out of the trip were the friendly welcome of the Dutch, the good hotel, quick passage by seacat and most of all the excellent Race organisation. When we return next year we want to feel that we deserve to enjoy the much hyped social scene. Only one thing will make that possible and that is to finish the biggest cat race in the world. Clive Shenton Blade Runner

LETTER RECEIVED FROM MIKE BOREHAM Dear Editor, After 50 years - we know where we bin but which way do we be goin? I would like to follow up on a couple of points which have been raised in recent issues of Navigans. MSC 50th Anniversay:- In November, 1998 issue of Navigans, our retiring Editor (Maureen Ball) reminded us that the MSC was not too far off its 50th Anniversay. The Sailing Section of the Marconi Athletic and Social Club (i.e. Marconi Sailing Club) held its Inaugural Meeting on 18 April, 1952, thus we have some way to go before celebrating our 50th. The MSC's first clubhouse was a former workshop on the sea wall at Heybridge and the club later moved to the somewhat neglected barge-yacht M/amgu moored nearby. So how come the ‘Honours Board’ shows the names of Commodores for 1950 and 1951? I believe the late Eric Payne was consulted about the list of past Commodores in about 1975 and presumably Enc named L L Jackson and C Christensen as past Commodores because of the pre-1952 activities. During the time that | was wnting the Navigans Past series of articles, I met quite a number of ‘old members’ but none could elaborate upon, or even remember, the existence of a recognisable group prior to the Inaugural Meeting in 1952. Following a proper course - part 1:- In June, 1999, Navigans, I was relieved to be able to infer from Frank Burgess’ Cruiser Racing News that perhaps Maggie and I were not the only ones to be unaware that there are now two channel markers designated No. 10. The Mona's Cup race was run on the same day as the cruiser race and the fact of there being two No. 10 cans in existence was not notified in the course instructions. In the event, it should come as no surprise to the Sailing Sub-Committee that some (perhaps even just one) competitor innocently sailed what was, in fact, a proper course as instructed even though it later transpired it was not the intended course. At the time of writing, Maggie and I are quite happy to retire from the race whatever our position. Following a proper course - part 2:- Commodore Clivee Shenton's notes in recent issues of Navigans and Sue Amold's letter make interesting reading. Clive's original question was "How would you feel about paying another £50 per year to pay for a really excellent shore based clubhouse”. “Not a lot" might have been my reaction, I had no detail or idea of why it might be necessary to charge me an extra £50 subscription each year to improve upon that which I already consider to be generally adequate shore-based facilites. | will need to know "why, where, when and how" of the plan in detail - in that order - before even considering saying "Yes". As a not particularly active member, I am generally content to have a place to park my dinghy, a loo to use when nature demands (complete with loo paper!), somewhere to change and hot water to shower. I regard these as the essential services, together with a reasonably safe and clean environment, which ought ultimately (even if indirectly) be provided by Marconi Athletic and Social Club to members of its Sailing Section. I would be more interested in upgraded changing rooms rather than an upgraded bar but I'm not sure if either are worth an extra charge of £50 on my annual subscription - but I could be persuaded. Five-year long term plans and ‘wish lists’ are nothing new in the club but it is good to see that the debate continues. I look forward to the outcome of this particular exercise and hope | will be able to keep an open mind on whatever ‘new ideas’ are forthcoming. Perhaps, when the real 50th anniversary comes around, we'll be able to look as eagerly to the future as we can look back with pride on our past. Defining the proper course:- With reference to ‘following proper course’ (be it literal or metaphorical) I hope it will not continue to be the assumption that “everybody knows". A fair number of us ordinary members are not as aware of factors affecting club affairs and activities as we ought to be, despite the best efforts and beliefs of those in charge. ‘Tis nobody's particular fault - merely one of those difficult facts of club life that those in charge must continually bear in mind. Mike Boreham a

As we will not have our training day, which usually includes a boat tuning session this year, I thought it would be worth including the following tuning notes. The notes were supplied by Jim Hunt ( Purple Sails) and are unchanged from those issued two years ago. 10

SOLO TUNING GUIDE Mast Position The distance from the front of the mast at the heel to the outside of the transom at the floor is 3055mm. Forestay This should be just in tension when the mast (without sail) is pushed to the back of the gate. Shrouds These should be just in tension when the mast (without sail) is 10mm from the front of the gate. Chock Use one chock which just fits in front or behind the mast . Light airs Up to just sitting on the side deck. Upwind Chock behind the mast. No cunningham. Centreboard 25-50 mm of forward rake. Outhaul 20mm from black band. Kicker just slack Traveller 0-50mm from centreline. A small amount of leeward heel is acceptable. Off wind Use only enough centreboard to keep the rudder neutral. Leave outhaul on it’s upwind setting. Use enough kicker to stop the boom rising in gusts. Medium Airs Up to fully hiked Upwind Chock in front of mast. No cunningham. Centreboard vertical. Outhaul 10mm from black band. Kicker just slack Traveller 0-100mm from centreline. Increase mainsheet tension as the traveller moves away from the centreline. Offwind As for light airs except : Ease outhaul up to 100mm Use enough kicker to keep the back of the top batten parallel to the boom. Heavy Airs Fully hiked overpowered. Upwind Remove chock Use cunningham to progressively depower the sail (too much and pointing will suffer) Lift centreboard progressively to reduce weather helm. Outhaul to the black band. Kicker just tight. Ease traveller up to 380mm from the centreline to keep the boat footing - but pull it closer to the centreline in flatter areas to maintain pointing. Use more kicker if the mainsheet needs to be cased often in gusts Offwind Same as medium airs except only case outhaul and cunningham if more power is needed.

Cruiser Racing News The Race during the Burnham Rally was changed to a cruise in company to the Ferry Boat Inn at Fambridge. Approximatley 30 people sailed aboard Gabelle, West Marie, Killara 2 and Ocean Slipper, in strong winds, with the usual alcoholic refreshments at the pub! The Steeple Bay Trophy, was contested by 12 yachts on the traditional Steeple Bay SC course around Osea Island As expected it proved attractive to the smaller yachts, and included our first catamaran entry, Mr Clark’s Hirondelle Claneda. The fleet rounded the green buoy at the end of the Osea spit and then found they needed to beat upwind to keep clear of the spit itself. The catamaran showed its reaching/running potential by moving ahead of the fleet by the top of the island, however on the beat back it was ‘reeled in’ by the windward performance of Roger Brown’s Seal 26 ‘Out of Focus’ and Dave Payne’s Sonata ‘Live Wire’. The Seal just beat the Sonata to the line with Robin Lovett’s Moonfleet and the cat arriving soon after, but it was the performance of the slower yachts which provided the surprise. John Walker’s Snapdragon, John Easton’ Westerly Pageant, J.Burgoyne’s Jaguar 22. and the Vivacity 21, all achieved a good result. Eric Cockerton’s Griffon, Jess and Sophie’s Contessa 26, and Chris Davies’s Hunter Duette completed the field....... and the winner?....Colin Leveridge in the Debutante ‘Bluster’. The next races offer the prospect of longer distances. July 11th Cruiser race 2 starts at 10.00am and we have the opportunity to set a course from the published list for perhaps 4-5 hours duration. August 28" is the passage race to Shotley for the club Rally starting at 13.00hrs (HW 14.32) September 18" The Big One, ‘The Medusa Race’ to Medusa Buoy and back to Bradwell starting at 6.30am (HW Stansgate). Colin Leveridge has sportingly promised, he will enter this long distance event, so come on, who can beat him? Good Sailing................ Frank Burgess, Ocean Slipper. Two extracts from previous Navigans which may serve as useful reminders. In case you have not seen it in the yachting press this was reported in the August 1998 edition of “Sailing Today” “The Holland Decca Chain “D’ Purple Slave Station at Thorpness in the UK (52 11°N 01 36’E) is to close at 2359 on July 31 this year, This means you will no longer be able to get Decca fixes in the Southern part of the North Sea using the Purple and Green Slave Stations. The ‘C’ Green Slave is located at Sas van Gent (51 13°N 02 52’E), the ‘B’ Red Slave at Heiloo (52 35°N 04 45’E) and the Master at Gilze-Rijen (51 37°N 04 56E) Special care should be taken when sailing in the vicinity of any base line extension areas. Transmissions from the remaining Decca stations in the Holland Chain 2E, covering the Central part of the North Sea and the Frisian Islands (Chain 9B), will continue until 2359 on December 31 1999” What with the phasing out of Decca and the millennium Bug and its possible effects on GPS systems, I guess it will be back to basics soon! What on earth did I do with my Protractor, Compass, Parallel Ruler etc.? Derek Kirby Cruiser Fleet Captain. Attention all GPS Users. First the good news. GPS Systems do not have a Year 2000 problem. Now the bad news, some may have a 21st August 1999 problem! The following information was received over the Internet. A US Air Force worker noticed that there was no mention of any field in any GPS message to tell him which 1024 week cycle he was in. Guess when week 1025 arrives? Yes 21st August 1999, The Air Force worker contacted GPS Companies in the OSC, some of whom were aware of the problem, some were not. Apparently manufacturers who were aware of the problem kept quiet in the hope of putting some of their rivals out of business. This will be of scant comfort to our cruisers returning from Holland on 22nd August 1999. Perhaps a check with your GPS manufacturer might be a good idea. One last piece of advice from our helpful American fnend - don’t travel on 22nd August 1999, unless you have a sextant with you. (For computer Nerds - check out http://www. yachtingnet.com/forums/power/|.html.) Happy sailing Keith Starkey.

Alex and I have been on our travels again, this time it was the ARTI cat race around the Isle of Wight. Two other Marconi boats joined us, helmed by Phil Longhurst with Marcus and Paul Harrison with Michele. We all finished safely in about mid order in times of around 9 2 hours. The sailing was very varied, with many calms but a good 3-4 geneker reach from St. Catherine's to the Needles. An unusual feature of the area was the several overfalls at headlands where the sea was very confused, flat one second and boiling, swirling and breaking the next, accompanied by a calm. We expected a sea monster to rise up and eat us like a sixties sci-fi film. So, it was better than Texel for us, but still room for improvement. Phil is already getting together the 'posse’ for next year. I want to remind you about your ‘wish list’ for the Five Year Plan as set out in the June edition of Navigans. You have until mid August to tell me, your Fleet Captain or a Main Committee member, the direction you would like to see the Club take over the next five years. I have had several people tell me that they like the Club like it is, and they don’t want improvements. This is a legitimate opinion and should be expressed. However most responses so far have wanted some improvements somewhere, and it is the purpose of the Plan to first assemble all ideas(whichI refer to as the wish list for short) and then to structure, costs and prioritise the list. The Main Committee will begin this task at the early September meeting, hence the deadline of mid August. We anticipate that much discussion will take place during Camping Fortnight to enable members to clarify their views. If you don't let us know your views they are unlikely to be actioned within the next five years, so make sure you tell someone. Views should be in writing or email as verbal opinions are very difficult to correlate. I make no apology for repeating my warning of last month about the Club bars. The Main Committee is determined to ensure that the licensing laws are followed. The Bar Supervisors have the full backing of the Main Committee, when they say the bar will close, that is what they mean. The rules will be posted in the bars and a copy is included in this edition. Now to something a little bizarre - Mooring E7. Leonard Scholl, who is allocated this mooring, is convinced that the mooring has been tampered with in some way, causing the anchors to break free and cause a hazard. Neither the Executive nor the Moorings sub committee can find any logic or motivation for such an act. If you have any information please contact me. I am very keen to get to the bottom of this one. The Piers Race is less than two weeks away and its all systems go. My thanks, as always, go to Lee Harrison, Charles Anderson and their hard working ECPR Committee. My equally heartfelt thanks go to the Cruiser fleet and to every other fleet, except the Cats, who give up their weekend so the glory boys can race. Thank you all. All we need now is a good wind and reasonably fine weather and the Cirdan Trust should be anticipating another sizeable donation. See you on the water, have a good summer's sailing, Clive Shenton Home phone:- [redacted] email:- [redacted]

Social Events - Quiz Night Many thanks (slightly belated) to all those who came along to the Fitting Out event at MASC back in May. Despite a couple of days of mild panic, we were well supported, and a pleasant evening was had. We were particularly pleased to be joined by a number of new members. So, now that we've got the ball rolling, it's time to move on to the more serious stuff. On Friday 24th September, we will be holding a Quiz night at MASC, Beehive Lane. It will be a 7.30 for 80'clock start. Teams should be of no more than eight people, and tickets cost £6.50 per person, including a buffet meal. The bar will, of course be open. If you usually "do" quiz nights with teams from outside the club, feel free to bring them along - more the merrier! As before. it would be great to see members from all the fleets - how about a windsurfing team? Tickets are available from us on the numbers below. Meanwhile, at the loony bin... Have you laid plans yet for the Millennium celebrations? It has been suggested that there could be a celebration at the club site, with food, music, fireworks, lots of heaters and camping. Clearly, this is ridiculous - here's why I think it's a good idea: 1. It would solve the problem of what to do at New Year; Yes, camping would be rather chilly at that time of year, but we now have two large portacabins on site that might be used, cruiser owners have their snug berths to return to and caravans tend to be warmer than tents; 3. As in the summer, the club is a great venue for family events - adults and cadets can all enjoy themselves, and parents can have a worry-free evening: If there's camping, there's no need to worry about taxis home; Aue Bar prices anywhere else will be astronomical; Can you think of a better bunch of people to see in the millennium with?! If this appeals to you, let me know - we need some feedback on this! As ever, if you have any thoughts, ideas or suggestions for social events, let us know. Claire Davies. SOLO MATTERS Our SOLO Open Meeting took place on 27" June and the following report by Roger Smith covers the event. Many thanks to all club members who helped in any way with the arrangements for the Open Meeting and all those who carried out duties on the day. The club SOLO is back in use and seems to be going quicker ! Roger Smith has recently donated a replacement sail and everything is in good working order. Should you wish to use the boat, to try SOLO sailing, please contact myself or any SOLO fleet member. On Saturday 10 July seventeen SOLO fleet members enjoyed a very pleasant day on the barge Thistle sailing from Mistley to "The Walton Backwaters" via Harwich. The weather was perfect, with continuous sun and a force 4-5 breeze. We are already considering repeating this event next year and an early booking should enable us to avoid the limitation in numbers which restricted us this year. [redacted] SOLOS AT MARCONI Marconi Sailing Club held it's annual Solo Open Meeting as part of the Eastern Travellers Series on Sunday 27th June. 25 Solos, comprising of 14 visitors and 11 club members, arrived at the club on the River Blackwater Estuary in cool, showery and overcast conditions in stark contrast to the beautiful weather on Saturday. Mike Turner, the Race Officer, ably assisted by Kate Williams, Richard Green and others, set long courses to cover the area of the river normally sailed by Marconi to allow visitors to experience the full range of our great site. The first race was held in a gusty force 4 over a choppy sea. A kerfuffle at the start resulted in the capsize of two prominent visitors and Steve Ede set the pace to round the first mark in the lead. In the long broad reach against the tide to No. 1 mark, he decided to battle it out against the tide in the middle of the river, whereas others tried to keep out of the tide by taking the longer route along the shore. Steve Ede still prevailed however and led the race to the finish followed by Jerry Garner and Tony Cook. John Salmon, showing good speed in his new boat was 4th. Following back to back, the second race was over the same course as the first, the difference being that the tide changed halfway through the race. The lead changed several times but eventually Steve Ede came through again for another first place, this time followed by Mike Wilkie and Tony Cook. The changing tides caused many reversals and changes of places throughout the fleet, as people who had overstood the 3rd mark in the first race found that they could not lay it this time. John Salmon was again the best placed Marconi helm at 5th, with Doug Eyles showing a creditable 8th place. After the break the wind has eased slightly and the third race followed a similar course against the ebbing tide. This time Mike Wilkie established an early lead and held it to the finish. Steve Ede came second, making him the overall winner. Jerry Garner was third giving him second overall. John Salmon was 5th again with Doug Eyles and Steve Ash again showing well. Steve Monks had a good outing in the Club Solo, now watertight following some homework by Fleet Captain Geoff Josey. Results: 1st 4226, Steve Ede, Ardleigh S.C. 2nd 4189; Jerry Garner, Littleton S.C. 3rd 4150; Tony Cook, Littleton S.C. 4th 4005; John Salmon, Marconi S.C. 5th 4190; Mike Wilkie, Littleton S.C. 6th 4210; Gordon Barclay, Chichester Y.C. Roger Smith 10

Minutes of Meetimg held 14 June at MASC Chelmsford Previous minutes: Minutes proposed: R Godbold, seconded Colin Kidner. Executive Meeting: The Executive Committee discussed the following items:- Errant members, Marconi web-sites, Membership categories, Camping dates, Tractor courses, Windometer and Tannoy. Safety: Mr Bloomfield reported that Mr D Baker had now attended the tractor training course run by Writtle Agricultural College. Mr Clayton reported that Tractor repairs were still in progress. Mr. Kidner advised that a report on the risk assessment of equipment at the Sailing Club had been submitted to MASC. The following items are in progress: e Risk analysis had been carried out on the mast derrick and the mooring barge procedure for laying moorings — a number of action items have been identified. An analysis of lifting moorings will be completed at year end. Cruiser trailers have been reviewed — mostly in good condition. Tractor guidance notes have been revised in line with feedback and comments from Writtle Agricultural College. Further items for assessment have been identified, including electricity safety / supplies on site. The committee expressed its thanks to Colin, Malcolm, Peter and Murray for their efforts. ECPR: The Website is up to date and approximately 80 entries are expected. Clubhouse and Site: Mr Clayton advised the meeting of suitable members to close the bar during Camping fortnight. The list was approved. A definitive rota will be produced by the next meeting. A notice will advise members that the bar area will be shut and cleared by 11:15pm. Mr P Bloomfield advised the meeting of the following: Waste bins had now been cleared. The mower had been repaired by Mr M Richardson The addition to OOD notes regarding clearing up beer spillage in the cellar has been actioned. All gas appliances have been serviced and repaired as necessary. Outstanding items on the grass cutting tractor have now been complete (except for log book). Fence posts outside the clubhouse were removed for no apparent reason — these will be replaced. Mr Glynn advised that the Cadet Cabin would be delivered on 16" June. Mr Glynn requested £200 to cover cost of materials to action road repairs. This was approved. Mr Glynn raised the concern that several items of equipment required maintenance and that fewer members had the knowledge to do this, (eg shower pump, cruiser park electrics, sewage system etc). A more structured maintenance approach was required. It was noted that members should report faults in the log book and should be encouraged to do so, via Navigans. Mr Greygoose asked the location of other hosepipes on site. Moorings Sub-Committee Mr P Clayton reported on the following: e Due to some problems, a number of moorings had to be moved. e Repair work had been carried out on the tractors which were in a poor condition and work continues. Social Committee Nothing to report. Mr Glynn suggested that a Millennium New Year event be held at the club. Sailing Sub-Committee J Ball advised that the order had been placed with Tollesbury Saltings Ltd to fit the engine/consul to the Orkney and they would be collecting it shortly. The Jack B tender oars need to be replaced. 11

Commodores Notes I can barely believe it! Camping Fortnight and the Piers Race already over and with them the summer. It will soon be AGM time. The Piers Race was again a major success and blessed by good weather. It is always difficult to mention individuals, but Lee Harrison and Charles Anderson must be singled out, not only for great organisation but also for the 2 ’% page write up in Yachts and Yachting. My thanks, as always, also go to the tough and tenacious Cruiser crews who provided mother boats and gate boats, and to everyone who contributed in the many tasks necessary to make the race safe and enjoyable. Cadet Week was a similar success with upwards of 70 Cadets honing their skills under the watchful eye of their instructors. After many years running this Event, Chris Davies and Charles Anderson handed the baton over to Kevin Dowley, Peter Clayton and Steve Monks. I am sure every Cadet, past and present will join me in thanking Chris and Charles for effort above and beyond the call of duty. They will also wish to thank ail their team of instructors, organisers and willing slaves who all make it possible. I am told that the now traditional invasion of Shotley by the Cruiser fleet was again very well supported with upwards of 40 members sitting down to the evening meal. The next day the fleet departed in several directions with many spending the whole week exploring the east coast. I have now closed the wish list for the Five Year Plan and have combined them all into a single list. The Main Committee began discussion on the list at the early September meeting. Establishing costs and priorities is the next step. Late July also saw the delivery of the travel hoist, and inevitably some of the old debates were reopened. I will summarise its benefits. The hoist will enable some cruiser members to launch and recover their craft and then to transport them to their winter storage point without the need of a trailer. The hoist is fully certified for this purpose. Cruiser members will not need to rebuild or replace their trailers and so will save money. The cost of the hoist will be recovered via the Winter Storage Fees of those members whose craft are able to use the hoist. There has been no general increase in subscriptions as a result of this acquisition. You will see that the Nomination forms for Club Officers is included in this issue. I hope that you will consider serving in a capacity where your particular skills can be harnessed. Some specific posts fall vacant this year. 1 am sure we all appreciate the years of service that Roger Smith and Bob Goldbold have given to Dinghy Park Officer and Bar Manager respectively. If you think you may wish to put yourself forward for these posts please phone me on [redacted] and I will outline the job description. We are also seeking a bosun for the RIB, some knowledge of outboards may be an advantage, but Mick Richardson will give a full briefing to anyone who is interested, and be available to give backup and advice during service. Each of these posts is vital to the running of the Club so please think carefully and volunteer if you are able. We also have one or two places available on the Main Committee. The present Committee have divers skills and interests, and steer the Club's affairs with passion. However there is always room for a different point of view to strengthen the Team. For example those free spirits, the board sailors, are not represented, so how about finding someone to give up one Monday evening a month? See you all at Quiz Night on the 24”. Clive Shenton

VIEW FROM THE REAR All of a sudden, it's September!!! Mind you, as I write the weather is considerably better than it was in August - long may it last. We have had a very full and successful sailing season since the last Navigans, both at the club and further afield including the following:- East Coast Piers Race Some 80 boats took part in the ECPR this year, enjoying the sunshine even if the winds were light to start with. The event was a great success and thanks go to Lee and Charles, the ECPR Committee, Mike Turner and the Race Management Team and the army of cruisers, support boats and T.A. volunteers who all made the event possible. Hopefully, a good sum of money was raised for the Cirdan Trust. Cadet Week See reports on pages 7 - 10 Other Events Our club sailors have also been actively taking part in events further afield - we were represented at the Isle of Wight race and Texel. MSC sailors achieved some good results at the Hurricane Nationals and the Club was well represented at the Dart 15 Nationals at Heme Bay. We also have a number of competitors taking part at Burnham week, as I write. Finally, the cruiser fleet who always do things in style have enjoyed a number of cruises in company. Most recently, they headed up to Shotley Marina over the glorious August Bank Holiday. I know some of them have taken the opportunity to sail further up the coast this week whilst I was glaring at the sunshine through my office window!! ...oh well! There will have been other events and achievements that I have forgotten to mention here and I apologise in advance. May thanks, as ever, goes to all those volunteers who have sat on support boats, in race boxes, committee boats, repaired club kit etc etc. On the subject of volunteers, it is not long until we renew our Committee and Club positions. I am hoping that existing members will be able to continue their hard work and that we may also be able to get some new volunteers. If you think you may be able to help in anyway, please do not hesitate to contact myself or any other Committee Member. Happy Sailing! SUPPORT BOAT NOTICES Our support boats have provided their usual invaluable service for this summer's sailing activities and we have been fortunate in the number of volunteers who have manned them. As we move towards the end of the season, I would just like to make the following reminders:- ORKNEY ze This is intended as an OOD boat and is ready to be launched quickly while the RIB and Jack B are occupied supporting racing. 2. The Orkney may also be used to cover a race if the RIB of Jack B are unavailable. 3, On NO ACCOUNT should the Orkney be used to lay race marks. Not only will the gel coat not take it, the boat is not structurally designed to take the stram. Race Officers and OOD's should also ensure that this does not happen. 4. The Orkney does create a lot of wash even a low speeds (more than the RIB) - please be aware of this - particularly in the vicinity of the hard or the moorings. RIB It has been noticed over the past few months that the RIB has been driven too fast on a few occasions. Could drivers kindly remember the following: 7, The RIB should only be driven at low speeds in the moorings and within the 8 knot limit (e.g. around Osea shoreline). One of our drivers was stopped by the River Police for speeding because they had not noticed they were within the 8 knot limzt. 2: The RIB should only be driven at high speed to get to the scene of an incident, to catch up with the fleet or other similar reason. Please avoid constantly speeding up and down the river - it is very costly on fuel and could give the club a poor reputation with other niver users. 3. Finally, could drivers and crews keep aware the level of wash they are making - at the very least, wash creates inconvenience for small boats - at worst, injury could result if it causes someone to spill hot drinks or slip. I should note that the level of support boat driving is good and responsible within the Club and would only ask that drivers and crews keep the above points in mind, to maintain the high standard. Thank you for your support. Jenny Ball - Rear Commodore

CRUISER COMMENTS Once again we had an excellent turnout for this year's Shotley Cruise with 20 boats attending, although, this was slightly down on last year. The meal in the 'Shipwreck Stour Suite’ was attended by 40 members, sadly Frank and Angie - 'Ocean Slipper’ could not make it as Frank had picked up a tummy bug and had to leave his boat at Felixstowe Ferry and retum home. We have since heard he is alright now and busy organising a race to the Medusa. Following up from the Shotley visit, 8 boats entered the River Deben making their way up to the Tidemill at Woodbridge where we had a most successful Bar B Q, this time being joined by Roy and Margarete in 'Serupin 11' who were unable to join us earlier due to Roy having an OOD commitment at the club on the Sunday. After that the fleet split up each doimg their own thing, even so four of us met up in the Walton and Frinton Yacht Club pond on the Thursday and got together for an evening meal in the Yacht Club. The weeks activity finally ended up with most of the fleet meeting up again at Brightlingsea where the 'Barge Match' was being held, so a meal at the Colne Yacht Club was not possible so we all went off for fish & chips at "Winkies’. It must be said the weather during the whole week was absolutely fabulous as was the company. In last months Navigans I mentioned winter storage. I am still trying to organise this and as soon as I can, the usual layout board will be displayed in the clubhouse. One of the problems is knowing who will be coming out on the travel hoist, if you are one of them would you please let me know. I will only be able to allocate specific locations to those still using trailers, those using the travel hoist will be allocated an area, possibly at the end of the cat field where craft will be placed as they come out. This is the first time we will be using the travel hoist so please bear with us. Lastly may I ask you to make a note in your dairy that this years Cruiser A.G.M. will be held on Thursday 18th November at M.A.S.C. commencing at 8pm. The agenda for this will be published in next months Navigans. Derek Kirby - Cruiser Fleet Captain. SOLO MATTERS Since the last Navigans issue we have had a number of new boats in the fleet. Mike Taylor and John Salmon have recently acquired wooden boats and Steve Monks now has Mike's old wooden boat. I use the term "old" loosely ! CADET WEEK 1999 As most people will now know, Cadet week 1999 was to be our swan song. After seven years of running the event, we were hoping for a good turn-out of Cadets, an excellent offering of well-maintained boats and weather which graduated from flat calm for capsize dnill on Monday to something more demanding at the end of the week. It is truly astonishing to report that we got virtually everything we wished for. We were once again able to borrowa selection of boats from the Laser Centre to enhance what has become an extensive and well- presented fleet of club-owned Cadet boats. During the week we had use of Mirrors, Picos, Toppers, 420s, Lasers, Laser 2, Byte, Laser Fun and Wayfarers - all owned by club members. These were augmented by 5 Picos and a showroom-fresh Laser 3000, The rhubarb and custard colours of some of the Picos added vibrancy to the overall scene. The ability to source a number of high-performance dinghies this year provided Jenny Ball, Claire Davies, Lucy Boreham and Mark Bulkley with an exciting opportunity to introduce some of the older Cadets to spinnakers and trapeze work. For this quite sizeable group there was also great attention given to racing starts and race techniques. The remaining 45 or so youngsters were divided into a Beginners section and a much larger Intermediate group. The Intermediates were sub-divided in to nine tutor groups for work both ashore and afloat. They developed their sailing skills in Mirror dinghies, usually sailing in pairs accompanied by their tutor, and the more confident Cadets were able to move on to helm Toppers at the end of the week. The Beginners’ activities for the most part mirrored those of their more experienced friends and relations but were carried out in larger groups aboard the Wayfarers and other large dinghies. We are not always blessed with weather and tide conditions which allow an Osea Outing and a Thirslett Treat in one and the same Cadet Week. In 1999 we enjoyed picnics at both locations, with excellent racing out and back on both occasions. Miraculously, everyone concerned was re-united with their own lunch pack on arrival and, unusually, we got off Thirslett before Charles and I were knee-deep on the highest point of the spit! Having been blessed with an annually expanding Cadet section, we now find ourselves doubly blessed by the addition of a Cadet Centre for the club. Full credit for this must go to Debbie and Steve Glynn; their work and negotiation skills with British Petroleum enabled us to acquire this large cabin free, yes completely free. As with any negotiation, it takes two to tango and our unbounded gratitude must go to Lindsay Walker of BP for his great support (not least of which included talking to Debbie a lot) in securing such a favourable arrangement. As usual, we held the awards ceremony on Saturday (see end of report) and we were delighted that Lindsay was able to join us to present the trophies to the lucky Cadets. This presentation was then followed by a naming ceremony for the BP Cabin (see photo in August Y&Y), which again was performed by Lindsay Walker. After popular acclaim, and as the scissors hovered over the ribbon, the sealed envelope was ripped open to reveal that it was to be known as ‘Jabbah’. ( Please don’t ask either of us oldies why - all enquiries to [redacted] ). Formalities over, a very successful under-18s Regatta was held in which 36 dinghies took part . There were visiting boats from Blackwater SC, Harlow SC, and Brandyhole SC to join us in good racing in variable conditions. We even signed-up the Brandyhole Cadets Joshua, Jerram and Joseph; we are pleased to welcome them as members of the Cadet section and secretly we think dad (John Bird) will join as as well. Cadet Week 1999 for us will be especially memorable for having produced the best possible combination of support, circumstances and conditions that we could have wished for. The support of our ever-willing and oh-so-patient tutors is a crucial factor to Cadet Weeks as we know them. Our gratitude is immense and so our alphabetical thanks go to Rupert Anderson, Thomas Anderson, Ben Ashley, Jo Ashley, Ian Chaplin, Peter Clayton, Andrew Greenhalgh, Ed Hiller, Gavin Jones and Ryan Jones - in addition to the Gang of Four mentioned above, We are no less grateful to the large band of families and friends who provided all of the support for our on-water activities. We were both very touched to be presented with engraved plaques to record our time as Cadet co-ordinators. It is nice to know that we have been appreciated, of course, but we do feel just a bit guilty about taking the plaudits for doing something that we have both so much enjoyed. We are confident that the new team headed by Pete Clayton, with assistance from Kevin Dowley and Steve Monks, will have just as much fun as we have, we wish them luck and look forward to supporting them as they, and so many others, have supported us over the years. And so, finally to the list of awards..................

We offer our deepest sympathy to Pam Wainwright on the sad news of the death of her husband Peter. Commodore's Notes Quite a lot happening this month both on and off the water. The Quiz night was a great success with over 90 entrants. The inaugural trophy was won by the Team "Serendipity". The last time I can remember being so soundly beaten was when there were potential Olympic participants in the field. The event was good fun and I believe the Social Committee are going to make it an annual event. We had a good result in the Forts race where boats from our Club filled 3 of the top eight places. This event has been plagued by poor winds in previous years, but this year Phil Longhurst, Marcus Wallace and Grant Piggot and their crews found the windier conditions to their liking. Phil was so pleased with himself he donated 25 kg. of daffodils to the Club. This brought an enthusiastic smile to the face of our resident gardening guru, Bob Anderson. The Main Committee meeting was dominated by AGM business and was in session for about 3 hours. We have received many nominations for key positions, and these are printed elsewhere in this issue. However we still need a nomination for Bar Manager as after many years dedicated service, Bob Godbold is standing down. Anyone interested should contact me or Bob and we will give a run down on what is involved. If the post is not filled we will not be able to open the Bars next year, so please think hard and volunteer. TO ALL WINDSURFERS We value your membership, and recognise the near mystical calling of your sport. However I am concerned that you do not have a voice at Main Committee and are thus the only sub section of the Club that is not represented. I appeal to one of your number, who can give one evening a month, to consider joining the Committee in order to give we mortals an insight into your requirements, likes and dislikes. Your fellow members need you. Steve Glynn tells me that 75% of the tickets for the Laying Up Supper have already been sold, but there may be enough left if you contact him quickly. The event is at Three Rivers Country Club as usual, on Saturday 20 November, with the AGM the day after at MASC in Chelmsford. The Cat boys are organising a Winter Series again this year. One Race every other weekend through the winter. They are hoping to widen the appeal to all club classes this time, so if you want to Race this winter get in touch with Lee Harrison or Phil Longhurst and negotiate. The charge last year was £25 for the series which included a good meal at the Prize Giving. As I write this piece HOTY is next Saturday. That's the Helm of the Year series of Races to determine the most gifted tiller hand. A new dimension this year is the inclusion of the premier cruiser racing skipper and a Cadet representative. With no previous form to go on, the bookies are worried. I shall have a grandstand seat from Jack B. I look forward to seeing you at Laying Up Supper and the AGM. Clive Shenton

CRUISER COMMENTS With this year's sailing activities sadly drawing to an end, those of you intending to winter your boats at M.S.C. will have noticed this year's "Winter Storage Plan" is now displayed on the Club's notice board together with the "Haul Out List". The introduction of the travel hoist and power winch have added another dimension to the hauling out process, both, I may add in the interests of the "Health and Safety Act". As a result of this I would draw your attention to the following:- a) A list is being published (not by me) of boats that must only be hauled out or launched using the power winch with an authorised operator. b) Boats hauled out on the travel hoist must also use the power winch as above. Cc) Members not falling into either of the above catagories will still need to make arrangements with an authorised tractor driver to ensure they can be handled on the day required. Just turning up and expecting to be handled will not do. Clearly we will be going through a learning curve as far as the power winch and travel hoist are concerned. One lesson already learned is not to clutter up the hard with trailers. A code of practice covering these procedures is being drawn up (not by me) and members will be advised accordingly. During weekend 11/12 September we hosted members of the RNSA to a Barbeque and an evening in the Dell Bar. Added interest was created by broadcasting of the last night at the proms, Land of Hope and Glory, Rule Britannia with vocal accompaniment from those present. The weather was fine and a great night was had by all. By the time you read this Happy Medium should be laid up. Doreen and I spent the last few days visiting Salcote Creek, Brightlingsea and the river Crouch. The trip to Brightlingsea during Saturday 25 September turned out to be a bit of a club affair with the arrival of West Marie, Two Jays, Fantasea, Winkler, Capricorn and Reflection. The Dismasting Of "TAHITI" It was to be for us a cruise to Brightlingsea following a chase with several yachts taking part and then once there we were to split from the rest of the fleet as we had been invited to a wedding reception in Wivenhoe, just 15 minutes by bus. The breeze being an easterly 3-4 with a bit of north in it was adequate for a good beat down river. The event was due to start at 13.30 hours, we were soon ship shape and heading out towards the start, luffing up in a stiff breeze opposite Osea Island. Suddenly "BANG", in a split second mast, sails and rigging were over to port side , Pauline and I were momentarily stunned but fortunately unhurt. Then I saw the base of the starboard lower stay toggle with nothing attached to it, the toggle had parted putting all the pressure at the top of the mast making it banana shaped and breaking just below the cross trees. Checking to see that no rigging was near the prop, I started the engine and slowly edged our way over towards Osea Island where I could safely drop anchor and take stock of the situation. Our first task was to get the sails from the mast, boom and forestay. "Want some help there" a voice from a yacht circling us. I think we can manage thank you, "are you sure". Yes, but he continued slowly circling. Then Jenny and Ray came over in their Even to assist. As they were near to the water they started to sort out the masses of rigging over the side. The circling yacht now came along side. I'm John from the Little Ship Sailing Club, this happened to me some time ago, I think I may be of some use. Welcome aboard we said, within two hours everything was sorted out and the mast lashed down. Poor Tahiti looking a sorry sight headed back to our mooring reflecting our luck of not being out in the open sea and nobody had been hurt. We did eventually get to the wedding, only 2 hours late!! Next day I contacted St Margarets Insurance and after weeks of haggling got a fair settlement from them. The problem was the grey area of the age of the ngging and when it should be replaced, it depends on the type of yacht and how it is used. There are no hard and fast rules governing the situation. The surveyors recommend every 10 years for replacement and my rigging was 15 years old. Finally we would like to thank everybody who helped to get Tahiti back sailing again, especially John from Little Ship Sailing Club Larry Sutton Heybridge Sailing Club Don Holdsworth Ken Evans Alan Clark Mike Silvey John Easton Ray and Jenny Ball Murray Bates Eric and Pauline Cockerton SOLO MATTERS It was good to see so many SOLO Fleet members at the Quiz Night last month. Medusa Race September 18TM Start 6.30am. A doom laden forecast discouraged many entrants, but 6 yachts came to the line at high-water, to start for the Medusa Race. With a F5-6 South Easterly Sea Gem and Live Wire were sent on a less exposed course to Colne No 16 upriver from Pyfleet via the Bench Head, returning to Bradwell the same way. Both boats had a heavy return beat out of the Colne, Dave Payne and his crew in Live Wire reaching Bradwell first, but beaten on handicap by John Easton single handing Sea Gem. On the Medusa course Derek and Hilary with Dave Stewart in Killara led the fleet down river pursued by Ray Bailey in Hartley, and Mike Turner’s Sea Brume. Frank Burgess with son Mark and Kevin Dowley in Ocean Slipper eventually passed Sea Brume as the fleet ploughed on through the heavy conditions of the Wallet, the fleet reaching the Medusa in 3 hours! The return against a foul tide was very heavy going but the wind remained in the South East providing a close reach, and a final beat to the line at Bradwell. Killara crossed the line first and won the race saving her time on handicap. An evening in the ‘Bradwell Green Man’ for all the crews rounded off a great race.
